q.explanation: This is one of the commonly agreed definitions of good governance.

q.q: Which definition stresses that citizens articulate their interests, exercise their rights, meet their obligations and mediate their differences?
options: The mechanisms through which citizens act
q.explanation: It is the definition about effective mechanisms, processes and institutions for citizens.

q.q: Which single word names the way rules, norms and actions are structured, sustained, regulated and held accountable?
q.explanation: That word is governance.

q.q: A country enjoys good governance simply because it holds regular elections.
q.explanation: Elections alone are not enough; accountability and honest management are also required.

q.q: Give the term for the institutions and processes through which common concerns are decided upon and regulated.
q.explanation: That term is good governance.

q.q: In the lesson, good governance requires an administration that is:
q.explanation: Good governance means a public service is efficient, a judicial system reliable and an administration accountable to its public.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why good governance is broader than government.
q.answer: many actors take part|courts, media, civil society, business and citizens also take part
q.explanation: Government is only one actor; many institutions and citizens share in governance.

q.q: Arrange the steps for judging a local office in the correct order.
q.explanation: The order is efficiency, reliability, accountability and citizen voice.

q.q: Name one group, other than government officials, that takes part in governance.
q.explanation: Courts, media, civil society, business and citizens all take part in governance.

q.q: Which principle requires elected and appointed officials to be answerable for the decisions and acts they undertake?
q.explanation: Accountability makes officials answerable for their decisions and acts.

q.q: The involvement of citizens in the process of decision making is called:
q.explanation: Participation is the involvement of citizens in decision making.

q.q: All the elements of good governance are interrelated.
q.explanation: The textbook says the effectiveness of one element depends on the others.

q.q: Which element means that institutions and processes try to serve all stakeholders within a reasonable time frame?
q.explanation: This is the definition of responsiveness.

q.q: Impartial enforcement of the law requires:
options: An independent judiciary and an incorruptible police force
q.explanation: Impartial implementation of laws requires an independent judiciary and an impartial, incorruptible police force.

q.q: Name the element that means the free availability of information to the general public.
q.explanation: That element is transparency.

q.q: Which element requires all groups, especially the most vulnerable, to have opportunities to improve their well-being?
q.explanation: This is equity and inclusiveness.

q.q: Accountability can be effective even when there is no transparency.
q.explanation: The textbook says accountability cannot be effective unless there is transparency and openness.

q.q: Explain in one sentence how transparency helps fight corruption.
q.answer: it reduces uncertainty and inhibits corruption|information freely available stops hidden deals
q.explanation: Transparency reduces uncertainty and can help inhibit corruption among public officials.

q.q: Arrange these actions of a well-governed office in a logical order.
options: Serve stakeholders within a reasonable time
q.explanation: The order is: publish information, invite citizens, hold officials answerable, serve within a reasonable time.

q.q: Name one element of good governance that covers the sustainable use of natural resources and protection of the environment.
q.explanation: Efficiency in good governance covers sustainable use of natural resources and protection of the environment.

q.q: Which of the following is a role of good governance in economic development?
options: Ensuring the rule of law and better allocation of resources
q.explanation: Good governance ensures the rule of law, efficiency and better allocation and distribution of resources.

q.q: Development means only an increase in income or economic growth.
q.explanation: It also includes sustainable improvements in living standards and social well-being.

q.q: Good governance strengthens social cohesion mainly by:
options: Ensuring people have a stake and the poorest voices are heard
q.explanation: Cohesion comes from broad consensus and hearing the poorest and most vulnerable.

q.q: How does good governance promote peace?
options: By giving groups pathways to have issues represented and grievances heard
q.explanation: Peace comes from participation, representation and equitable benefits.

q.q: Name the role of good governance that gives every individual an unreserved and unhindered opportunity for development.
q.explanation: This is social justice.

q.q: Which role of good governance improves the capacity of the state and increases the efficiency of government performance?
q.explanation: This is enhancing government performance.

q.q: Transparent, responsible, accountable and participatory governance is a prerequisite for lasting respect for human dignity.
q.explanation: The textbook states this directly in the section on human rights.

q.q: Explain in one sentence how decentralization supports economic development.
q.answer: it lets society participate in its own affairs|citizens become subjects not objects of development
q.explanation: Decentralized development ensures society's participation, so citizens are subjects, not objects, of development.

q.q: When a governance system is not participatory, accountable and transparent, some groups feel excluded, which contributes to:
q.explanation: Excluded groups contribute to instability.

q.q: Which role of good governance protects the values of political and social minorities through judicial flexibility?
q.explanation: Good governance ensures social justice and opens legal systems to new justice claims.

q.q: Good governance treats citizens as:
options: Subjects who take responsibility for their lives
q.explanation: Decentralized governance means citizens are subjects who take responsibility for their own development.

q.q: Which of the following is listed as a governance challenge in developing countries?
q.explanation: The textbook lists officials who are unaccountable as a challenge.

q.q: Poverty provides fertile ground for the promotion of rights and participation.
q.explanation: The textbook says poverty does not provide fertile ground for rights and participation.

q.q: One way corruption damages the economy is by:
options: Creating a consistent budget deficit and persistent inflation
q.explanation: Corruption distorts the economy, causing a budget deficit and persistent inflation.

q.q: Name the misuse of public office or power for private gain.
q.explanation: That is corruption.

q.q: Give the term for a system in which political support is traded for jobs, money or favours.
q.explanation: This system is called clientelism.

q.q: Corruption makes democratic institutions more efficient in delivering public services.
q.explanation: Corruption makes democratic institutions inefficient and ineffective in delivering public services.

q.q: Weakness of the rule of law makes it easier for leaders to:
options: Mobilize violence at the grassroots and commit electoral fraud
q.explanation: Weak rule of law makes it easier to mobilize violence and facilitates electoral fraud and violence.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why poverty and bad governance reinforce each other.
q.answer: bad governance keeps people poor and poverty stops them demanding better governance
q.explanation: Each condition feeds the other: poverty blocks voice, and weak governance keeps people poor.

q.q: Corruption is considered a failure of institutions, especially those in charge of:
q.explanation: Corruption is a failure of institutions, particularly those in charge of investigation, prosecution and enforcement.

q.q: Which governance challenge describes courts that decide cases under pressure instead of fairly?
q.answer: courts that are not independent|dependent courts|weak judiciary
q.explanation: Courts that are not independent are a listed challenge.

q.q: Name the challenge that results in exclusion, isolation and loneliness for very poor people.
q.explanation: Extreme poverty results in exclusion, isolation and loneliness.

q.q: Governments that make decisions for those in power, without public participation, always experience:
q.explanation: The textbook says such governments always experience political instability.

q.q: The rule of law is important because it ensures the operation of power and stands against:
q.explanation: The rule of law stands against the arbitrariness of absolute rule.

q.q: Injustice can come from a lack of proper distribution of essential resources.
q.explanation: The lesson says injustice comes from poor distribution and from missing a fair share.

q.q: Give the impact that occurs when people have no chance to voice their needs while policies are formulated.
q.explanation: This is lack of empowerment.

q.q: Name the system that supports the equality of all citizens before the law and prevents arbitrary power.
q.explanation: That system is the rule of law.

q.q: Selling medicines allotted for public clinics is an example of:
options: Inefficient service delivery caused by corruption
q.explanation: It is a case of inefficient service delivery caused by corruption and weak accountability.

q.q: Give the impact when government offices do not work according to the required rules and data is not managed properly.
q.explanation: This is administrative irregularities.

q.q: Citizens can easily question government practices when there is no information about how government works.
q.explanation: Without information, government practices cannot be properly questioned.

q.q: When the political structure of a country becomes weak, every political leader is tempted to:
options: Manipulate laws and break laws on security, property and life
q.explanation: A weak political structure tempts leaders to manipulate and break laws.

q.q: In which two sectors does the lesson say failure of good governance causes lack of standards and corruption?
q.explanation: The lesson names the education and health sectors.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why lack of transparency hides official failure.
q.answer: there is no information about how government works until disgrace appears
q.explanation: With no information, failures stay hidden until some disgrace surfaces.

q.q: Corruption is defined as:
options: The honest use of public office
The misuse of public office or power for private gain
q.explanation: Corruption is the misuse of public office or power for one's own private gain.

q.q: A form of favouritism in which an office holder with the right to make appointments prefers to nominate his or her own relatives is called:
q.explanation: This is the definition of nepotism.

q.q: The direct or indirect offer of an undue payment or advantage to an official in violation of legal duties is:
q.explanation: This is the definition of bribery.

q.q: Which form is the theft or misappropriation of public resources by public officials?
q.explanation: Embezzlement is the theft or misappropriation of public resources.

q.q: Name the form of corruption that involves extracting money by coercion or threats of force.
q.explanation: This is extortion.

q.q: Corruption is more common where institutions are weak and officials are not accountable or transparent.
q.explanation: The lesson lists these conditions as where corruption is more common.

q.q: Give the mechanism of fighting corruption that uses media, campaigns, training and workshops to inform the public.
q.explanation: This mechanism is creating public awareness.

q.q: Which anti-corruption measure involves depoliticization and professionalization of officials and simplification of procedures?
q.answer: strengthening the civil service|civil service reform
q.explanation: This is strengthening the civil service.

q.q: A free and independent media fights corruption by:
options: Detecting and exposing incidents of corruption
q.explanation: Media detect, investigate and expose corruption and enhance accountability.

q.q: An independent judicial system is not needed to make sure laws against corruption are enforced.
q.explanation: Reliable, independent and effective judicial systems make sure laws and regulations are actually enforced.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why citizen participation helps fight corruption.
q.answer: it facilitates accountability and transparency and lets citizens report corrupt activities
q.explanation: Participation facilitates accountability and transparency and gives citizens a way to report corruption.

q.q: Peace can best be described as:
options: A state of mutual harmony between people or groups
A rule made by the government
q.explanation: Peace is a state of mutual harmony between people or groups and an agreement to end hostility.

q.q: Which type of peace is also called peace of mind or peace of the soul?
q.explanation: Internal peace is the state of calm within a person, free from worry and mental disturbance.

q.q: External peace in its broader sense includes social harmony, justice and respect for human rights.
q.explanation: External peace in its broader sense includes social harmony, justice, equality, order and respect for human rights.

q.q: Positive peace is best described as:
options: The absence of direct violence only
A lasting peace built on justice for all peoples
q.explanation: Positive peace is true, lasting and sustainable peace built on justice for all peoples.

q.q: Negative peace is called a false sense of peace because:
options: it is always broken by open war immediately
conflict is not reconciled even though tension remains beneath the surface
q.explanation: In negative peace, conflict is not seen in the open but the tension boils just beneath the surface because it was never reconciled.

q.q: In negative peace, the conflict has been fully reconciled, so tension cannot return.
q.explanation: In negative peace the conflict was never reconciled, so tension remains beneath the surface.

q.q: Name the type of peace that occurs in society, states and the world.
q.explanation: External peace is peace that occurs in society, states and the world.

q.q: Give the type of peace that eliminates the root causes of war, violence and injustice.
q.explanation: Positive peace involves the elimination of the root causes of war, violence and injustice.

q.q: Which of the following belongs to the features of negative peace?
options: Absence of war and direct violence
q.explanation: Negative peace is the absence of war, direct violence, fear of violence and repression.

q.q: Arrange these ideas in the order used by the lesson, starting from the peace within a person.
options: Peace among states and the world
Peace built on justice for all
q.explanation: The lesson starts with internal peace, then external peace, then positive and negative peace.

q.q: Which of the following is a security impact of the absence of peace?
options: Direct and structural violence and the denial of the right to participate
q.explanation: The absence of peace leads to direct and structural violence and denies people the right to participate.

q.q: Absence of peace undermines socio-economic development mainly because:
options: resources are diverted from health and education to military expenditure
q.explanation: During violent conflict, competing forces divert resources from health, education and investment to military spending.

q.q: Quiet streets always prove that a community enjoys true peace.
q.explanation: Tension can boil beneath the surface while open conflict is hidden; quiet streets do not always mean peace.

q.q: Which group often suffers most from the consequences of conflict?
q.explanation: Women and children face a high risk of sexual and gender-based violence, abuse and displacement.

q.q: When groups compete for power and resource control and leaders become more tribal than national, the absence of peace has caused:
options: a failure to accommodate cultural diversity
q.explanation: The struggle for power and resources leads to tribalism and inter-tribal oppression, endangering cultural diversity.

q.q: Displacement can result when families cannot fulfil their basic needs because of conflict.
q.explanation: Inability to fulfil basic needs forces people to be displaced and to migrate to other areas.

q.q: Name the kind of violence that is built into social structures, such as the exclusion of the poor.
q.explanation: Structural violence is inherent in the exclusion of the poor and in the denial of participation.

q.q: Give the term for the long-lasting violent quarrel between families or clans in which each side seeks revenge.
q.explanation: The escalation of conflict into revenge between families is called a bloody feud or blood feud.

q.q: Which of these is an impact of the absence of peace on human rights?
options: People are deprived of the right to live in dignity
q.explanation: People in conflict-affected areas are deprived of their right to live in dignity and of opportunities to develop.

q.q: What is created when conflict is hidden but suspicion and hatred divide people into a trusted group and an excluded group?
q.answer: in-groups against out-groups|in-group and out-group|social disharmony
q.explanation: The absence of peace puts in place suspicion, hatred and the creation of in-groups against out-groups.

q.q: Besides farming and trading, name one economic activity that declines when peace is absent.
q.explanation: The textbook states that trading, farming, fishing and investment decline when there is no peace.

q.q: Peace building is best defined as:
options: A single meeting to sign an agreement
A long-term process of ensuring durable peace by addressing root causes of conflict
The use of force to stop fighting
q.explanation: Peace building is a long-term process of ensuring peace and preventing the recurrence of violence by addressing root causes.

q.q: Simply stopping the fighting means putting a permanent end to violence.
q.explanation: The lesson states clearly that stopping the fighting does not mean putting a permanent end to violence.

q.q: Peace building seeks to integrate competing or alienated groups into mainstream society by providing:
options: only financial aid for a short period
equitable access to political decision-making, social networks, economic resources and information
q.explanation: Integration is achieved through equitable access to decision-making, social networks, economic resources and information.

q.q: Give the term for restoring good relations between former opponents so that they can live together in peace.
q.explanation: Reconciliation is the restoration of good relations between former opponents.

q.q: Which of the following is a peace building activity?
options: Promoting a culture of justice, truth and reconciliation
Forcing one side to leave the area
q.explanation: Peace building promotes a culture of justice, truth and reconciliation and reforms justice and security institutions.

q.q: Peace building strives to transform the social institutions and the discourse that reproduce a culture of violence.
q.explanation: Peace building transforms institutions and discourse that reproduce a culture of violence and structural violence.

q.q: Name the kind of peace that peace building aims to create because its causes have been transformed.
q.explanation: Peace building creates self-sustaining and durable peace.

q.q: According to the lesson, which is a dimension of peace building?
options: Returning to violence when talks fail
q.explanation: Successful peace building reforms justice and security institutions among its many activities.

q.q: Name the principle that requires everyone, including leaders, to be subject to the law applied fairly.
q.explanation: Creating rule of law mechanisms is one of the goals of successful peace building.

q.q: Arrange these peace building actions in the order likely to lead to lasting peace.
options: Address the root causes of the conflict
Bring the conflicting parties together to talk
q.explanation: Peace building starts with bringing parties together, then addressing root causes, then reforming institutions for the long term.

q.q: Name one thing that peace building additionally protects besides peace itself.
q.explanation: Peace building protects human rights and creates rule of law mechanisms.

q.q: Indigenous conflict resolution mechanisms are best defined as:
options: Courts set up by the central government
Grass-roots and community-based ways of solving conflict according to customary practices
q.explanation: They are grass-roots and community-based mechanisms based on the customary practices of a society.

q.q: In indigenous conflict resolution, one of the parties always wins and the other always loses.
q.explanation: Rather than one party winning and the other losing, both parties stand to benefit from reconciliation.

q.q: Which mechanism belongs to the Amhara people?
q.explanation: Shimagille, also called Shimglina, is the indigenous mechanism of the Amhara.

q.q: The Oromo indigenous conflict resolution mechanism is called:
q.explanation: Jaarsummaa is the Oromo indigenous conflict resolution mechanism.

q.q: Name the Somali customary system of conflict resolution mentioned in the lesson.
q.explanation: Xeer is the indigenous conflict resolution mechanism of the Somali.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT a common feature of indigenous conflict resolution mechanisms?
q.explanation: The mechanisms are flexible and context specific, not rigid; rigidity is not one of their features.

q.q: Indigenous conflict resolution mechanisms rely on social pressure and exclusion for non-compliance rather than coercion.
q.explanation: They do not have coercive mechanisms and rely on social pressure and exclusion from the community.

q.q: Who usually leads the process of indigenous conflict resolution in Ethiopia?
q.explanation: The process is led by influential elders or community leaders.

q.q: Give the term for the restorative penalty paid by one family or clan to another that enables reconciliation.
q.explanation: Compensation is often paid as a restorative penalty that enables parties to be reconciled.

q.q: Elders acquire their position in the community mainly by virtue of:
options: age, knowledge of culture, lineage, tradition or influence
q.explanation: Elders acquire their position through age, knowledge of culture, lineage and tradition, or influence in the community.

q.q: Besides elders, name one other actor in the indigenous resolution process.
q.explanation: Other actors include religious leaders, family members and community members.

q.q: Indigenous social institutions in Africa have served as means of:
options: governance, conflict resolution and security promotion
q.explanation: They serve as means of governance, conflict resolution, security promotion and the provision of social, economic and political functions.

q.q: The ultimate aim of sustainable peace, according to the lesson, is:
q.explanation: The ultimate aim of sustainable peace is the restoration of relationships.

q.q: Indigenous conflict resolution is geared towards the future rather than towards punishing past deeds.
q.explanation: The issue at stake is not punishment for past deeds but the reinstitution of a basis for reconciliation.

q.q: Which traditional institution is described as a burial and mutual-aid society?
q.explanation: Idir is the community association that provides burial support and mutual aid.

q.q: Name the traditional rotating savings association that strengthens economic trust in the community.
q.explanation: Iqub is the rotating savings and credit association.

q.q: Why do indigenous institutions address the spiritual and emotional side of conflict?
options: because mental healing of traumatised people is as important as material reconstruction
q.explanation: The mental healing of those traumatised by conflict is an aspect of peace building at least as important as material reconstruction.

q.q: Indigenous social institutions are less accessible to the community than modern institutions.
q.explanation: Unlike other modern institutions, indigenous social institutions are accessible to communities.

q.q: Give the decision method that indigenous institutions rely on, in which accused and accuser argue until one side is more persuasive.
q.explanation: They tend to rely on consensus, allowing accused and accuser to argue without interruption.

q.q: Name the action of bringing a deviant member back into the community instead of excluding them permanently.
q.explanation: Re-establishing harmony implies reintegrating deviant members to restore good relations.

q.q: Which of the following is a role of indigenous social institutions?
q.explanation: Ensuring accessibility to the community is one of the roles described in the lesson.

q.q: Name one spiritual authority, besides elders, who carries out purification and healing in customary processes.
q.explanation: Customary healers, priests and sheiks carry out traditional methods of purification and healing.

q.q: Federalism is best defined as:
options: A system in which all power is held by the central government
A system in which power is divided between federal and regional governments
A system with no government at all
A system in which regions have no powers
q.explanation: Federalism divides power between federal and regional governments.

q.q: Under a federal arrangement neither the federal nor the regional governments is supreme.
q.explanation: Devolution makes neither level supreme; power is coordinated between them.

q.q: What is the name of the principle of federalism that transfers power to the regions that make up the federation?
q.explanation: Devolution transfers power to the regions that constitute the federation.

q.q: The main reason for coordinating power between the centre and the regions is to:
q.explanation: Coordinated power helps to avoid a monopoly of power.

q.q: Give the term for the level of government that governs issues of local concern under a federation.
q.explanation: Smaller regional governments govern issues of local concern.

q.q: According to the scholar definitions, each level of government in a federation:
options: takes orders from the other level
makes final decisions on some activities
is created by the other level
q.explanation: Each kind of government has activities on which it makes final decisions.

q.q: In a federation each level of government is directly elected by its citizens and can deal directly with them.
q.explanation: Each level is empowered to deal directly with its citizens and is directly elected by them.

q.q: In the Lower Omo case, the regional state could not cope with the flood alone. This shows that:
options: the two levels of government are interdependent
the federal government owns all land
q.explanation: The case showed the interdependence of the regional states and the federal government.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why the Lower Omo flood response involved both the federal and regional governments.
q.answer: the disaster was beyond the capacity of the regional state|the challenge exceeded the capacity of one level
q.explanation: Confronting the disaster was beyond the capacity of the regional state, so coordinated action was needed.

q.q: Arrange the steps of the Lower Omo story in the correct order.
options: The regional governments mobilise resources for the victims
The federal and regional governments coordinate their effort
Heavy rain makes the river overflow and the regional state cannot cope
The federal government steps in to help the victims
q.explanation: The flood exceeds the regional capacity first, then the federal government helps and the wider coordinated effort follows.

q.q: Which statement describes dual federalism?
options: Government authority is clearly divided between state and national governments
Only the central government has powers
q.explanation: Dual federalism clearly divides government authority between state and national governments.

q.q: Cooperative federalism is also known as marble cake federalism.
q.explanation: Cooperative federalism is called marble cake federalism because powers mix together.

q.q: What other name is given to dual federalism?
q.explanation: Dual federalism is often called layer cake federalism.

q.q: In con-federal arrangements:
options: the central government has direct authority over citizens
the central government has no direct authority over citizens' lives
the states have no power at all
q.explanation: In con-federal arrangements the central government has no direct authority over citizens' lives.

q.q: Which is an advantage of dual federalism?
options: It increases tension between the levels
It protects local jurisdictions from federal overreach
It weakens the unity of the states
q.explanation: Dual federalism protects local jurisdictions and prevents the federal government from holding too much power.

q.q: Give the name of the classification in which an existing state restructures itself to hold its diverse groups together.
q.explanation: This is holding-together federalism, the pattern followed by Ethiopia.

q.q: One disadvantage of cooperative federalism is a decrease in the powers of the states.
q.explanation: The federal government may intervene in policies once reserved to the states.

q.q: Explain in one sentence how federal laws differ from state laws in a federation.
q.answer: federal laws apply in all states while state laws apply only in their own region|federal laws apply to all states
q.explanation: Laws made by the states apply to their own regions, while federal laws apply to all states.

q.q: The federal government giving tax revenue to the states to fund interstate highways, with the states managing construction, is an example of:
q.explanation: Shared funding and implementation are features of cooperative federalism.

q.q: A disadvantage of dual federalism is that:
options: local laws can never be made
tension between the state and federal governments stays at the brim
q.explanation: Dual federalism keeps tension between the two levels high, harming cooperation.

q.q: Arrange the levels of federal power from the most local to the widest community.
q.explanation: The order is local government, then state government, then the federal government.

q.q: Federations are distinguished from other polities primarily because political power is:
options: constitutionally divided between the federal government and the states
q.explanation: Political power is constitutionally divided between the federal government and the states.

q.q: In a federation the states are creations of the federal government.
q.explanation: In a federation the states are not creations of the federal government; both levels derive authority from the constitution.

q.q: Which branch of government adjudicates constitutional disputes in a federation?
q.explanation: A special judiciary with wide powers adjudicates constitutional disputes.

q.q: In a decentralised system of government, local governments:
options: are equal partners of the centre
are subordinate to the centre and may be revoked by it
derive power from the constitution in their own right
q.explanation: Local governments in a decentralised system are subordinate to the centre and subject to unilateral revocation.

q.q: Which of the following is a key feature of federalism?
options: A written and supreme federal constitution
A single house of parliament only
q.explanation: The division of power is based on a written and supreme federal constitution.

q.q: Give the name for the principle that allows the centre to take back delegated authority on its own decision.
q.explanation: Delegation in a decentralised system is subject to unilateral withdrawal or revocation by the centre.

q.q: A constitution of a federation should be more or less rigid.
q.explanation: A rigid constitution protects the autonomy of the federating states from the centre.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why the authority of each level of government must come from the constitution.
q.answer: so that neither level depends on the other|the authority of one should not depend on the other
q.explanation: If the two levels are to remain autonomous, the authority of one should not depend on the other.

q.q: The dual principle implicit in every federation is the desire to be:
q.explanation: The underlying notion is the desire to be united for some purposes and autonomous for others.

q.q: Which body may declare a national or local law invalid when it conflicts with the constitution?
q.explanation: The special judiciary is vested with power to declare any law at variance with the constitution invalid.

q.q: Arrange the creation of a federal bargain in the correct order.
options: Both levels are bound by the supreme constitution
A written constitution records the terms of the bargain
A bargain is struck between the union and the states
q.explanation: The bargain comes first, then it is written into a constitution that binds both levels.

q.q: Which of the following is an advantage of federalism?
q.explanation: Federalism divides power and spreads it among branches, which deters tyranny.

q.q: A federal government must have a written constitution.
q.explanation: A federation is a political partnership and therefore needs a written agreement.

q.q: What must a federation establish to adjudicate constitutional disputes?
q.explanation: A special judiciary with wide powers is established to guard the constitution.

q.q: The cookie-cutter method of law and policy making is criticised because:
options: it is too expensive to write
a national solution may be effective in some states and less effective in others
it gives too much power to the states
q.explanation: Uniform national solutions suit some states and not others, which reduces efficiency.

q.q: Which is a disadvantage of federalism?
q.explanation: Federalism allows regional inequalities in services such as education, taxes and health care.

q.q: Give the term for the situation in which each level of government blames the other instead of taking responsibility.
q.explanation: Shared responsibility can produce a lack of accountability.

q.q: Under federalism, citizens can participate in decision making at the grass roots.
q.explanation: The dual level of government increases citizen participation at the grass roots.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why a flexible constitution is dangerous in a federation.
q.answer: it allows the central government to curtail the autonomy of the states|the centre could reduce state autonomy
q.explanation: A flexible constitution allows the centre to reduce the autonomy of the federating states.

q.q: The biggest problem arising from having two bodies of government in power is:
q.explanation: Both levels intend to assert their power over the other, which causes conflict.

q.q: The special judiciary in a federation should act as:
options: the custodian and guardian of the constitution
q.explanation: It acts as the custodian and guardian of the constitution and may declare invalid conflicting laws.

q.q: Arrange these duties of a court in a federal dispute in the correct order.
options: Declare the law invalid if it conflicts with the constitution
Receive a dispute between the centre and a unit
Compare the disputed law with the constitution
q.explanation: The court first receives the dispute, then compares the law with the constitution, and only then decides.

q.q: The main rationale of federalism in contemporary Ethiopia is:
options: increasing the size of the army
reconciling ethnic diversity with political unity
q.explanation: The rationale is primarily the reconciliation of ethnic diversity with political unity.

q.q: Before federalism, Ethiopia experienced a highly centralised unitary state structure for almost a century.
q.explanation: For almost a century Ethiopia had a highly centralised unitary state structure.

q.q: In which year did Ethiopia begin implementing its federal system?
q.explanation: Ethiopia has been implementing federalism since 1995.

q.q: The slogan of one nation, one language and one religion had the effect of:
q.explanation: This propaganda completely sidelined the virtues of diversity.

q.q: According to Article 50(8) of the FDRE constitution:
options: the states and the federal government must respect each other's powers
only the federal government has powers
regions may cross into federal affairs
q.explanation: The states shall respect federal powers and the federal government shall respect state powers.

q.q: Name the upper house of the Ethiopian federal legislature.
q.answer: House of Federation|the house of the federation
q.explanation: The House of Federation is the upper house.

q.q: Each nationality in Ethiopia is represented in the House of Federation by at least one member.
q.explanation: Each nationality is represented at least by one member, with more for larger groups.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why some weak constituent states call for an asymmetric federal system.
q.answer: they have not yet evolved as viable regional governments|weak capacity requires more extensive federal powers
q.explanation: Some states lack experience, manpower and resources, so federal powers need to be more extensive in relation to them.

q.q: Which power is given to the House of Federation in the Ethiopian constitution?
q.explanation: The Ethiopian constitution empowers the House of Federation to interpret the constitution.

q.q: Which of the following countries is named in the lesson as a state that implements federalism?
q.explanation: India is listed with Ethiopia, Nigeria, Brazil, the United States, Canada, Australia and Germany.

q.q: Arrange these Ethiopian federal features from the widest national organ to the group-based house.
q.explanation: The House of Peoples Representatives is the supreme political organ; the House of Federation follows as the upper, group-based house.

q.q: Human rights are best defined as:
options: Privileges granted by a government to loyal citizens
Fundamental entitlements that belong to every member of the human race
Rights enjoyed only by adults who pay taxes
Rules made by the United Nations for its members only
q.explanation: Human rights are fundamental entitlements belonging to every member of the human race because they are human.

q.q: According to the UDHR, the only criterion a person must fulfil to enjoy human rights is:
options: Being a citizen of a UN member state
q.explanation: Article 2 of the UDHR says the only criterion is being human.

q.q: Which feature means human rights cannot be lost because they are linked to the very fact of human existence?
q.explanation: Inalienability means the rights cannot be lost because they are linked to human existence.

q.q: First generation rights consist mainly of:
options: Rights of the state over its citizens
q.explanation: The first generation consists of civil and political rights linked to the English, American and French revolutions.

q.q: Human rights apply equally to all people everywhere in the world and with no time limit.
q.explanation: This is the feature of universalism described in the lesson.

q.q: The universality of human rights means that all cultures must become uniform.
q.explanation: The lesson states that universality is not synonymous with uniformity.

q.q: Name the 1948 declaration adopted by the UN General Assembly that sets out human rights.
q.explanation: This is the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

q.q: Give the feature that means human rights cannot be taken away by any power or authority because they belong to a person simply because he or she is human.
q.explanation: The lesson defines this feature as irrevocable.

q.q: Explain what it means that human rights are indivisible and interdependent.
q.answer: they are intrinsically connected|one right depends on the enjoyment of many others|no right is more important than the rest
q.explanation: Rights are connected, the enjoyment of one depends on others, and no right is more important than the rest.

q.q: Which of the following is a second generation right?
options: The right to a fair and public trial
q.explanation: The right to education appears in Articles 22 to 27, which cover economic, social and cultural rights.

q.q: Arrange the generations of human rights in the order in which they emerged.
options: Second generation (economic, social and cultural rights)
q.explanation: The correct order is first generation, then second generation, then third generation.

q.q: According to the lesson, a person's obligation arises from:
q.explanation: The lesson states that your obligation arises from the right you enjoy.

q.q: Which of the following is listed as an obligation of citizens for protecting human rights?
q.explanation: The lesson lists respect for religious equality, gender equality, the rights of others and the national flag.

q.q: Human rights involve responsibility and duty towards other people and the community.
q.explanation: This is stated at the start of the lesson.

q.q: The obligation that requires the state to refrain from interfering with the enjoyment of rights is the obligation to:
q.explanation: The obligation to respect means the state must not interfere with the enjoyment of rights.

q.q: Which obligation requires states to protect individuals against abuses by non-state actors and foreign state agents?
q.explanation: The obligation to protect concerns abuses by non-state actors, foreign state agents, or state agents acting outside official capacity.

q.q: The obligation to protect entails both a preventative and a remedial dimension.
q.explanation: The lesson states that the obligation to protect has both dimensions.

q.q: Give the state obligation that requires positive action so that human rights can be realized, including providing free and compulsory primary education.
q.explanation: The obligation to fulfill requires positive action to ensure rights can be realized.

q.q: Name one obligation of citizens mentioned in the lesson.
q.answer: respect for religious equality|respect for gender equality|respect for the rights of others|respect for the national flag
q.explanation: Any of the four citizen obligations listed in the lesson.

q.q: Explain why the state must be aware of possible threats in order to meet the obligation to protect.
q.answer: because the obligation to protect includes a preventative dimension|the state must act when it is aware or could have been aware of threats
q.explanation: The preventative dimension obliges the state to act when it is aware, or could have been aware, of threats to human rights.

q.q: Under the obligation to fulfill, states should create which conditions that rights holders need?
options: Only conditions chosen by foreign states
q.explanation: States should create the legal, institutional and procedural conditions needed to realize rights in full.

q.q: Arrange the three state obligations in the order in which the lesson presents them.
q.explanation: The lesson presents respect first, then protect, then fulfill.

q.q: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly on:
q.explanation: The UDHR was adopted on December 10, 1948.

q.q: The UDHR is a legally binding treaty that directly binds every state.
q.explanation: The UDHR is not a legally binding instrument, although it is highly influential.

q.q: Which article of the UN Charter refers to the human rights and fundamental freedoms that the UDHR was adopted to define?
q.explanation: The Declaration defined the rights referenced in Article 55(c) of the UN Charter.

q.q: Which of the following is a core international human rights instrument?
options: The Convention on the Rights of the Child
q.explanation: The CRC is one of the core UN human rights instruments.

q.q: In which year was the FDRE Constitution ratified?
q.explanation: The FDRE Constitution was ratified in 1994.

q.q: Give the article of the FDRE Constitution which states that human rights and freedoms, emanating from the nature of mankind, are inviolable and inalienable.
q.explanation: Article 10 articulates that human rights are inviolable and inalienable.

q.q: According to Articles 9(4) and 13 of the FDRE Constitution, international agreements ratified by Ethiopia are:
options: An integral part of the law of the land
q.explanation: Ratified agreements are an integral part of the law of the land and guide interpretation of rights.

q.q: Name the national institution established to promote and protect human rights in Ethiopia.
q.answer: Ethiopian Human Rights Commission|national human rights commission|Human Rights Commission
q.explanation: The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission is the national human rights institution.

q.q: Regional human rights systems cover Africa, the Americas and Europe.
q.explanation: The regional human rights systems cover Africa, the Americas and Europe.

q.q: Explain why the UDHR can be called a common standard even though it is not legally binding.
q.answer: it defines human rights and fundamental freedoms|many states incorporated its principles into their constitutions|it is the foundation of later treaties
q.explanation: The UDHR defines human rights and fundamental freedoms and became the foundation of constitutions and later treaties.

q.q: Arrange these instruments in the order in which they were adopted.
options: The Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees (1951)
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)
q.explanation: The order is Slavery Convention 1926, UDHR 1948, Refugee Convention 1951, International Covenants 1966.

q.q: The word patriotism comes from the Latin term patria, which means:
q.explanation: Patria is the Latin word for fatherland.

q.q: Patriotism is only a feeling and is never shown through action.
q.explanation: The lesson states that patriotism is practical or action oriented.

q.q: In a democratic system, patriotism means devoting time, ability, knowledge and even life for:
options: The fundamental principles on which the nation's security and welfare depend
q.explanation: In a democratic system patriotism is devotion to the fundamental principles on which the nation's security and welfare depend.

q.q: In which settings does the textbook say patriotism is expressed?
q.explanation: Patriotism is expressed in the war front, research, good ethics, competence in work, leadership and responsibility.

q.q: Give the term for being excessively or overly loyal to one's country, race or gender, often at the expense of others.
q.explanation: This is the glossary definition of chauvinism.

q.q: The definition of patriotism depends on the nature of the existing political system.
q.explanation: The textbook says the definition of patriotism depends on the nature of the existing political system.

q.q: Nationalism in modern history refers to a movement in which:
options: The nation state is regarded as paramount for realising the aspirations of the people
q.explanation: Nationalism regards the nation state as paramount for the realisation of social, economic and cultural aspirations.

q.q: Explain how patriotism creates a feeling of oneness among citizens.
q.answer: shared sentiment|same homeland|attachment to the country
q.explanation: Citizens who share love and attachment for the same homeland are drawn together into a feeling of oneness.

q.q: Which Greek-style Latin word is the origin of the term patriotism?
q.explanation: The term comes from the Latin patria, meaning fatherland.

q.q: Which statement best describes a true patriot?
options: Someone proud of the country's history, culture and standing in world affairs
Someone who takes undue advantage of the country
Someone who abandons the country in hardship
q.explanation: A true patriot feels proud of the country's history, culture and standing in world affairs.

q.q: Constitutional patriotism refers to strong commitment or alignment with:
q.explanation: Constitutional patriotism is commitment or alignment with democracy and human rights.

q.q: Traditional patriotism is best described as:
options: Readiness to give one's life for the motherland
Respect for the national anthem only
q.explanation: Traditional patriotism is readiness to give one's life for the mother land.

q.q: Which type of patriotism is shown by an individual whose actions have a positive impact on the country, even at the risk of life?
q.explanation: Icon patriots show love through actions with a positive impact and are willing to risk their lives.

q.q: Symbolic patriotism is shown by respect for national symbols such as the flag and the national anthem.
q.explanation: Symbolic patriotism is symbolised by respect for national symbols.

q.q: Capital patriotism focuses mainly on:
options: The development of the national economy
q.explanation: Capital patriots focus on developing the national economy and raising the image of the country.

q.q: Give the type of patriotism shown by someone who loves and improves the country's environment.
q.explanation: This is environmental patriotism.

q.q: Traditional patriotism always aligns the patriot's feelings with democratic principles.
q.explanation: In traditional patriotism there is no attempt to align one's feelings with democratic principles.

q.q: Which one of the following is NOT a type of patriotism discussed in the lesson?
q.explanation: The types discussed are constitutional, traditional, icon, symbolic, capital and environmental patriotism.

q.q: Explain how constitutional patriotism treats people of different language, colour, sex and religion.
q.explanation: It calls on individuals to acknowledge and appreciate such differences and to live in coexistence and tolerance.

q.q: An Ethiopian doctor returns from abroad to work in a rural hospital in a difficult area. Which type of patriotism is shown most clearly?
q.explanation: The doctor shows love for the country through an action with a strong positive impact, which characterises icon patriotism.

q.q: Constitutional patriotism is based upon the principle of:
q.explanation: Constitutional patriotism is based upon the principle of equality.

q.q: In Ethiopia today the basis of patriotism lies in citizens' rights and responsibilities.
q.explanation: The textbook states that the basis of patriotism in Ethiopia nowadays lies in citizens' rights and responsibilities.

q.q: In a democratic system, citizens are expected to be loyal to all of the following EXCEPT:
q.explanation: Loyalty is owed to the constitution, the people, the elected government and the community, not to personal desire alone.

q.q: Give the name of the important attribute of true patriotism that means respecting and accepting differences in values as normal for peaceful coexistence.
q.explanation: This attribute is tolerance.

q.q: Tolerance is a gift that citizens give to others.
q.explanation: Tolerance is not a gift; it is a very important constitutional and civil obligation.

q.q: Which battle is given as the example of Ethiopians defending their country's independence?
q.explanation: The victory of Adwa represents the patriotic deed of Ethiopian nations, nationalities and peoples.

q.q: According to the lesson, any law, customary practice or official decision that contravenes the constitution shall be:
q.explanation: The constitution is supreme and anything contravening it shall be of no effect.

q.q: Explain why praising only the country's mountains, rivers and soil does not by itself show patriotism.
q.answer: must include citizens' rights and responsibilities|patriotism is based on citizens
q.explanation: Patriotism today is based on citizens' rights and responsibilities, not merely on praise of geography and natural values.

q.q: True patriots carry out their tasks without what?
q.explanation: True patriots carry out their tasks without any enforcement and are self-reliant.

q.q: Which base of patriotism is shown by a citizen who gives up personal benefit for the good of the community?
options: Sacrificing personal desires and interests for the common good
q.explanation: True patriots sacrifice their personal desires and interests for the common good.

q.q: According to the lesson, growing up with patriotic sentiments helps children to:
options: Have a better sense of self
q.explanation: Children who grow up with patriotic sentiments tend to have a better sense of self.

q.q: Watching the Ethiopian flag waving high at different events makes Ethiopians feel:
q.explanation: The flag gives Ethiopians a sense of belonging and helps them feel good about their country.

q.q: Fighting for a better nation means getting involved in a wrangle with other citizens.
q.explanation: Fighting for a better nation does not mean quarrelling with citizens; it means working to remove the country's drawbacks and injustice.

q.q: Patriotic citizens make sure that they fulfil their duties and do not take undue advantage of what?
q.explanation: Patriotic citizens do not take undue advantage of their rights and privileges.

q.q: Explain how patriotism builds a stronger nation.
q.answer: motivates each individual to work for the country's betterment|helps the nation work together and stay united
q.explanation: Patriotism motivates individuals to work for the country's betterment and helps the whole nation to work together and stay united.

q.q: Patriotism is contagious and often affects the people around the conscious citizen.
q.explanation: The textbook says patriotism is contagious and affects people around, which is how conscious citizens help their country.

q.q: Which of the following is a trait of a patriotic citizen?
options: Waiting for others to act first
Eagerness to make the country better
q.explanation: Eagerness to make the country better is a listed trait of patriotism.

q.q: In the case study, the nurse Roza should refuse the 500 birr because:
options: Accepting it would give unfair favour and harm patients on the waiting list
The hospital forbids tips only for nurses
She did not like the patient
q.explanation: Accepting the money would take undue advantage of her position and would injure the rights of other patients.

q.q: Give the trait of patriotism shown by citizens who voice their opinions about wrongdoings and injustice in order to free the country from them.
q.explanation: This is the trait of fighting for a better nation.

q.q: Conscious citizens are not those who expect other people to take the first step; what do they do instead?
q.answer: take the initiative|take the tasks ahead
q.explanation: Conscious citizens take the initiative to take the tasks ahead.

q.q: History is defined in the lesson as the narration about the past based on:
q.explanation: History is the narration about the past based on fact.

q.q: Fabricated history teaches true values and helps citizens live in harmony.
q.explanation: True history teaches values, whereas fabricated history creates false impressions used to mislead.

q.q: Give the term for information whose exposure endangers the very existence of the nation.
q.explanation: Such information is called a state secret.

q.q: The common good, also called civic virtue, means:
options: The subordination of personal interest to the good of the community
The interest of a single ethnic group
q.explanation: The common good denotes the subordination of personal interest to the good of the community.

q.q: Which of the following is a factor affecting the common good?
options: Common spirit and joint effort of citizens
q.explanation: Selfish personal interests are a factor that works against the common good.

q.q: Corruption is characterised by acts such as nepotism and embezzlement.
q.explanation: Corruption is unlawful behaviour characterised by such acts as nepotism and embezzlement.

q.q: Give the duty shown by a citizen who gives service to the community not for price or personal enrichment.
q.explanation: This is voluntarism.

q.q: Poverty reduction aims to reduce poverty to a level where citizens can meet at least what?
q.answer: their basic necessities|basic needs of life
q.explanation: Poverty reduction aims at a level where citizens meet at least their basic necessities of life.

q.q: Why is poverty described as a stumbling block for democracy?
options: Because it is followed by inequalities, transgression and rebellion
Because it reduces the number of parties
q.explanation: Poverty is followed by inequalities, transgression and rebellion that work against democratic ideas.

q.q: Arrange the steps Zeleke took to improve his old school.
options: Collect the money and equipment with the committee
Observe that the school lacks teaching materials
Form a committee of community members and teachers
Explain the problem to the elders and write to former students
q.explanation: He first observed the problem, explained it to the elders and wrote to former students, then formed a committee that collected the money and equipment.

q.q: Explain why a patriot must know the true history of the country.
q.answer: it shapes values and beliefs|it helps solve current problems and build tolerance
q.explanation: Understanding the true history helps citizens understand present problems, develop tolerance and mutual understanding, and build a patriotic feeling.

q.q: Globalization refers to:
options: the linkages and interconnections between states and societies
the traditions of a single country
q.explanation: Globalization is the multiplicity of linkages and interconnections between the states and societies of the modern world system.

q.q: The integration of national economies through trade, investment, capital flows, migration and technology is called:
q.explanation: This is the definition of economic globalization.

q.q: Globalization explains how events in one part of the world can have consequences in distant parts.
q.explanation: Globalization describes how events and decisions in one place affect communities far away.

q.q: The spread of political policies, ideologies and institutions across countries describes:
q.explanation: Political globalization is the diffusion of policies, ideologies, political culture and institutions across countries.

q.q: Sharing ideas and information through the internet and social media is the:
q.explanation: The social dimension covers the sharing of ideas and information between countries using the internet and social media.

q.q: Name the four dimensions of globalization.
q.explanation: Globalization combines political, economic, social and cultural dimensions.

q.q: Explain what is meant by cultural globalization.
q.answer: sharing of ideas, meanings and values across cultures|integration and diffusion of cultures worldwide
q.explanation: Cultural globalization is the circulation of ideas, values, meanings and cultures across countries.

q.q: Which example best shows cultural globalization?
options: Ethiopian coffee drunk around the world
q.explanation: Coffee originating in Ethiopia and consumed worldwide shows the spread of a product and taste across cultures.

q.q: Economic globalization is the only dimension of globalization.
q.explanation: Globalization also has political, social and cultural dimensions.

q.q: Give the term for the increasing interdependence of world economies.
q.explanation: Economic globalization is the increasing interdependence of world economies.

q.q: According to the lesson, whether globalization helps or harms a country depends mainly on:
q.explanation: The advantage or disadvantage of globalization depends on the way governments manage it.

q.q: Which is an economic advantage of globalization?
options: a sharp increase in trade and economic growth
q.explanation: Globalization led to a sharp increase in trade and economic exchange and strong global economic growth.

q.q: Globalization can help protect human rights through international treaties.
q.explanation: Participation in international treaties helps protect human rights at international and regional level.

q.q: Receiving money from a relative abroad through a money transfer agent is an example of:
q.explanation: Financial globalization eases the flow of capital, including remittances from relatives abroad.

q.q: The negative impact in which criminals use open markets and new technology for illegal trade is called:
q.explanation: Personal insecurity arises as criminals use deregulated markets, technology and cheap transport for illicit trade.

q.q: Give one disadvantage of globalization for a developing country.
q.explanation: Any listed disadvantage such as wider inequality, brain-drain or cultural loss is correct.

q.q: Explain what is meant by the homogenization of culture.
q.answer: cultures becoming more alike|losing differences|imported culture replaces local culture
q.explanation: Cultural exchange has made cultures more alike, so some local cultures and languages disappear.

q.q: The movement of educated people from poor to rich countries is called:
q.explanation: Economic stagnation triggers a substantial brain-drain from poor countries.

q.q: Globalization has no effect on the environment.
q.explanation: Globalization contributes to greenhouse emissions, global warming, deforestation and plastic pollution.

q.q: Explain why good management matters for globalization.
q.answer: it decides whether effects are positive or negative|management turns opportunities into benefits
q.explanation: If countries manage globalization well they gain its advantages; if not, they suffer its disadvantages.

q.q: Ignoring the very real costs of globalization is described as:
q.explanation: The textbook states that ignoring the real costs of globalization is not possible and defensible.

q.q: Teaching local creativity in agriculture, medicine and food preparation is a way of:
q.explanation: This is promoting indigenous knowledge through the education system.

q.q: Community development works because local people know best what their community needs.
q.explanation: Local people know better than anyone else what will make a difference to their lives.

q.q: School feeding and public employment schemes are examples of:
q.explanation: Protective measures are basic transfers that stop vulnerable groups from starving, such as school feeding.

q.q: Sustained cooperation among three or more countries for mutual gains is called:
q.explanation: This is the definition of regional cooperation in the lesson.

q.q: Explain the role of an innovation fund.
q.answer: rewards research useful to developing countries|encourages innovations of benefit to developing countries
q.explanation: An innovation fund encourages innovations of benefit to developing countries through a prize system.

q.q: Name one traditional Ethiopian mutual-help group named in the lesson.
q.explanation: Traditional and community-based support mechanisms are the first line of defence in Ethiopia.

q.q: Which measure prevents people from falling into destitution?
q.explanation: Preventive measures stop people from falling into destitution through savings, insurance and child allowances.

q.q: Arrange the five ways of fighting the negative impacts of globalization in the order given in the lesson.
q.explanation: The order is: indigenous knowledge, community development, social protection, regional cooperation, innovation fund.

q.q: Explain why promoting indigenous knowledge is important for young people.
q.answer: helps them value their own traditions|value their own creative efforts
q.explanation: It helps the young value their own creative efforts and traditional practices rather than depending only on foreign ideas.

q.q: A global issue is best described as:
options: any issue that adversely affects the global community and environment
q.explanation: A global issue is any issue that adversely affects the global community and environment.

q.q: Which of the following is a criterion for identifying a global issue?
options: the extent or scope of the issue
q.explanation: The criteria are extent or scope, urgency or intensity, and centrality or location.

q.q: Global issues can range from minor shared problems to catastrophic risks threatening the whole human race.
q.explanation: Global issues vary from minor issues that affect everyone to global catastrophic risks.

q.q: The biggest problem caused by climate change is:
q.explanation: Although many problems exist, the biggest problem of climate change is global warming.

q.q: Which is a main human cause of climate change?
q.explanation: Massive industrialization, rapid population growth and rapid urbanization are named as human causes.

q.q: Explain why poverty is considered a global issue.
q.answer: its effects cross borders|weakens states and threatens stability|can no longer be contained within national boundaries
q.explanation: Poverty and its outcomes can no longer be contained within national boundaries and threaten global stability.

q.q: The state in which people are looking for jobs but cannot find them is called:
q.explanation: This is the definition of unemployment given in the lesson.

q.q: Growth in travel and migration has helped spread diseases such as HIV/AIDS and Covid-19.
q.explanation: Travel and migration helped spread these diseases to new locations around the world.

q.q: Define terrorism as given in the lesson.
q.answer: unlawful use of violence against civilians to intimidate or coerce|use of violence against non-combatants for a political cause
q.explanation: Terrorism is the use of violence against civilians or non-combatants for political aims.

q.q: Name two major global issues discussed in the lesson.
q.explanation: The lesson covers climate change, poverty, population, unemployment, disease and terrorism.

q.q: Why is terrorism a global agenda?
options: it creates uncertainty in developing countries only
it threatens the security of all countries of the world
q.explanation: Terrorism threatens the security of all countries of the world, which makes it a global agenda.

q.q: Which of the following is FALSE about utility?
options: The utility of a product can be different at different places and time
Utility is the pleasure derived from the consumption of a good or service
The same commodity gives different utilities to different consumers
q.explanation: Utility and usefulness are not synonymous: usefulness is the concern of the product, utility is the concern of the consumer.

q.q: Utility is the power of a commodity to satisfy human wants.
q.explanation: The textbook defines utility exactly as the power of a commodity to satisfy human wants.

q.q: A non-smoker gains no satisfaction from cigarettes while a smoker does. This shows that utility is:
q.explanation: Utility is relative to the needs of each person, so the same commodity gives different utility to different consumers.

q.q: The utility of wearing a jacket is the same during the cold season and the hot season.
q.explanation: The utility of a product differs at different places and times; the jacket satisfies far more in the cold season.

q.q: The approach that measures utility only by ranking bundles as 1st, 2nd and 3rd is called what?
q.explanation: The ordinal approach ranks consumption bundles in order of preference.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why utility and usefulness are not synonymous.
q.answer: usefulness is the concern of the product while utility is the concern of the consumer|utility belongs to the consumer not the product
q.explanation: Usefulness is the concern of a product, whereas utility is the concern of the consumer.

q.q: Tea drunk early in the morning gives different satisfaction from the same tea at lunch time. This illustrates that utility varies:
options: With the size of the cup
With the colour of the tea
q.explanation: The textbook notes that utility from drinking tea early in the morning differs from utility during lunch time.

q.q: Economists try to quantify the qualitative concept of utility in two different ways.
q.explanation: Since utility is qualitative, economists quantify it through cardinal utility and ordinal utility.

q.q: Arrange the chain of a purchase in the logical order, starting with what happens first.
options: The consumer gains utility from it
q.explanation: The order is: the consumer feels a want, chooses the commodity, consumes it, then gains utility.

q.q: Give one reason the same product provides different utility to different individuals.
q.explanation: Utility is subjective to a person's needs, so individuals derive different satisfaction from the same product.

q.q: A product that is useful for everyone gives exactly the same utility to every consumer.
q.explanation: Utility is not absolute; the same commodity provides different utilities to different consumers.

q.q: Marginal utility is defined as:
options: The average utility of all units consumed
The change in total utility from consuming one more unit
Total utility divided by its price
q.explanation: Marginal utility is the additional utility obtained from consuming an additional unit of the commodity.

q.q: Total utility is the sum of all marginal utilities.
q.explanation: TU at n units equals the marginal utilities of the 1st up to the nth unit added together.

q.q: At the saturation point of a commodity, marginal utility is:
q.explanation: MU becomes zero exactly when total utility reaches its maximum.

q.q: In the banana table, total utility reaches its maximum of 37 utils at 7 units of banana.
q.explanation: TU rises to 37 utils at the 7th unit, where MU is zero; after that TU falls.

q.q: Total utility from 2 oranges is 10 utils and rises to 12 utils with a 3rd orange. The marginal utility of the 3rd orange is:
State the law of diminishing marginal utility in one sentence.
q.answer: utility from successive units decreases as consumption increases|each additional unit gives less satisfaction|mu falls as more is consumed
q.explanation: As quantity consumed increases per unit of time, the utility from successive units keeps decreasing, other consumption constant.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT an assumption of the cardinal utility theory?
options: Marginal utility of money is constant
q.explanation: The diminishing marginal rate of substitution belongs to the ordinal approach, not the cardinal assumptions.

q.q: When marginal utility becomes negative, consuming more of the commodity causes total utility to fall.
q.explanation: Beyond the saturation point the 8th and later bananas bring negative additional utility, so TU falls and dissatisfaction results.

q.q: What unit of measurement of satisfaction did the cardinal school suggest?
q.explanation: The cardinal school suggested a subjective unit called the util.

q.q: Explain why total utility increases at a decreasing rate in the banana table.
q.answer: marginal utility diminishes|each extra unit adds less than the previous one
q.explanation: As consumption rises, MU falls with each additional unit, so TU rises more slowly.

q.q: The equation TU = f(X1, X2, ... Xn) means the total utility of a basket depends on the quantities of the individual commodities.
q.explanation: The fifth cardinal assumption expresses total utility as a function of the quantities in the bundle.

q.q: For a single commodity X, the consumer is in equilibrium when:
q.explanation: With one commodity, equilibrium is where the marginal utility of X is equated to its market price.

q.q: If MUx is greater than Px, the consumer can increase his welfare by purchasing more units of X.
q.explanation: When MUx exceeds Px, extra units add more satisfaction than they cost, so the consumer buys more.

q.q: With two or more commodities, utility is maximized when:
options: Quantities of all commodities are equal
The ratios MU/P for all commodities are equal
q.explanation: The condition is the equality of the ratios of the marginal utilities of the commodities to their prices.

q.q: Write the consumer's budget equation for one commodity X bought at price Px with income I.
q.explanation: The expenditure on X, PxQx, equals the consumer's budget in the one-commodity case.

q.q: In Table 1.4, with bread priced at 2 birr, the consumer reaches equilibrium at:
q.explanation: At 2 loaves MU = 2 = price, so MU per birr equals the marginal utility of money.

q.q: Why does the consumer in the bread example stop at the 2nd loaf?
q.answer: mu equals price|beyond 2 loaves mu falls below the price
q.explanation: After 2 loaves, MU (1, 0, -1) is less than the 2 birr price, so further loaves lower welfare.

q.q: At the consumer's equilibrium, expenditure on all goods must add up exactly to the consumer's income.
q.explanation: The budget equation PxQx + PyQy = I holds with equality, as shown by 2(3) + 4(4) = 22.

q.q: An individual with 22 birr buys bread at Px = 2 and injera at Py = 4. The utility-maximizing bundle is:
q.explanation: At 3 bread and 4 injera, MUx/Px = 2/2 = 1 = 4/4 = MUy/Py, and 2(3) + 4(4) = 22 birr.

q.q: The maximum total utility the bread-and-injera consumer receives at equilibrium is:
If MUx/Px is greater than MUy/Py, the consumer gains satisfaction by shifting spending toward commodity Y.
q.explanation: Utility per birr is higher on X, so the consumer should spend more on X and less on Y until the ratios are equal.

q.q: Arrange the steps of solving a two-commodity maximization problem in the correct order.
options: Compare MU/P values so the ratios are equal
List the MU of each unit of both goods
Check the budget equation against income
Divide each MU by its price
q.explanation: List MUs first, then divide each by its price, then equalize the ratios, and finally verify the budget equation.

q.q: When we rank the utility gained from consuming different commodities as 1st, 2nd and 3rd, we are measuring utility:
q.explanation: Ranking bundles in order of preference is the ordinal approach to utility.

q.q: In the ordinal utility approach, different consumption bundles are ranked according to preferences.
q.explanation: Utility cannot be measured absolutely, so bundles are ranked 1st, 2nd, 3rd and so on.

q.q: Which of the following assumptions is common to both the cardinal and ordinal approaches?
options: Measuring the utility of each commodity in numbers
q.explanation: Rationality of the consumer is assumed by both approaches; the other assumptions belong to one approach only.

q.q: What is the term for the rate at which a consumer is willing to substitute one commodity for another so that total satisfaction remains the same?
q.explanation: This rate is called the marginal rate of substitution.

q.q: The marginal rate of substitution diminishes as the consumer consumes more and more of a good.
q.explanation: The diminishing marginal rate of substitution means fewer and fewer units of the other good are given up per additional unit.

q.q: State the transitivity assumption of consumer choice.
q.answer: if a is preferred to b and b is preferred to c then a is preferred to c|if a>b and b>c then a>c
q.explanation: Transitivity: if bundle A is preferred to B and B is preferred to C, then bundle A is preferred to C.

q.q: If bundle A is preferred to bundle B, consistency requires that:
options: B is later preferred to A
The consumer will not choose B over A under the same conditions
A and B give equal utility
B must be cheaper than A
q.explanation: Consistency means the consumer will not reverse the choice between the same two bundles under identical conditions.

q.q: Why does the ordinal approach avoid stating utility in utils?
q.answer: satisfaction cannot be expressed in absolute terms|consumers can only rank preferences relatively
q.explanation: Consumers cannot express utility in absolute terms like 1 util or 2 utils but can express it only in relative, ranked terms.

q.q: The law of diminishing marginal utility is an assumption of ordinal utility theory.
q.explanation: The ordinal theory assumes the diminishing marginal rate of substitution; diminishing marginal utility is a cardinal assumption.

q.q: As a consumer substitutes more and more of commodity Y for commodity X, he will be prepared to give up:
options: More units of X for each additional unit of Y
Fewer units of X for each additional unit of Y
The same units of X each time
q.explanation: The diminishing MRS means each additional unit of Y is obtained by giving up fewer units of X.

q.q: A consumer knows that A > B and B > C. Place the three baskets from most preferred to least preferred.
q.explanation: By transitivity A outranks B, and B outranks C, so the order is A, B, C.

q.q: Demand for a commodity exists only when a person has:
options: money even if unwilling to buy
q.explanation: Demand = willingness to buy + ability to pay; desire alone is not demand.

q.q: A desire for a good without the ability to pay for it is still demand.
q.explanation: Demand requires both willingness to buy and ability to pay.

q.q: Which expression is the demand function as given in the lesson?
q.explanation: The demand function is Qd = f(P) = a - bP, with b the coefficient of price.

q.q: The downward movement along a demand curve caused by a fall in price is called:
q.explanation: A fall in price produces an extension of demand along the fixed curve.

q.q: For complements such as tea and sugar, a fall in the price of one commodity leads to:
options: a fall in the demand for both
a rise in the demand for both
no change in demand for either
a rise for one and a fall for the other
q.explanation: In the case of complementary goods, a fall in the price of one raises the demand for both.

q.q: An increase in consumer income shifts the demand curve of most goods rightward.
q.explanation: Consumer income is directly related to demand, so higher income means greater demand and a rightward shift.

q.q: Which of the following is a shifting factor of demand rather than a cause of movement along the curve?
options: the price of the good itself
the slope of the demand curve
q.explanation: All determinants except the good's own price are shifting factors; income is one of them.

q.q: State the difference between a change in quantity demanded and a change in demand.
q.answer: own price moves along the curve|other factors shift the curve
q.explanation: A change in quantity demanded is movement along the curve caused by own price; a change in demand is a shift caused by other determinants.

q.q: Using Amina's demand function Qd = 9 - 0.2P, when the price is Birr 20 the quantity demanded is:
Arrange the steps for deriving a market demand curve.
options: Join the plotted points to form the market curve
Write the demand schedule of each consumer
Plot the market totals against price
Add the quantities all consumers demand at each price
q.explanation: The order is: write each schedule, add quantities at each price, plot the totals, then join the points.

q.q: The individual demand of a product is QI = 50 - 5P and there are 100 identical buyers. The market demand function is:
Supply refers to the amounts of a product that a producer is:
options: willing and able to produce and sell at given prices
forced to hand over to the government
already storing in a warehouse only
q.explanation: Supply is the amount producers are willing and able to produce and make available for sale at given prices, ceteris paribus.

q.q: The supply curve slopes upward from left to right.
