q.q: In Koppen's classification, the group whose primary criterion is precipitation is:
q.explanation: Group B (dry) has precipitation as its primary criterion, while A, C, D and E are temperature groups and H is altitude.

q.q: Name the German climatologist and botanist (1846-1940) whose classification is the most widely used.
q.explanation: Wladimir Koppen devised the most widely used climate classification scheme.

q.q: Which latitudes belong to the Temperate Zone?
q.explanation: The Temperate Zone extends from 40 to 60 degrees latitude.

q.q: Explain why dense cloud cover in the tropical zone reduces the heating of the ground.
q.answer: clouds reduce the solar radiation reaching the ground|cloud cover blocks part of the incoming radiation
q.explanation: Frequent and dense cloud cover reduces the effect of solar radiation on the ground temperature.

q.q: Arrange the global climate zones from the equator toward the pole.
q.explanation: The sequence outward from the equator is tropical, subtropics, temperate, cold.

q.q: Average temperature is the most important factor in determining climate regions of the world, though precipitation and other weather aspects also play roles.
q.explanation: Average temperature is the most important factor, with other weather aspects like precipitation playing roles.

q.q: Which is NOT among the approximately five major climate types used today?
q.explanation: Today's five major types are tropical, dry, temperate, continental and polar; oceanic is not one of them.

q.q: What angle does the sunlight form with the ground at the equator at noontime?
q.explanation: At the equator the sunlight reaches the ground almost perpendicularly, at about 90 degrees.

q.q: Koppen believed that the best expression of an overall climate is the distribution of:
q.explanation: Koppen held that the distribution of natural vegetation was the best expression of an overall climate.

q.q: Africa is called the most tropical of all continents because:
options: its climate is always hot everywhere
the equator and both tropics run through it
all of it lies south of the equator
q.explanation: The equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn all run through Africa.

q.q: The climate of Africa is more variable in rainfall amount than in temperature.
q.explanation: African temperatures are consistently high, but rainfall amounts vary greatly.

q.q: Name the Libyan station that recorded the highest temperature ever measured in the region and in the world: 58 degrees C.
q.explanation: The record of 58 degrees C was set at Azizia, Libya.

q.q: The harmattan is best described as:
options: a warm, dry, northeasterly wind from the southern Sahara, often laden with sand and dust
the rainy monsoon of East Africa
q.explanation: The harmattan is a warm, dry northeasterly or easterly wind blowing out of the southern Sahara.

q.q: Give two reasons why the western African coast from Cape Three Points in Ghana eastward to Benin receives less than 1,000 mm of rain.
q.answer: cold offshore water chills and stabilises the maritime air|winds blow parallel to the shore|no highlands give orographic rain
q.explanation: Cold offshore water makes the lower maritime air stable, winds tend to blow parallel to the shore, and the absence of highlands deprives the region of orographic rainfall.

q.q: Which current helps keep the western Sahara coast dry but also creates rich fishing grounds?
q.explanation: The cool Canary Current off the western coast of the Sahara causes dry conditions and supports rich fishing grounds off Morocco and the Spanish Saharan coasts.

q.q: Cool ocean currents tend to create rich fishing grounds.
q.explanation: The cool Canary and Benguela currents create rich fishing grounds off Morocco, the Spanish Saharan coasts and the Namibian coast.

q.q: A place has mild wet winters brought by moist westerly winds, dry hot summers and annual rainfall of about 500-750 mm. Its climatic region is:
q.explanation: Mild wet winters under westerlies with 500-750 mm per year define the Mediterranean climate region.

q.q: Name the two deserts that make up the hot desert climatic region of Africa.
q.answer: Sahara and Kalahari|the Sahara and the Kalahari
q.explanation: The hot desert region consists of the Sahara and Kalahari deserts, under dry continental tropical air masses.

q.q: Using the lapse rate, explain why the highest East African peaks carry snow despite lying near the equator.
q.answer: temperature falls about 6.4 degrees C per 1000 m so the peaks are below freezing|altitude lowers temperature below freezing point
q.explanation: Air temperature decreases with altitude at an average rate of 6.4 degrees C per 1000 m, so the very high tops fall below freezing point.

q.q: Arrange these climatic regions in the order they appear moving southward from the equator across southern Africa.
q.explanation: Moving southward the sequence is equatorial, tropical wet-and-dry, hot desert, then the Mediterranean fringes - Africa's mirror-image symmetry about the equator.

q.q: Agriculture's average share of Africa's labour force is about:
q.explanation: Agriculture accounts, on average, for about 70 percent of the labour force and over 25 percent of GDP.

q.q: Agriculture accounts for over what percentage of Africa's Gross Domestic Product?
q.explanation: Agriculture contributes over 25 percent of the GDP.

q.q: The bulk of agricultural systems in Sub-Saharan Africa depend on rains rather than irrigation.
q.explanation: The region is marked by a strong dependence on rain-fed agriculture and natural resources.

q.q: Which pair shows an obvious climate-health link from the lesson?
options: floods cause drownings; drought leads to crop failure and hunger
q.explanation: A flood can cause drownings and a drought can lead to crop failure and hunger; temperature extremes pose a risk of exposure.

q.q: Explain why African agriculture is described as extremely climate-dependent.
q.answer: it relies on rain-fed farming and natural resources|farmers need a steady mixture of sun, warmth and rains
q.explanation: Agriculture has always been deeply dependent on the weather, needing sun, warmth and rains, and Sub-Saharan systems run on rain-fed farming.

q.q: Which example shows a climate-health connection that is difficult to diagnose?
options: the influence of climate on a disease epidemic or a conflict
q.explanation: Some connections are obscured by complex or unobserved processes, such as the influence of climate on a disease epidemic or a conflict.

q.q: Regions of extreme climatic conditions such as deserts and rainforests tend to have fewer people than places with better climates.
q.explanation: Some places are overpopulated due to better climate, while extreme regions like deserts and rainforests have fewer people.

q.q: Explain why persistent climate change may reduce Africa's surface-water supplies.
q.answer: stream levels, river flow and underground water depend on climate, so changed rains shrink the supply|less or more variable rainfall lowers river flow and recharge
q.explanation: The level and flow of streams and the volume of underground water depend on climate types and water availability, so persistent change may shrink surface-water supply and the regularity of streams and rivers.

q.q: The two reasons Africa is among the continents most highly affected by climate change are its spread across the warming tropics and its:
options: limited human, social and economic capacity to adapt
q.explanation: Africa is most affected because its land lies across the warming tropics and its countries have limited capacity to adapt.

q.q: Arrange the chain of events that links a late rainy season to a lost harvest.
q.explanation: Late rains first delay planting, the growing season then shortens, and the harvest finally falls short.

q.q: Climate variability differs from climate change because variability:
options: may arise from natural internal processes of the climate system and occurs with or without human action
q.explanation: Variability may be due to natural internal processes or anthropogenic external forcing, and climate variations occur with or without our actions.

q.q: Climate change is a change in the state of the climate system that persists for an extended period, typically decades or longer, due to natural and/or anthropogenic processes and drivers.
q.explanation: This is the textbook definition of climate change.

q.q: Which international panel assesses climate change and reported the drivers of Africa's vulnerability?
q.explanation: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) reported the factors driving Africa's vulnerability.

q.q: According to the IPCC, the drivers of Africa's vulnerability to climate change include:
options: weak adaptive capacity, high dependence on ecosystem goods for livelihoods, and less developed agricultural production systems
q.explanation: The IPCC lists weak adaptive capacity, high dependence on ecosystem goods for livelihoods, and less developed agricultural production systems.

q.q: List four signs that climate change is already happening in Africa.
q.answer: higher temperatures, drying soils, pests and diseases, shifting crop and livestock zones, desertification, floods, deforestation, erosion|drying soils and shifting growing areas among others
q.explanation: Higher temperatures, drying up of soils, increased pest and disease, shifts in suitable areas for crops and livestock, desertification, floods, deforestation and erosion are all signs.

q.q: The two most extensive land-based end-of-century projected decreases in rainfall anywhere on the planet occur over:
q.explanation: The largest projected land-based decreases fall over Africa, particularly in North and South Africa.

q.q: For the world's poorest people, adaptation to climate change is a matter of sheer survival.
q.explanation: Poor people live on the frontlines of pollution, disaster and degradation, so for them adaptation is a matter of sheer survival.

q.q: Climate change will strongly affect Africa's ability to achieve:
options: the Millennium Development Goals and the Africa 2063 goal
q.explanation: Climate change affects Africa's path to the MDGs and the Africa 2063 goal, with added pressure on agriculture, water, health and political stability.

q.q: Explain why hundreds of millions of Africans depend directly on the climate system.
q.answer: they depend on rainfall to grow their food|African society is closely coupled with the climate system through rain-fed farming
q.explanation: African society is very closely coupled with the climate system because hundreds of millions depend on rainfall to grow their food.

q.q: What does the lack of reliable economic figures about climate change in Africa imply?
q.answer: the costs are real but hard to quantify, so the threat is easily under-appreciated|no exact and reliable figures exist for individuals or society
q.explanation: Despite growing concern, no exact and reliable figures are available to quantify the economic costs of the negative impacts for individuals or society as a whole.

q.q: Arrange the chain linking climate change to Africa's development, from cause to final effect.
options: Food insecurity and water stress build up
Higher temperatures and shifting rainfall arrive
Pressure on the MDGs and Africa 2063 grows
q.explanation: Higher temperatures and shifted rainfall first cut rain-fed harvests, then food insecurity and water stress build, and finally pressure on the MDGs and Africa 2063 grows.

q.q: Which of the following is an example of a nonrenewable natural resource?
q.explanation: Fossil fuels like petroleum and coal exist in fixed amounts and are nonrenewable.

q.q: About what percent of all water on Earth is fresh?
q.explanation: Only about 2.5% of Earth's total water is freshwater; 96.5% is ocean water.

q.q: People do not make natural resources; they gather them.
q.explanation: The textbook states that people do not make natural resources, they gather them.

q.q: What share of the world's freshwater is held by glaciers and permanent snow?
q.explanation: Glaciers and permanent snow hold 68.7% of freshwater, the largest freshwater store.

q.q: Name the process by which soil takes nitrogen from the air and converts it into basic ingredients that let plants make their own food.
q.explanation: Soil is an agent of the nitrogen cycle.

q.q: Distinguish between consumptive use and public-good services provided by natural resources.
q.answer: consumptive use reduces supply, like mining and logging; public good benefits many people whether or not they paid
q.explanation: Consumptive use is use that reduces supply; a public good benefits many whether or not they paid.

q.q: Sustainable use means people should completely stop using natural resources.
q.explanation: Sustainable use means using resources at a rate that does not degrade the environment, not ending use.

q.q: The general estimate for how long remaining oil reserves may last is:
q.explanation: The general estimate is that remaining oil reserves will last possibly the next few decades.

q.q: Which is NOT a key strategy of sustainable natural resource management?
options: Degrading the marine and coastal environment
q.explanation: Protecting, not degrading, the marine and coastal environment is a key NRM strategy.

q.q: Identify the largest store of the Earth's freshwater and the proportion of freshwater it holds.
q.explanation: Glaciers and permanent snow hold 68.7% of freshwater, more than groundwater's 30.1%.

q.q: Arrange these water stores from the largest share of total water to the smallest: oceans, glaciers and permanent snow, rivers.
q.explanation: Oceans hold 96.5%, glaciers and permanent snow 1.74%, and rivers only 0.0002% of total water.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT among the Nile basin countries?
q.explanation: Chad belongs to the Chad basin, not the Nile basin.

q.q: About what percent of the Nile's water comes from Ethiopia?
q.explanation: Eighty-six percent of Nile water comes from Ethiopia, mainly through the Baro, Abbay and Tekeze.

q.q: The largest swamp interrupting the course of the Nile's headstreams in South Sudan is:
q.explanation: The Sudd is the largest of the swamps interrupting the river's course.

q.q: The Congo River is second only to the Amazon in volume of water.
q.explanation: The Congo is the Earth's second-largest river by volume, next to the Amazon.

q.q: The Niger River rises in the:
q.explanation: The Niger rises in the Futa Jalon highlands of Guinea.

q.q: Name the largest hydroelectric dam project on the Niger River.
q.explanation: The Kainji Dam in Nigeria was completed in the late 1960s.

q.q: The two main tributaries that join the Zambezi on its left bank downstream from Kariba are the:
q.explanation: The Kafue and the Luangwa are the two main left-bank tributaries of the Zambezi.

q.q: Navigation is impossible throughout the Orange River's course.
q.explanation: Irregular flow, constant falls and rapids, and silting make navigation impossible.

q.q: Explain how a watershed differs from a drainage basin.
q.answer: a watershed is the divide separating one drainage area from another, while a drainage basin is the whole area drained
q.explanation: The watershed is the boundary divide; the drainage basin is the area within that boundary.

q.q: State the mean depth of Lake Chad in meters.
q.explanation: Lake Chad is a shallow lake with a mean depth of 1.2 meters.

q.q: Explain why the Congo River keeps a stable flow all year.
q.answer: its basin lies above and below the equator, so at least one part always has a rainy season
q.explanation: Because large sections of the basin lie on both sides of the Equator, at least one section always experiences a rainy season.

q.q: The dominant soil type in Africa, covering 22% of the continent's soils, is:
q.explanation: Arenosols are the dominant soil in Africa, covering 22% of its soils.

q.q: Leptosols occur mainly in:
options: mountainous and desert regions where hard rock is exposed
lava fields of the Rift Valley
q.explanation: Leptosols occur especially in mountainous and desert regions where hard rock is exposed or near the surface.

q.q: Ferralsols are strongly leached soils dominated by aluminum oxides, iron oxides and kaolinite.
q.explanation: After losing nearly all weatherable minerals, ferralsols are dominated by aluminum oxides, iron oxides and kaolinite.

q.q: The soil type in which precipitated calcium carbonate can form a hard calcrete pan impenetrable to plant roots is:
q.explanation: In calcisols, precipitated calcium carbonate cements the soil into a calcrete hard pan.

q.q: What name is given to the material below the 1-2 m depth where soil-forming processes end?
q.explanation: The material below this depth is known as the soil parent material.

q.q: Africa's largest petroleum producer is:
q.explanation: The continent's largest petroleum producer is the West African country Nigeria.

q.q: South Africa holds more than 90% of the world's platinum reserves.
q.explanation: South Africa holds 91.3% of world platinum reserves, ranking first.

q.q: Which pair of countries produces most of the world's cobalt?
options: The Democratic Republic of Congo and Zambia
q.explanation: The DRC and Zambia produce more than half of the world's cobalt and much of its copper.

q.q: Why were colonial railroads in Africa built, and why did this harm later development?
q.answer: to carry minerals to coastal ports rather than link cities and industries
q.explanation: Railroads were built to move minerals to ports for export, not to connect populations or industries.

q.q: Arrange the major soil types from the largest share of African soils to the smallest: arenosols, leptosols, ferralsols, calcisols.
q.explanation: The order is arenosols (22%), leptosols (17%), ferralsols (10%), calcisols (6%).

q.q: Name the mineral for which Ethiopia ranked sixth in world production in 2019.
q.explanation: Ethiopia ranks sixth in world tantalum production.

q.q: The natural vegetation type that covers the largest surface area of Africa is:
q.explanation: Tropical desert covers 8,737,674 km2, about 29.3% of the continent.

q.q: Annual rainfall in the tropical rainforest ranges from:
q.explanation: Rainforest rainfall ranges from 1,000 to more than 2,000 mm per year due to the permanent ITCZ.

q.q: Somalia is dry despite lying across the Equator because the trade winds blow parallel to the coast and the winter monsoon crosses large continents.
q.explanation: These phenomena make Somalia semi-arid with 400-750 mm of annual rainfall.

q.q: Above 3,000 m in tropical African mountains, the vegetation consists of:
q.explanation: Above 3,000 m the Ericaceous belt is followed by Afro-alpine shrublands and grasslands.

q.q: The Atlas Mountains reach their maximum altitude in:
q.explanation: The Atlas altitude reaches 4,165 m in Morocco.

q.q: What is the biological name for vegetation?
q.explanation: Biologically, vegetation is known as flora.

q.q: Name the four factors that affect the distribution and composition of plant communities.
q.answer: climate, landform, soils and biotic factors
q.explanation: Climate, landform, soils and biotic factors control vegetation distribution.

q.q: Africa's largest antelope is the:
q.explanation: The eland is the largest antelope named in the lesson.

q.q: The aardvark is endemic to Africa and feeds mainly on termites.
q.explanation: The aardvark rips open termite nests and laps up the insects inside.

q.q: Which reptiles live only on Madagascar?
q.explanation: Boa constrictors and iguanas live only on Madagascar.

q.q: Explain why the vegetation map of a region looks very similar to its climate map.
q.answer: climate, especially temperature and precipitation, controls the distribution of plants
q.explanation: Climatic elements are critical to vegetation distribution, so the two maps resemble each other.

q.q: The human population entered the twentieth century with a size of about:
q.explanation: The textbook states that humanity entered the twentieth century with 1.6 billion people.

q.q: About how many people were added to the world population between 1960 and 1975?
q.explanation: A billion people were added between 1960 and 1975, and another billion between 1975 and 1987.

q.q: Asia is the most populous continent and Oceania is the least populated continent.
q.explanation: Asia holds 59.4% of humanity while Oceania has only about 43 million people.

q.q: By mid-2020, Africa's share of the world population was about:
q.explanation: Africa had more than 1.3 billion people, about 17.5% of the world total.

q.q: Population doubling time depends mainly on the total size of the population rather than on its growth rate.
q.explanation: Doubling time is computed as 70 divided by the growth rate; it does not depend on population size.

q.q: Write the Rule of 70 used to compute population doubling time.
q.answer: dt = 70/r|70 divided by the growth rate
q.explanation: Doubling time equals 70 divided by the population growth rate.

q.q: Using the Rule of 70, a country growing at 2.5 percent per year doubles its size in about:
q.explanation: 70 divided by 2.5 equals 28 years, as in the Ethiopia example.

q.q: An area starts the year with 2,000,000 people, records 50,000 births, 30,000 deaths, 10,000 in-migrants and 25,000 out-migrants. Its end-of-year population is:
q.explanation: Natural increase is 20,000 and net migration is -15,000, so the population rises by 5,000 to 2,005,000.

q.q: The rate of natural increase in Sub-Saharan Africa is reputed to be about:
q.explanation: Sub-Saharan Africa has the world's highest rate of natural increase, about 3% per year.

q.q: Explain why the world population is still growing although fertility has declined.
q.answer: mortality fell faster than fertility|death rates declined faster|life expectancy rose
q.explanation: Fertility has fallen from 4.5 to below 2.5 children per woman, but mortality has not fallen at the same pace, so births still exceed deaths.

q.q: There has been more population growth since 1950 than in all previous years of human existence.
q.explanation: The textbook states that more population growth has occurred since 1950 than in the previous years of human existence.

q.q: Total fertility rate is best defined as:
options: the average number of children a woman would bear during her lifetime
the number of births per 1000 population in a year
the number of infant deaths per 1000 live births
the average number of years a newborn can expect to live
q.explanation: TFR is the average number of children a woman would bear if she experienced present-day age-specific fertility rates.

q.q: Africa's crude birth rate of 33/1000 in mid-2020 means that:
options: 33 births occurred per 1000 people on average during the year
33 women gave birth during the year
q.explanation: CBR expresses annual live births per 1000 of the mid-year total population.

q.q: Southern Africa has the lowest total fertility rate among Africa's major regions.
q.explanation: Southern Africa's TFR stood at 2.4 in 2020, the lowest, ahead of Northern Africa.

q.q: Which country had the highest crude birth rate in Africa in 2020?
q.explanation: Somalia's CBR was 49/1000, the continent's highest, while Mauritius was lowest at 11/1000.

q.q: Which African region had the highest infant mortality rate in 2020?
q.explanation: Central Africa led with 62 infant deaths per 1000 live births.

q.q: A country recorded 1,600,000 live births and a mid-year population of 40,000,000. Its crude birth rate is:
q.explanation: CBR = 1,600,000 / 40,000,000 x 1000 = 40 births per 1000 population.

q.q: Infant mortality rate counts infant deaths per 1000 of the total population.
q.explanation: IMR counts infant deaths per 1000 live births, not per 1000 total population.

q.q: State two reasons why fertility remains high in Africa.
q.answer: less access to contraceptives|poverty|low status of women|children needed for labor|low education|traditions and culture|early marriage
q.explanation: Causes include less access to contraceptives, poverty, low status of women, high child labor needs, low education and traditional values.

q.q: Africa's crude death rate by mid-2020 was about:
q.explanation: The crude death rate fell from 14 per 1000 in 2007 to 8 per 1000 by mid-2020.

q.q: By 2050, Africa's population is projected to reach about:
q.explanation: Projections put Africa at about 2.5 billion people by 2050, 25% of the world total.

q.q: Why is the infant mortality rate called the most widely used indicator of a country's general health situation?
q.answer: it reflects health services|it reflects sanitation|it reflects nutrition and living conditions
q.explanation: IMR summarizes the quality of health care, sanitation and living standards affecting the most vulnerable group, infants.

q.q: Africa's median age by mid-2020 was about:
q.explanation: Africa's median age was 19.7 years, indicating a very young population.

q.q: Africa's population is dominated by the old age group.
q.explanation: Only about 3% of Africans are 65 or older; young people dominate the structure.

q.q: Which African region has the highest age dependency ratio?
q.explanation: Central Africa's ADR is 96.1, the continent's highest, with 46% of its people under 15.

q.q: A constructive population pyramid usually displays:
options: under 30% aged 1-14 and over 6% aged 75 and above
a very broad base and tapering apex
high birth rates with short life expectancy
q.explanation: The constructive pyramid shows an aging population typical of developed countries with adequate health services.

q.q: A country has 3.6 million males and 4.0 million females. Find its sex ratio.
q.explanation: Sex ratio = 3.6 / 4.0 x 100 = 90 males per 100 females.

q.q: If 42% of a population is aged 0-14, 53% is aged 15-64 and 5% is 65+, the age dependency ratio is about:
q.explanation: ADR = (42 + 5) / 53 x 100 = about 88.7 dependents per 100 workers.

q.q: What does an expansive population pyramid indicate about a country?
q.answer: high birth rate|high death rate|short life expectancy|rapid growth|less developed
q.explanation: An expansive pyramid shows high birth and death rates, rapid growth and short life expectancy, typical of less developed countries.

q.q: In a population pyramid, the bars for females are drawn on the right of the central vertical axis.
q.explanation: Males are on the left of the axis and females on the right.

q.q: Explain how a predominantly young age structure affects African economies.
q.answer: increases demand for education|health|food|housing|jobs|pressure on scarce resources
q.explanation: High fertility sustains pressure on scarce resources and demand for food, education, health, housing and employment, so growth dwarfs economic achievement.

q.q: A stationary population pyramid occurs when:
options: births equal deaths and the growth rate is zero
q.explanation: The stationary type shows unchanging fertility and mortality, where B = D and population growth is zero.

q.q: Give Europe's median age by mid-2020 as stated in the lesson.
q.explanation: Europe's median age was 42.5 years, far above Africa's 19.7.

q.q: Africa's average crude population density in mid-2019 was about:
q.explanation: The continent's average crude density was about 44 people per km2 in mid-2019.

q.q: The vast Sahara has few permanent residents.
q.explanation: Some parts of the continent, particularly the vast Sahara, have few permanent residents.

q.q: Which pair of regions share the continent's highest crude density of 65 persons/km2?
q.explanation: Both Eastern and Western Africa have the continent's highest crude density of 65 persons/km2.

q.q: Which of the following is a physical factor of population distribution?
q.explanation: Climate is a physical factor; economic and political situations are human factors.

q.q: A region has 50 million people on 1,000,000 km2 of land. Compute its crude population density.
q.explanation: Density = 50,000,000 / 1,000,000 = 50 persons per km2.

q.q: Explain why being populous does not necessarily mean being densely populated.
q.answer: density depends on area|a large country spreads people over a big area|density is population divided by area
q.explanation: Density depends on both numbers and land area; large countries like Nigeria and DRC have many people but lower average densities than small countries like Mauritius.

q.q: Compared with Southern Africa at 25 persons/km2, Eastern Africa at 65 persons/km2 is about:
q.explanation: 65 divided by 25 is about 2.6.

q.q: Crude population density is calculated as total population divided by total land area in square kilometres.
q.explanation: Crude density divides the total population by the total area, giving persons per km2.

q.q: State two causes of the uneven distribution of Africa's population.
q.answer: climate|relief|availability of water|soil fertility|distribution of minerals|economic conditions|political situations
q.explanation: Physical factors include climate, relief, water, soil fertility and minerals; human factors include economic conditions and political situations.

q.q: Which region has Africa's lowest crude population density?
q.explanation: Southern Africa is lowest at 25 persons/km2, behind Central Africa at 27 and Northern Africa at 31.

q.q: Name the most populous country in Africa.
q.explanation: Nigeria heads the list of Africa's most populous countries, followed by Ethiopia, Egypt, DRC and South Africa.

q.q: Which country is the least urbanized in Africa?
q.explanation: Burundi is the least urbanized country, with only 12% of its people in urban areas.

q.q: The most urbanized region of Africa is:
q.explanation: Southern Africa leads with 62% urban, while Eastern Africa is least at 26%.

q.q: Gabon has almost 90% of its population living in urban areas.
q.explanation: The textbook states Gabon's urban population is almost 90%.

q.q: About what share of Africa's population currently lives in urban areas?
q.explanation: The urban population is currently about 41% of the total and is projected to keep rising.

q.q: Name three African countries that are still predominantly rural.
q.explanation: Burundi, Rwanda, Malawi, Ethiopia and Burkina Faso are still predominantly rural.

q.q: Why does rapid urban growth strain African development?
q.answer: migrants need land|infrastructure|basic services|health care stretched
q.explanation: Migrants into cities require access to land, infrastructure and basic services, and this stretches health care services.

q.q: Which country appears in the bottom 10 for urbanization?
q.explanation: Ethiopia is among the bottom 10, together with Kenya, Eritrea, Chad, Niger, Swaziland, Uganda, South Sudan, Malawi and Burundi.

q.q: Uncontrolled rapid urbanization has depopulated rural areas and crippled agricultural production, especially food crops.
q.explanation: The unit summary states that uncontrolled rapid urbanization depopulated rural areas and crippled food crop production.

q.q: Explain how rapid urban growth can deepen poverty in both rural and urban areas.
q.answer: rural depopulation cuts farm labor and output|urban services stretched and slums grow|poverty rises in both places
q.explanation: Rural areas lose people and food production suffers, while cities cannot absorb migrants, so poverty grows in both rural and urban areas.

q.q: A region has 40 million people and 62% of them live in urban areas. Its urban population is:
q.explanation: 40 million x 62 / 100 = 24.8 million urban dwellers.

q.q: Arrange the chain of effects of rapid urban growth in the correct order.
options: Cities grow rapidly and services are strained
Rural poverty pushes people to move to towns
Rural areas lose people and food production falls
Migrants need land, infrastructure and basic services
q.explanation: Correct order: rural poverty pushes people to move, migrants need land and services, cities grow and services strain, then rural areas lose people and farming suffers.

q.q: Which sector is based on knowledge and includes ICT and research and development?
q.explanation: The quaternary sector is knowledge-based and includes ICT, research and development and financial planning.

q.q: Developed countries have most of their workers in the:
q.explanation: Developed countries have more people working in the tertiary sector.

q.q: The quaternary sector is included in the standard assessment of the economies of countries.
q.explanation: The quaternary sector is newly emerging and is not included in the assessment of economies.

q.q: Developing countries have more people engaged in the primary sector, particularly in agriculture.
q.explanation: The textbook states that developing countries concentrate workers in the primary sector, especially agriculture.

q.q: Which sector is also called 'manufacturing'?
q.explanation: The secondary sector changes raw materials into finished products, so it is called manufacturing.

q.q: Developing countries (DVCs) are home to about how much of the world's population?
q.explanation: More than 60 percent of the world's population lives in developing countries.

q.q: State the GNI per capita range for lower middle-income economies in 2021.
q.explanation: Lower middle-income economies had a GNI per capita between $1,036 and $4,045 in 2021.

q.q: Which set of countries dominates the low-income group in 2020?
options: Afghanistan, Bangladesh and sub-Saharan African nations
q.explanation: The low-income group is dominated by Afghanistan, Bangladesh and the sub-Saharan African nations.

q.q: Name the two former DVCs that became high-income countries.
q.answer: South Korea and Singapore|South Korea, Singapore
q.explanation: South Korea and Singapore achieved impressive success and became high-income countries.

q.q: What does the employment structure of a country show?
q.answer: how the labor force is divided among sectors|division of labor force between primary secondary and tertiary
q.explanation: Employment structure shows how the labor force is divided between primary, secondary and tertiary activities.

q.q: Arrange the sectors from raw material extraction to knowledge-based work.
q.explanation: The order is primary, secondary, tertiary, then quaternary.

q.q: By far the single most important economic activity in Africa is:
q.explanation: Agriculture is by far the single most important economic activity in Africa.

q.q: Agriculture provides employment for about what share of Africa's working population?
q.explanation: Agriculture employs about two-thirds of the continent's working population.

q.q: Which of the following cannot be included under tertiary activity?
q.explanation: A tannery processes raw hides into leather, so it belongs to the secondary sector.

q.q: Africa's forests comprise 15.6 percent of the world's forest cover.
q.explanation: Africa has 624 million hectares under forests, 20.6 percent of its land area and 15.6 percent of the world's forest cover.

q.q: The transformation of copper ore into electric cable is an example of which sector, and why?
q.explanation: Processing a raw material into a new product is the secondary sector, or manufacturing.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT a factor hindering Africa's economic growth listed in the textbook?
q.explanation: The listed factors are limited technology, aid dependence, poor economic structures and poor education; manufacturing investment is too low, not excessive.

q.q: Over-relying on foreign aid leads to the stagnation of the economy of a country.
q.explanation: The textbook states that over-relying on foreign aid leads to economic stagnation.

q.q: Name two raw materials that African countries still export in their raw forms.
q.answer: cocoa, diamond, gold, bauxite|cocoa and gold|diamond and bauxite
q.explanation: African countries export raw materials including cocoa, diamond, gold and bauxite.

q.q: Working poverty in Africa refers to people who are employed but earning less than:
q.explanation: Working poverty means being employed but earning less than US$2 a day.

q.q: Explain two ways youth unemployment harms African societies.
q.answer: cycles of poverty and weak social cohesion|crime and violence|dangerous migration
q.explanation: Youth exclusion from the labor force continues generational poverty, breaks social cohesion, is linked to crime and violence, and pushes youth onto dangerous migration routes.

q.q: Africa is not keeping up with worldwide improvements in the manufacturing industry.
q.explanation: Although the secondary sector is growing rapidly, Africa is not keeping up with worldwide manufacturing improvements.

q.q: A person who quits a job because he has just started his own small business is an example of:
q.explanation: Voluntary unemployment occurs when a person is jobless by choice rather than from a lack of opportunities.

q.q: University graduates who are willing to work but cannot find jobs are involuntarily unemployed.
q.explanation: Involuntary unemployment is being willing and able to work for a given wage but unable to find a job.

q.q: What is the usual measure of unemployment?
q.explanation: Unemployment is usually measured by the unemployment rate.

q.q: Define unemployment in one sentence.
q.answer: employable and actively seeking a job but unable to find one|people actively seeking work who cannot find a job
q.explanation: Unemployment refers to individuals who are employable and actively seeking a job but are unable to find a job.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT an effect of unemployment described in the lesson?
options: Reduced demand for goods and services
q.explanation: Governments lose tax income during unemployment, so they reduce budgets and workforces.

q.q: Arrange the effects of unemployment in the order given in the lesson.
options: Reduced demand for goods and services
q.explanation: The order is financial hardship, reduced demand, lower profits, then businesses disappear and government cuts.

q.q: The definition of sustainable development that meets present needs without compromising future generations comes from the:
q.explanation: The Brundtland Commission Report (1987) gave this definition of sustainable development.

q.q: Name the four dimensions of sustainable development.
q.answer: society, environment, culture and economy|society environment culture economy
q.explanation: The four dimensions are society, environment, culture and economy, and they are intertwined.

q.q: Sustainable development leads to sustainable employment.
q.explanation: The textbook concludes that sustainable development leads to sustainable employment.

q.q: Why should children be encouraged to broaden their career choices beyond doctor or pilot?
q.answer: everyone cannot be a doctor or pilot|diverse economy
q.explanation: Not everyone can enter those professions; broadened choices let people innovate in different fields and diversify the economy.

q.q: A region has 20,000 unemployed people in a workforce of 200,000. Its unemployment rate is:
Agenda 2063 is a plan covering how many years?
q.explanation: Agenda 2063 is a 50-year plan from 2013 to 2063.

q.q: The Organization of African Unity was the predecessor of the African Union.
q.explanation: The OAU, predecessor of the AU, focused on the struggle against apartheid and political independence.

q.q: Agenda 2063 refocused Africa's agenda away from the old focus on:
q.explanation: The agenda moved beyond the struggle against apartheid and the attainment of political independence.

q.q: What does the acronym AfCFTA stand for?
q.explanation: AfCFTA is the African Continental Free Trade Area, a flagship program of Agenda 2063.

q.q: Which flagship program of Agenda 2063 has already missed its target year?
q.explanation: Silencing the guns carried a target year of 2020, which has passed.

q.q: Name the flagship program that plans a major hydropower project on the Congo River.
q.answer: Grand Inga Dam|Grand Inga Dam project
q.explanation: The Grand Inga Dam project is one of the Agenda 2063 flagship programs.

q.q: SAATM stands for:
options: Sahel Action and Aid Trust Mission
q.explanation: SAATM is the Single African Air Transport Market.

q.q: Mention two changing global contexts that made a long-term plan for Africa necessary.
q.answer: increased globalization and the ICT revolution|globalization|ICT revolution
q.explanation: The textbook cites increased globalization and the ICT revolution as changing global contexts.

q.q: Arrange these milestones from earliest to latest.
q.explanation: The order is OAU independence focus, AU creation, Agenda 2063 launch in 2013, and the 2020 target year passing.

q.q: Quote the key phrase describing Africa's desired future image under the Pan African Vision.
q.answer: an integrated, prosperous and peaceful Africa|integrated prosperous and peaceful Africa
q.explanation: The Pan African Vision is an integrated, prosperous and peaceful Africa, driven by its citizens.

q.q: Agenda 2063 gives priority to gender equality and youth empowerment.
q.explanation: Gender equality and youth empowerment are among the initiatives behind the need for the long-term plan.

q.q: The Sustainable Development Goals are a collection of how many interlinked global goals?
q.explanation: The SDGs are a collection of 17 interlinked global goals.

q.q: In which year were the SDGs set up, and by which body?
q.answer: 2015 by the United Nations General Assembly|UN General Assembly 2015|2015 UN
q.explanation: The SDGs were set up in 2015 by the United Nations General Assembly.

q.q: The SDGs are intended to be achieved by the year 2030.
q.explanation: The SDGs are intended to be achieved by the year 2030.

q.q: The UN Resolution containing the SDGs is called:
q.explanation: The SDGs are included in a UN Resolution called Agenda 2030.

q.q: Which earlier global framework did the SDGs succeed, and when did it end?
q.answer: MDGs in 2015|Millennium Development Goals which ended in 2015
q.explanation: The SDGs succeeded the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs), which ended in 2015.

q.q: People earning less than US$1.90 a day, lacking food, clean water and sanitation, are the target of which SDG?
q.explanation: Goal 1 targets the absolute poor earning less than US$1.90 a day.

q.q: The statement that ending discrimination against women and girls is a basic human right belongs to which SDG?
q.explanation: This statement belongs to Goal 5, Gender equality.

q.q: According to the lesson, income inequality is lowest in which region and highest in which region?
options: Lowest in Africa, highest in Asia
Lowest in Europe, highest in the Middle East
Lowest in Asia, highest in Europe
Lowest in the Americas, highest in Africa
q.explanation: Income inequality is lowest in Europe and highest in the Middle East.

q.q: Give one similarity and one difference between Agenda 2063 and Agenda 2030.
q.answer: both aim at prosperity and sustainability; 2063 is continental and longer while 2030 is global and ends earlier|similar aims different scope and time
q.explanation: Both pursue prosperity, equality and peace, but Agenda 2063 is Africa's 50-year plan while Agenda 2030 is the UN's global framework ending in 2030.

q.q: The SDGs were developed as the future global framework to succeed the MDGs.
q.explanation: The SDGs were developed in the Post-2015 Development Agenda to succeed the MDGs.

q.q: Which SDG responds to economies dependent on fossil fuels that are creating drastic changes to climate?
q.explanation: Goal 7 calls for investing in solar, wind and thermal power instead of fossil fuels.

q.q: Africa is home to what fraction of the world's 6,000 languages?
q.explanation: Africa hosts one-third of the world's 6,000 languages.

q.q: Africa is the most linguistically diverse continent in the world.
q.explanation: With one-third of the world's languages and less than one-seventh of its population, Africa is the most linguistically diverse continent.

q.q: How many living languages are there in Africa?
q.explanation: There are more than 2,000 living languages in Africa.

q.q: Which African country has the largest number of major languages in the textbook table?
q.explanation: Nigeria has 514 languages, the most of the 22 listed countries.

q.q: How many major languages are spoken in Ethiopia according to the table?
q.explanation: Ethiopia has 86 major languages, ranking 6th of the 22 listed countries.

q.q: Define a living language.
q.answer: still spoken today with at least one first-language speaker|a language currently in use with at least one native speaker
q.explanation: A living language is still spoken now and must have at least one speaker whose first language it is.

q.q: The Religious Diversity Index runs on a scale from:
q.explanation: The RDI is on a scale from 0 to 10, with 10 the maximum possible diversity.

q.q: State the RDI score range that counts as 'very high' religious diversity.
q.explanation: Very high diversity means a score of 7.0 and higher.

q.q: Name the two African countries that score 7.5 on the RDI.
q.explanation: Guinea Bissau and Togo each score 7.5 on the Religious Diversity Index.

q.q: Africa contains a mixture of both local beliefs and global beliefs.
q.explanation: Africa is home to many religions and contains a mixture of local and global beliefs.

q.q: In today's Africa, individuals adhere mostly to:
options: Christianity, Islam and traditional African beliefs
q.explanation: Most Africans adhere to Christianity, Islam and traditional African beliefs (folk religions).

q.q: Population change is best defined as:
options: the increase in the number of individuals in a population
the difference in the size of the population from the beginning to the end of a certain period
the number of births in a country per year
the number of people moving across borders
q.explanation: Population change is the difference in population size from the beginning to the end of a period.

q.q: Mortality and emigration decrease the number of individuals in a population.
q.explanation: Deaths (mortality) and out-migration (emigration) decrease a population, while fertility and immigration increase it.

q.q: Which combination caused the stagnation of sub-Saharan Africa's population between 1500 and 1900?
options: Slave trade, colonization and the spread of deadly diseases
q.explanation: The textbook names slave trade, colonization and deadly diseases as the causes of the stagnation.

q.q: By how many people did Africa's population grow between 1500 A.D. and 1900 A.D.?
q.explanation: It grew from 80 million to 100 million, an increase of only 20 million people.

q.q: Between 1980 and 2015, which sub-region of Africa had the highest average annual population growth rate?
q.explanation: Central Africa grew fastest at 3.0 percent per year, followed by Eastern Africa at 2.9 and Western Africa at 2.7 percent.

q.q: Explain why cities are said to couple rapid population growth with heavy demands on services.
q.answer: growing numbers of children need schooling and health care|young people need education and employment
q.explanation: Rapidly growing countries must provide schooling and health care to growing numbers of children and jobs for more youth.

q.q: Which of the following correctly compares the continents in 2021?
options: Africa is the most populous continent with 4.68 billion people
Asia is the most populous continent with 59.5 percent of humanity
Oceania is the second least populated continent
Europe holds 17.2 percent of the world population
q.explanation: Asia leads with 4.68 billion people (59.5 percent); Africa is second, and Oceania is the least populated.

q.q: Asia and Africa are the only continents that have crossed the one-billion-people milestone.
q.explanation: Only Asia (4.68 billion) and Africa (1.37 billion) have crossed one billion, together sharing about 77 percent of the global population.

q.q: What was the estimated population of sub-Saharan Africa by mid-2015?
q.explanation: By mid-2015 sub-Saharan Africa held about 962 million people, roughly ten times its 1900 level.

q.q: The high growth of the world population over past centuries is largely the result of:
options: advances in modern medicines and improved living standards
an increase in earthquakes and tsunamis
q.explanation: Modern medicines and better living standards cut infant, child and maternal mortality and raised life expectancy.

q.q: If a country's population grows at 2.45 percent per year, its doubling time is closest to:
q.explanation: Doubling time = 70 / 2.45 = about 29 years.

q.q: Environment is best defined as:
options: the surroundings or conditions in which persons, animals or plants live or operate
only the plants and animals of a place
the number of people in a region
q.explanation: The textbook defines environment as the surroundings or conditions in which persons, animals or plants live or operate.

q.q: The relationship between human beings and the environment is two-way or reciprocal.
q.explanation: Human beings and the environment affect each other in a reciprocal direction.

q.q: Which statement describes environmental determinism?
options: People choose from many possible responses
The physical environment essentially dictates culture and controls human activities
Humans never depend on the environment
q.explanation: Determinism asserts that the natural or physical environment shapes cultures and controls human activities.

q.q: In which decade was environmental determinism rejected and substituted by environmental possibilism?
q.explanation: The view that human activities are governed by the environment was rejected in the 1950s.

q.q: According to possibilism, what happens to the influence of the natural environment as modernization and technological advancement increase?
q.explanation: The degree of influence of the natural environment declines with increasing modernization and technological advancement.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three types of human-environment interaction listed in the lesson?
q.explanation: The three types are dependence, modification and adaptation; determinism is a theory, not a type.

q.q: Reforestation is an example of a green (ecosystem-based) adaptation measure that can stop desertification and recharge groundwater.
q.explanation: Green measures give nature-based solutions; reforestation stops desertification and recharges groundwater supplies in times of drought.

q.q: Name the two raw materials the environment provides for the manufacture of clothing products.
q.explanation: The environment supplies silk and cotton, used in making clothing.

q.q: List the ecosystem services the environment provides indirectly to economic activities.
q.answer: carbon sequestration|water purification|managing flood risks|nutrient cycling
q.explanation: Ecosystem services include carbon sequestration, water purification, managing flood risks and nutrient cycling.

q.q: Building a house on higher ground to avoid floods is an example of:
q.explanation: Adjusting to a hazard by changing where people live is adaptation, one of the three types of interaction.

q.q: Arrange the stages of the adaptation process correctly.
options: Analyze current and future exposure to shocks and stresses
q.explanation: The order is: analyze exposure and impacts, address critical issues, design and implement strategies, monitor and evaluate, then share lessons.

q.q: Indigenous knowledge in Africa is mainly characterized by:
options: accumulation among indigenous peoples and oral transfer across generations
transfer through formal schools and universities
q.explanation: Indigenous knowledge has been accumulated among indigenous peoples and orally transferred across many generations.

q.q: Plant medicine became an important part of the health care system in Africa partly because health care centers and medical professionals are few, especially in rural areas.
q.explanation: The textbook lists local availability, low price, community acceptance and the low number of health facilities as the reasons.

q.q: In which county of Kenya did the case study of the Teso community take place?
q.explanation: The case study was conducted in the Teso community in Busia County, Kenya.

q.q: Which activities were prohibited in the Teso protected areas?
options: Farming, grazing of animals and settlement
q.explanation: Farming, grazing of animals and even settlements were prohibited in the protected areas.

q.q: Explain how a strict prohibition on disturbing a sacred site led to a conservation outcome.
q.answer: no human activity allowed vegetation to regenerate into dense forests|forests formed habitats for flora and fauna
q.explanation: With no human activity, the sites remained very thick forests and became important habitats for a variety of flora and fauna.

q.q: The Ekutet ceremony was carried out in the presence of children and foreigners.
q.explanation: The ceremony was done in the absence of children and foreigners, by a special group of elderly men and women.

q.q: How old, at a minimum, were the graves from which the Teso exhumed the remains of the dead?
q.answer: ten years|at least ten years old
q.explanation: Remains were dug out from graves that were at least ten years old.

q.q: Why were reptiles such as snakes, frogs and toads protected by the Teso community?
options: Because of the belief that they helped sustain the important water points
Because they were valuable food for livestock
Because they were exported to other countries
Because the government fined anyone who harmed them
q.explanation: The Teso protected these reptiles due to the belief that they helped maintain and sustain the lives of the ponds, rivers and wells.

q.q: Give four uses for which African people highly depend on biological resources.
q.explanation: Besides the well-known uses for food and building houses, Africans depend highly on biological resources for medicinal purposes.

q.q: According to the unit summary, what is the key to survival in human-environment interactions?
options: Exploiting resources as fast as possible
Maintaining a suitable balance in interacting with the environment
Stopping all use of natural resources
q.explanation: Although interactions are inevitable for co-existence, maintaining a suitable balance is the key to survival.

q.q: Arrange the Teso sacred-site protection chain correctly.
options: Dense forest forms habitat for flora and fauna
Remains exhumed and transferred by basket
All human activity banned in the site
Remains stored in a strictly protected central site
q.explanation: The order is: exhume and transfer by basket, store in the protected site, ban human activity, then the dense forest forms.

q.q: Urbanization is best described as:
options: The population shift from rural to urban areas
Only the building of new government offices
Any movement of animals between habitats
q.explanation: Urbanization is the population shift from rural to urban areas, involving growth of the urban area and its population.

q.q: Which factor mainly drives rapid urbanization in African cities?
options: Rural-urban migration in search of jobs and a better life
q.explanation: Rural-urban migration, driven by the prospect of greater employment opportunities and hope of a better life, is a main factor.

q.q: Africa is still largely rural, yet it is one of the fastest urbanizing continents in the world.
q.explanation: The textbook states that although Africa is still largely rural, it is among the fastest urbanizing continents.

q.q: Which of the following African cities is NOT named in the lesson among the continent's seven megacities?
q.explanation: The seven megacities listed are Cairo, Kinshasa, Lagos, Accra, Johannesburg-Pretoria, Khartoum and Nairobi.

q.q: What is the key term for a city with a population of over 10 million people?
q.explanation: A city with over 10 million people is called a megacity.

q.q: Explain why unplanned urbanization in combination with high population density, poverty and lack of infrastructure harms residents' health.
q.answer: it fosters conditions for communicable diseases|poor sanitation and crowding spread disease
q.explanation: High density, poverty and missing infrastructure create unsanitary conditions that foster communicable diseases.

q.q: About 60 percent of jobs in African urban areas are found in the:
q.explanation: Roughly 60 percent of urban jobs are informal or grey-economy jobs, which are neither taxed nor monitored by government.

q.q: Slums and squatter settlements in Addis Ababa are identical types of unregulated settlement.
q.explanation: Slums are congested central areas with deteriorated infrastructure; squatter settlements are built illegally without title deeds, mainly on the periphery.

q.q: Set the chain of unplanned growth in its correct order. The first item of the correct order is:
options: Rural migrants arrive faster than planning can absorb
q.explanation: The order is: rapid migrant influx, spread of slums and squatters, poor sanitation, then disease spread.

q.q: The structural adjustment program of which international institution is named as a policy cause of unplanned African urbanization?
q.explanation: The policy pressure of international institutions is exemplified by the IMF's structural adjustment program.

q.q: According to the Addis Ababa case study, more than what share of the city's population is believed to be living in slums?
q.explanation: More than two-thirds of Addis Ababa's population is believed to live in slums.

q.q: Human migration is best defined as:
options: A short holiday visit to another region
The permanent change of residence by an individual or group
The growth of a city's population by birth
q.explanation: Migration is the permanent change of residence by an individual or group of people.

q.q: Which of the following is a pull factor at the place of destination?
q.explanation: Better job opportunities attract migrants; conflicts and instability are push factors at the origin.

q.q: A family moving from a rural area to a city within the same country is undertaking internal migration.
q.explanation: Movement between areas of one country, such as rural to city, is internal migration.

q.q: Forced migrations usually involve people expelled by:
options: war, drought, famine, natural disasters and political conflict
q.explanation: Forced migrations involve people expelled by war, drought, famine, natural disasters or other political conflicts.

q.q: What effect did slave migrations compelled by European slave traders between the 16th and 19th centuries have on Africa's total population?
q.answer: significantly reduced it|reduced the total population
q.explanation: The forced slave migrations significantly reduced the total population of the continent.

q.q: Give the key term for the place from which a migrant moves away.
q.explanation: The place a migrant leaves is called the origin.

q.q: In Africa, the movement of people is often limited by political boundaries.
q.explanation: Movement is often not limited by political boundaries, so communities are spread across two or three nation states.

q.q: Poor governance, corruption and civil strife are examples of:
q.explanation: They are political and social factors at the origin that push both skilled and unskilled workers to migrate.

q.q: Explain the underlying mismatch that produces the economic push factors in African origins.
q.answer: rapid population growth outpaces available resources|population growth exceeds jobs and resources
q.explanation: Economic push factors arise from a mismatch between rapid population growth and available resources, plus low technology and job-creating capacity.

q.q: Order the migration process from first to last. The first step of the correct order is:
options: New residence established at the destination
Push factors worsen conditions at the origin
q.explanation: The order is: push factors worsen, pull factors attract, the move occurs, and a new residence is established.

q.q: Migration is classified by distance as internal and ____ migration, and by will as voluntary or forced.
q.explanation: The two distance categories are internal and international migration.

q.q: The most frequent cause of coastal pollution problems is:
options: discharge of municipal sewage and industrial wastes into coastal waters or estuaries
q.explanation: The discharge of municipal sewage and industrial wastes through low quality disposal facilities is the most frequent cause.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT among the major classes of pollutants reaching coastal waters?
options: Heavy metals and other toxic matter
q.explanation: The four classes are organic materials, heavy metals and toxic matter, inorganic substances, and pathogenic organisms.

q.q: Persistent pollutants discharged into rivers far upstream from a river mouth can still reach the sea in substantial quantities.
q.explanation: The textbook states that persistent pollutants discharged into rivers even far upstream reach the sea in substantial quantities.

q.q: Which factor negatively affects the self-purification of the sea?
q.explanation: Dilution, temperature, adsorption, sedimentation and nutrient deficiencies all negatively affect self-purification.

q.q: Name the two natural coastal ecosystems whose destruction has accelerated nutrient buildup because they act as filters for sediment and wastes.
q.explanation: Wetlands and mangroves act as natural filters for sediment, excessive nitrogen and wastes.

q.q: Explain why coastal pollution can be traced to land-based human activities located far from the sea.
q.answer: rivers and watersheds carry wastes to the sea|polluted air precipitates pollutants into seas
q.explanation: Wastes generated inland enter seas through watersheds, rivers and precipitation from polluted air.

q.q: According to the WWF, over 80 percent of marine pollution in South Africa originates from:
q.explanation: Over 80 percent of South Africa's marine pollution comes from land-based sources.

q.q: Africa produces about 5 percent and consumes about 4 percent of global plastic volumes.
q.explanation: With 1.3 billion people in 2020, Africa produced 5 percent and consumed 4 percent of global plastic volumes.

q.q: How much plastic, per person, was consumed in Africa in 2015?
q.explanation: African plastic consumption in 2015 was 16 kg per person against a global average of 45 kg.

q.q: Suggest two actions that could reduce coastal pollution in Africa, according to the case study and lesson.
q.answer: better waste management and recycling|protect wetlands and mangroves|multi-stakeholder coordinated action
q.explanation: Improved waste management and recycling, protecting wetlands and mangroves, and coordinated multi-stakeholder action all answer the problem.

q.q: Why are pathogenic organisms a special risk in coastal waters near large cities?
options: They multiply fastest in cold polar seas
In temperate and warm coastal waters near large cities they survive near the coastline and in estuaries
They arrive only from cruise ships
They are killed instantly by salt water everywhere
q.explanation: Although the marine environment is generally unfavorable to pathogens, in temperate and warm coastal waters near large cities they persist near the coastline and in estuaries.

q.q: Information is best described as:
options: data processed, manipulated and organized to add knowledge
q.explanation: Information is the result of processing, manipulating and organizing data in a way that adds to the knowledge of a receiver.

q.q: Data is used as an input for the computer system, whereas information is an output of data.
q.explanation: The textbook table gives exactly this difference between data and information.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT one of the three parts of geospatial data?
options: The brand of the GPS receiver
q.explanation: Geospatial data combines location, attribute and temporal information; the receiver brand is irrelevant.

q.q: Give the term for data about objects, events or phenomena that have location information of the surface of the earth they represent.
q.explanation: This is the definition of geospatial data.

q.q: What are data that lack a location said to be, and what mapping value do they have?
q.answer: aspatial|non-spatial|aspatial or non-spatial and have no mapping value|no value at all
q.explanation: Without locations, data are aspatial or non-spatial and have no mapping value at all.

q.q: A lake within the surrounding landscape is an example of:
q.explanation: A lake is a discrete object with known and definable boundaries in open space.

q.q: The temporal element is required for every representation of geographic data.
q.explanation: Time is an optional element; it can safely be omitted for slowly changing features such as elevation.

q.q: Which government office is given in the lesson as a source of existing secondary data?
q.explanation: Existing secondary data may be obtained from different offices, for example the Central Statistical Agency.

q.q: Why is time very important when mapping temperature but not when mapping elevation?
q.answer: temperature changes daily or in minutes|elevation changes only over hundreds or thousands of years
q.explanation: Temperature can change dramatically within minutes with a cold front or thunderstorm, while elevation changes only through slow erosion and crust movements.

q.q: Which of the following is a social or economic attribute?
q.explanation: Attributes may be physical or environmental (temperature, elevation) or social and economic (population number, income).

q.q: Arrange the stages of the data cycle in the correct order.
q.explanation: The order is: data collection, data processing, data analysis, dissemination of results.

q.q: Continuous data is also referred to as:
q.explanation: Continuous data is also referred to as field, non-discrete, or surface data.

q.q: The first step in making a map is to:
q.explanation: The first step in making a map is to complete a field survey, in which surveyors observe, measure and record the area.

q.q: A GPS receiver must connect with at least how many satellites to calculate a precise location within a few meters?
q.explanation: The receiver needs to connect with four or more satellites orbiting the earth.

q.q: A GPS receiver provides latitudinal and longitudinal coordinate values of an area and its elevation value.
q.explanation: The GPS receiver provides latitudinal and longitudinal coordinate values and the elevation value of the area.

q.q: Which of the following is directly collected data?
options: Counting the number of trees in a farmland by observation
q.explanation: Counting trees in a farmland is observation data generated at the source, so it is directly collected.

q.q: Name one instrument used in digitization besides the table digitizer.
q.explanation: Instruments used in digitization include the table digitizer, the scanner and smartphones.

q.q: The spatial and location data needed to create the base map belong in the category of:
q.explanation: Base map data are primary sources because they are received for direct use in making the map.

q.q: A hard copy (analogue) map can serve as a secondary source of geographic data.
q.explanation: Hard copy maps can be used as a secondary source by enlargement or by digitizing on a computer.

q.q: Why should data from secondary sources be checked carefully before use?
q.answer: must be right and up-to-date|otherwise the final result will be wrong and outdated
q.explanation: If secondary data is not right and up-to-date, the final result will be wrong and outdated.

q.q: Remote sensing is best described as:
options: measuring the location of satellites only
gathering geographic information from a distance without physical contact with the site
q.explanation: Remote sensing gathers geographic information from a distance by an instrument not physically in contact with the mapping site.

q.q: Define georeferencing in one sentence.
q.answer: relating the internal coordinate system of an image to the geographic coordinate system of the area
q.explanation: Georeferencing means the internal coordinate system of a map or aerial photo image can be related to the geographic coordinate system of the area being scanned.

q.q: Which statement about data from a table digitizer versus a smartphone image is correct?
options: Digitizer data provides geo-referenced information, while smartphone images must be geo-referenced
Neither can be used for mapping
q.explanation: Data generated by a digitizer provides geo-referenced information, whereas images from scanners and smartphones should be geo-referenced.

q.q: Which of the following is the analogue form of geographic data representation?
options: A hardcopy map printed on paper
A satellite image on a computer
q.explanation: Hardcopy, also known as analogue format, is the form printed on paper or similar physical material.

q.q: Digital data are easy to copy and transmit at very high speeds.
q.explanation: This is one of the listed advantages of the digital format over paper maps.

q.q: Which of these is NOT an advantage of digital geographic data?
options: Stored at high density in small spaces
More subject to physical deterioration than paper
Easy to transform, process and analyze
q.explanation: Digital data is LESS subject to the physical deterioration that affects paper format.

q.q: Give the common name for an area feature described by a closed string of spatial coordinates.
q.explanation: An area feature is commonly referred to as a polygon.

q.q: Which of the following is an example of point data?
q.explanation: A water well, like a telephone tower or weather station, exists at a single location, so it is point data.

q.q: Define a node in the vector data model.
q.answer: a vertex that starts or ends an arc segment
q.explanation: A node is defined as a vertex that starts or ends an arc segment.

q.q: Every vertex in a vector segment carries an X coordinate and a Y coordinate.
q.explanation: Each vertex consists of a pair of X and Y coordinates, or latitudinal and longitudinal values.

q.q: In the raster data model, the geographic area is divided into:
options: cells identified by row and column
q.explanation: Raster data models use a grid-cell data structure identified by row and column.

q.q: The size of raster cells in a tessellated data structure is selected based on:
options: the data accuracy and the resolution needed by the user
q.explanation: Cell size is selected based on the data accuracy and the resolution needed by the user.

q.q: Match each raster representation to its feature: (a) areas, (b) lines, (c) points, with (1) collections of contiguous cells, (2) sequences of neighboring cells, (3) a single cell.
q.explanation: Raster represents points by a single cell, lines by sequences of neighboring cells, and areas by collections of contiguous cells.

q.q: Why are most polygon data considered homogeneous?
options: because they are consistent throughout the area
because they are always drawn small
because they come from satellites only
q.explanation: Most polygon data are considered to be homogeneous, and thus they are consistent.

q.q: According to the lesson, the human activity of graphically representing one's perception of the world:
options: pre-dates virtually all other forms of written communication
q.explanation: Mapmaking is a universally acquired skill that pre-dates virtually all other forms of written communication.

q.q: Early maps were highly accurate drawings of the actual world.
q.explanation: Early maps were a garbled or distorted mass of land that bore no resemblance to the actual world.

q.q: Which advances helped mapmakers accurately draw the general outline of the continents from the 18th century onward?
options: Advances in mathematics and astronomy, plus longitude and latitude
q.explanation: Advances in mathematics and astronomy and the division of the earth into lines of longitude and latitude were among the most notable.

q.q: The Geographic Information System (GIS) is best defined as:
options: a computer-based system that stores, visualizes, analyzes and interprets geographic data
a paper map of the earth
q.explanation: GIS is a computer-based system enabling us to store, visualize, analyze and interpret geographic data.

q.q: Name any three components of GIS.
q.explanation: The components of GIS are hardware, software, people, methods and data.

q.q: Which of the following belongs to GIS hardware?
q.explanation: Hardware includes the computer and attached devices such as printers, plotters and scanners.

q.q: Why is the role of satellites so important in 21st-century mapping?
q.answer: they perform continuous scans|provide up-to-date maps of nearly the entire earth
q.explanation: Satellites perform continuous scans to provide detailed up-to-date maps of nearly the entire earth.

q.q: List any four pieces of marginal information required in the final layout of an ArcMap administrative map.
q.answer: legend|scale bar|north arrow|coordinate information|gridlines|date of map compilation
q.explanation: The layout must include a legend, scale bar, north arrow, coordinate information, gridlines and the date of map compilation.

q.q: In the ArcMap exercise, which shapefile would you use to select a regional boundary such as the Oromia National Regional State?
q.explanation: The region is selected by right-clicking the etregio01co layer and highlighting Oromia in its attribute table.

q.q: GIS data must be accurate no matter what type of data it is.
q.explanation: One of the most important things about the data component is that the data must be accurate.

q.q: Arrange the ArcMap steps in the correct order.
options: Add the marginal information in layout view
Download and extract the Ethiopia shapefiles into a folder
Select the area of interest in the attribute table and export the data
Connect to the folder and add etbound01co and etregio01co
q.explanation: The order is: download and extract, connect and add shapefiles, select and export, then add marginal information in layout view.

q.q: Which chart is used to show relationships between different data series that are independent of each other?
q.explanation: A bar graph shows relationships between data series that are independent of each other.

q.q: A line graph is especially useful when you want to demonstrate:
options: how a whole divides into parts
trends or numbers connected over time
q.explanation: A line graph represents how data has changed over time, which is useful for trends or connected numbers.

q.q: The height or length of a bar in a bar graph indicates the measured value or frequency.
q.explanation: This is exactly what the bar height or length indicates.

q.q: SPSS stands for:
options: Statistical Package for the Social Sciences
Survey Program for Students and Schools
q.explanation: SPSS is the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences, used like a spreadsheet for making graphs and charts.

q.q: Why do presenters use graphs, charts and diagrams instead of raw numbers? Give any two reasons from the lesson.
q.answer: draw and keep attention|evidence-based work|help understand and memorize main points|describe trends|make comparisons|show relationships
q.explanation: They draw and keep attention, make the work evidence-based, help listeners understand and memorize main points, and describe trends, comparisons and relationships.

q.q: A pie segment must cover 25 percent of a circle. How many units of arc is that out of 360? Give just the number.
The unit project work asks students to collect the sex and age data of the class and draw:
options: a pie chart of the sex distribution
q.explanation: The project work is to draw a pie chart showing the sex distribution of students in the class.

q.q: Which program would you mainly use to draw the components of sustainable development as overlapping circles, and which for a rainfall bar graph?
q.answer: word for the diagram and excel for the bar graph|microsoft word and microsoft excel
q.explanation: Diagrams can be drawn in Microsoft Word, while bar graphs, line graphs and pie charts can be prepared in Microsoft Excel.

q.q: Each segment of a pie chart represents a particular category within the total data set.
q.explanation: Pie chart segments represent categories of the whole, showing its percentage distribution.

q.q: Define a diagram in one sentence.
q.answer: a plan drawing or outline to illustrate how separate parts work and overlap at the connecting points
q.explanation: A diagram is a plan, drawing or outline created to illustrate how separate parts work and overlap at the connecting points.

q.q: Arrange the pie chart computation steps in the correct order.
options: Convert each fraction to an angle by multiplying by 360
Add all category values to find the total
Draw the circle and label each segment
Divide each category value by the total to get its fraction
q.explanation: First total the values, then find each fraction, then convert to angles, then draw and label so all angles sum to 360.

q.q: Which European country was the first to be industrialized?
q.explanation: The textbook states that the Industrial Revolution first started in England in the 18th century.

q.q: The two social classes formed as a result of the Industrial Revolution were:
options: The peasantry and the feudal lords
q.explanation: Industrialization promoted the proletariat and the bourgeoisie.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of capitalism?
q.explanation: Capitalism is based on private, not public, ownership of the means of production.

q.q: In capitalism, most means of production are privately owned.
q.explanation: This is the defining feature of the capitalist system.

q.q: A command economy is one in which the government is in charge of the economy.
q.explanation: In a command economy the state controls production, distribution and prices.

q.q: Name the new source of power, along with coal, that replaced wind and water power after the Industrial Revolution.
q.explanation: Coal and steam became the main new sources of energy and power.

q.q: Give the name of the wealthy class that owns the means of production in a capitalist system.
q.explanation: The bourgeoisie, or capitalists, own the means of production.

q.q: Explain how the riches of the slave trade and plantations helped capitalism develop in Europe.
q.answer: capital funded industrialization|riches used to fund industry
q.explanation: Profits from colonies, plantations and the slave trade became capital used to fund Europe's industrialization.

q.q: In countries like Germany and Italy, industrialization was linked to mass militarization and nationalism, which ultimately led to:
q.explanation: The textbook links this militarization and nationalism ultimately to World War I.

q.q: Which British port town is named as receiving tremendous riches from the slave trade?
q.explanation: The slave trade delivered riches to British port towns such as Liverpool.

q.q: Which statement best describes a capitalist economy?
options: The government controls the entire business
Factories are owned by the working class
Production is privately owned and operated for profit
A command economy directs all prices
q.explanation: Capitalism is a system where production is privately owned and run for profit.

q.q: Nationalism is best defined as:
options: A feeling of belonging and loyalty to a nation
q.explanation: Nationalism is a feeling of belonging and loyalty that causes people to think of themselves as a nation.
