q.explanation: On 21 March 1960 police fired on unarmed demonstrators, killing 72 and wounding 186, which brought worldwide condemnation and sanctions.

q.q: The ANC's campaign of passive resistance in 1952 was led by all of the following EXCEPT:
q.explanation: Ian Smith led the white minority in Southern Rhodesia, not the ANC.

q.q: Apartheid denied all political rights to blacks and other non-whites.
q.explanation: Apartheid denied all political rights to blacks and other non-whites.

q.q: When Mandela left the presidency in 1999, power passed to:
options: his second in command in the ANC
q.explanation: In 1999 Mandela left the presidency to the next democratically elected president, his second in command in the ANC.

q.q: Explain what 'separate development of the races' meant in practice.
q.answer: segregation|no political rights|land reserved for whites
q.explanation: It meant rigid segregation in schools, hospitals, buses and other public places, no political rights for blacks, and 87 per cent of the land reserved for whites.

q.q: In which month and year did Nelson Mandela win the first democratic election?
q.explanation: Mandela won the election in April 1994.

q.q: Pan-Africanism is best defined as the idea that:
options: peoples of African descent have common interests and should be unified
African states should join the World Bank
Africa needs a single colonial administration
q.explanation: Pan-Africanism is the idea that peoples of African descent have common interests and should be unified.

q.q: In which city and month of 1963 was the OAU founded?
q.explanation: Delegates met at Addis Ababa between 22 and 25 May 1963 to establish the OAU.

q.q: How many independent African countries sent delegates to the founding conference of the OAU?
q.explanation: Delegates from 32 African countries convened at Addis Ababa in May 1963.

q.q: The Fifth Pan-African Congress met at Manchester in October 1945.
q.explanation: The Fifth Pan-African Congress was held at Manchester in October 1945, with African delegates dominating.

q.q: State the main difference between the Casablanca Group and the Monrovia Group.
q.explanation: Casablanca wanted a strong political union along Nkrumah's United States of Africa; Monrovia wanted a loose confederation of sovereign states.

q.q: Which of the following was NOT an objective of the OAU?
options: To rid Africa of colonization and apartheid
To safeguard sovereignty and territorial integrity
To create a single African currency in 1963
q.explanation: The objectives listed are decolonization, unity, development cooperation, sovereignty and international cooperation, not a single currency.

q.q: Name the OAU organ that met once a year in a different capital city.
q.answer: assembly of heads of state and government|assembly
q.explanation: The Assembly of the Heads of State and Government was the supreme organ and met once a year.

q.q: The OAU fully succeeded in bringing peace, prosperity and stability to Africa.
q.explanation: Its major failing was its inability to bring peace, prosperity, security and stability.

q.q: The African Union replaced the OAU and was launched in July 2002 at:
q.explanation: The AU was officially launched in July 2002 in Durban, South Africa.

q.q: Explain why a new organization, the African Union, was created to replace the OAU.
q.answer: oau too weak|failures outweighed|globalization|peace and security
q.explanation: The OAU's powers were too weak and its influence inadequate for conflict, poor governance, poverty and globalization, so comprehensive reform became imperative.

q.q: Which list arranges these events in correct chronological order, earliest first?
options: Manchester Congress, OAU founded, AU launched
OAU founded, Manchester Congress, AU launched
AU launched, OAU founded, Manchester Congress
Manchester Congress, AU launched, OAU founded
q.explanation: Manchester was in 1945, the OAU was founded in 1963, and the AU was launched in 2002.

q.q: Africa achieved substantial economic growth between:
q.explanation: Africa grew substantially from 1965 to 1974, with a downward trend afterwards.

q.q: Two principal factors that adversely affected African development in the 1980s and 1990s were:
q.explanation: The textbook names international debt and drought as the two principal adverse factors.

q.q: Since the 1960s, Africa's raw material exports have dropped in price ten or twenty times compared with manufactured imports.
q.explanation: This fall in export prices is the root of the adverse terms of trade.

q.q: Which regional economic community has twenty-one member states stretching from Tunisia to Swaziland?
q.explanation: COMESA has twenty-one members from Tunisia to Swaziland.

q.q: Explain the idea of adverse terms of trade.
q.answer: export prices fall|raw materials cheap|imports expensive|less foreign exchange
q.explanation: It means a country receives less for its exports while paying more for imports, so it earns less foreign exchange.

q.q: The African Economic Community was established under the:
q.explanation: The African Economic Community was established under the Abuja Treaty of 1991.

q.q: Which of the following countries is a member of IGAD?
q.explanation: IGAD includes Ethiopia, Sudan, South Sudan, Eritrea, Kenya, Uganda and Djibouti.

q.q: COMESA replaced a Preferential Trade Area that had existed since 1981.
q.explanation: COMESA was formed in December 1994, replacing a Preferential Trade Area existing since 1981.

q.q: In which year did COMESA replace the Preferential Trade Area?
q.explanation: COMESA was formed in December 1994.

q.q: Why did African governments turn to the IMF and World Bank, and what criticism is made of those institutions?
q.answer: foreign exchange|loans|interests of the west|raw materials
q.explanation: They ran out of foreign exchange and borrowed to pay interest, but the lenders were financed by western banks whose priorities reflected western interests in African raw materials.

q.q: The purpose of the Regional Economic Communities is to:
options: collect taxes for the African Union
facilitate regional integration and eventual continental integration
q.explanation: Their purpose is to facilitate regional economic integration and, through the wider African Economic Community, continental integration.

q.q: The Rwandan genocide took place between:
q.explanation: The violence occurred from April to July 1994 between the Tutsi and the Hutu.

q.q: Approximately how many people died in the Rwandan genocide?
q.explanation: The attempted extermination of the Tutsi resulted in 800,000 deaths, the majority being Tutsi.

q.q: The Biafra War is also known as the:
q.explanation: The Biafra War is also known as the Nigerian Civil War.

q.q: Of the world's 20 war-related conflicts in 2013, 11 were fought in sub-Saharan Africa.
q.explanation: The textbook states that 11 of the world's 20 war-related conflicts in 2013 were fought in sub-Saharan Africa.

q.q: Give two causes of poverty in Africa named in the lesson.
q.answer: population growth|war and crises|climatic conditions|diseases|agricultural infrastructure
q.explanation: The causes named are population growth, war and crises, climatic conditions, diseases and inadequate agricultural infrastructure.

q.q: Which two regions are particularly affected by climate change according to the lesson?
q.answer: east africa and the sahel|sahel|east africa
q.explanation: East Africa and the Sahel region are particularly affected.

q.q: Diseases such as AIDS, malaria and Ebola are described as:
options: both a cause and a result of poverty
q.explanation: The textbook says these diseases are the cause but also the result of poverty in Africa.

q.q: The 1980s in Africa are often called the lost decade.
q.explanation: The problems of the newly independent countries reached a climax in the 1980s, often known as the lost decade.

q.q: What is meant by Africa's second independence?
q.answer: democratic reforms|1990s|collapse of single-party rule|end of military rule
q.explanation: It was the democratic wave of the 1990s and 2000s that ended single-party dictatorships and military rule.

q.q: According to the lesson, the root cause of ethnic conflicts in African states is:
q.explanation: At the root of the ethnic conflicts have been political, economic and social injustices.

q.q: Which list arranges these events in correct chronological order, earliest first?
options: Biafra War, Rwandan genocide, the second independence
Rwandan genocide, Biafra War, the second independence
The second independence, Biafra War, Rwandan genocide
Biafra War, the second independence, Rwandan genocide
q.explanation: The Biafra War followed Nigerian independence in 1960, the Rwandan genocide was in 1994, and the democratic wave is dated to the 1990s and 2000s.

q.q: Which coalition toppled the Derg regime in 1991?
q.explanation: The EPRDF, a coalition of ethno-nationalist forces dominated by the TPLF, toppled the Derg.

q.q: The May 1991 London Conference was sponsored by:
q.explanation: The London Conference was sponsored by the United States of America.

q.q: The London Conference of 1991 failed because the insurgents occupied Addis Ababa on May 28, 1991.
q.explanation: The conference was overtaken by events when the insurgents occupied Addis Ababa on May 28, 1991.

q.q: Who chaired the Ethiopian Democratic and Peaceful Transitional Conference of July 1991?
q.explanation: Meles Zenawi chaired the July 1991 conference in Addis Ababa.

q.q: How many members did the Council of Representatives of the TGE have?
q.explanation: The new government included an 87-member Council of Representatives.

q.q: Give the name of the document that functioned as the transitional constitution of Ethiopia in 1991.
q.explanation: The National Charter functioned as a transitional constitution.

q.q: How many self-governing regions were established by the Transitional Charter?
q.explanation: The Charter established 14 self-governing regions of nations, nationalities and peoples.

q.q: The OLF remained a member of the government throughout the whole transitional period.
q.explanation: Nearly a year after the formation of the TGE, the OLF withdrew from the government.

q.q: Arrange these events of the transition in the correct order.
options: The occupation of Addis Ababa on May 28, 1991
The July 1991 national conference adopts the Charter
q.explanation: The order is: London Conference, occupation of Addis Ababa, July conference and Charter, then the 1994 Constituent Assembly.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why the years 1991 to 1995 are called a transitional period in Ethiopia.
q.answer: temporary institutions led to the 1995 constitution|the Charter was a transitional constitution
q.explanation: The National Charter and the TGE were temporary arrangements that led to the permanent 1995 constitution.

q.q: Which country offered Assab for Ethiopia's use as a free port?
q.explanation: The EPLF offered Assab for the use of Ethiopia as a free port.

q.q: How many articles does the 1995 FDRE Constitution contain?
q.explanation: It is a document of 106 articles contained in eleven chapters.

q.q: The two city administrations of the FDRE are Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa.
q.explanation: Ethiopia is a composite of nine states and two city administrations, Addis Ababa and Dire Dawa.

q.q: Which article of the 1995 constitution deals with the right to self-determination and secession?
q.explanation: Article 39 grants ethno-national communities self-determination, including the right to secede.

q.q: Which house of parliament has constitutional interpretation as its main task?
q.explanation: The main task of the House of Federation is constitutional interpretation under Article 62.

q.q: The largest regional state of the FDRE, accounting for about one-third of the landmass, is:
q.explanation: Oromia State accounts for one-third of the country's total landmass.

q.q: Give the term used to describe a federation whose constituent units are formed on an ethno-linguistic basis.
q.explanation: Commentators call Ethiopia's arrangement ethnic or ethnical federalism.

q.q: The constitution states that Ethiopia has thirteen chapters.
q.explanation: The constitution has 106 articles in eleven chapters, not thirteen.

q.q: Which is the smallest regional state by area?
q.explanation: Harari State is by far the smallest at only 340 square kilometres.

q.q: Name any three of the nine regional states of the FDRE.
q.explanation: The nine states are Tigray, Afar, Amhara, Oromia, Somali, Benishangul-Gumuz, SNNPRS, Gambella and Harari.

q.q: Which statement best describes the ethnic composition of the nine states?
options: Each state contains only one ethnic group
All states have exactly two groups
q.explanation: Although the states have an ethnic configuration, none of them is homogeneous.

q.q: Explain in one sentence the constitutional objective of the Ethiopian federal structure.
q.answer: unity in diversity|protect ethnic rights and cooperate
q.explanation: The objective is the creation of unity in diversity, protecting group rights within one cooperating country.

q.q: Approximately how long is the Nile River?
q.explanation: The Nile flows for about 6825 kilometres, the longest river in the world.

q.q: Which tributary contributes about 86 per cent of the annual volume of the Nile?
q.explanation: The Blue Nile contributes about 86 per cent of the annual volume of water to the Nile.

q.q: The Tekeze River is known as the Atbara after it enters Sudan near Gallabat.
q.explanation: After entering Sudan around Gallabat, Tekeze bears the name Atbara.

q.q: Where does the Blue Nile join the White Nile?
q.explanation: The Blue Nile joins the White Nile in Khartoum.

q.q: Under the 1959 Agreement, Egypt was granted how much water per annum?
q.explanation: The 1959 Agreement granted Egypt 55.5 billion cubic metres per annum.

q.q: Give the name of the all-inclusive basin-wide institution established on 22 February 1999.
q.explanation: The Nile Basin Initiative was established on 22 February 1999 at Dar es Salaam.

q.q: The 1929 Agreement had a binding effect on Ethiopia because Ethiopia was a signatory.
q.explanation: The 1929 Agreement did not include any upper riparian state, so it was not binding on Ethiopia.

q.q: The GERD is being constructed on which river and in which region?
q.explanation: Ethiopia started the GERD on the Abay River in the Benishangul-Gumuz region in April 2011.

q.q: Name any four of the eleven Nile riparian states.
q.explanation: The eleven riparian states are Burundi, DRC, Egypt, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Rwanda, Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda and South Sudan.

q.q: Arrange these Nile events in the correct chronological order.
options: The Nile Basin Initiative is established
q.explanation: The order is 1929 Agreement, 1959 Agreement, NBI in 1999, and the GERD from 2011.

q.q: Why is the Nile Basin Initiative considered different from the earlier agreements?
options: It was the first all-inclusive basin-wide institution
It divided the water between two states
q.explanation: For the first time an all-inclusive basin-wide institution was established for consultation and coordination.

q.q: What economic model did the TGE adopt in 1992?
q.explanation: In 1992 the TGE adopted a free-market economic model, departing from the previous socialist model.

q.q: The ALDI strategy aimed to industrialise Ethiopia by first:
q.explanation: ALDI sought to improve agricultural productivity so that surplus would stimulate consumerism and create demand for industry.

q.q: Ethiopia's economy grew by around 10.9 per cent per annum from 2005 to 2015.
q.explanation: Growth reached about 10.9 per cent per annum from 2005 to 2015, among the fastest for a non-oil-producing country.

q.q: By how much did Ethiopia's road network grow between 1991 and recent times?
q.answer: 18,000 km to over 120,000 km|from 18000 to over 120000
q.explanation: The road network grew from 18,000 km in 1991 to over 120,000 km.

q.q: Rapid economic growth meant that poverty was completely eliminated in Ethiopia.
q.explanation: About 25 million people, around a quarter of the population, still lived below the poverty line.

q.q: Name the region and river associated with the major infrastructure project mentioned alongside road expansion.
q.answer: GERD on the Abay in Benishangul-Gumuz|Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam
q.explanation: The textbook names the GERD, built on the Abay in Benishangul-Gumuz, as an example of infrastructure development.

q.q: Which two major opposition alliances took part in the 2005 election?
q.explanation: The major opposition alliances were the Coalition for Unity and Democracy and the Union of Ethiopian Democratic Forces.

q.q: In the 2005 election the opposition won up to how many of the 547 seats?
q.explanation: The opposition won up to 173 out of the 547 seats of the House of Peoples' Representatives.

q.q: Arrange these elections in the correct chronological order.
q.explanation: The order is 1995, 2000, 2005 and 2010.

q.q: Following the 2005 election, the opposition parties won all the federal parliamentary seats in Addis Ababa.
q.explanation: In the capital the opposition won all the federal parliamentary seats and those of the city administration council.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why the first two elections weakened the legitimacy of the political process.
q.answer: opposition boycott|largely boycotted by the opposition
q.explanation: The first two elections were largely boycotted by the opposition, which undermined the legitimacy of the process and of the ruling party.

q.q: Indigenous knowledge is often known as:
q.explanation: The textbook states that indigenous knowledge is often known as local knowledge.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT correct about indigenous knowledge?
options: It is transmitted orally from generation to generation
It provides problem-solving strategies for local communities
It is generated within a community in location and culture
It is expressed in universal languages
q.explanation: Indigenous knowledge is expressed in local languages, not in universal languages.

q.q: Indigenous knowledge is simple and practical.
q.explanation: The textbook begins its account of the characteristics by saying that indigenous knowledge is simple and practical.

q.q: Give the other term that is often used for indigenous knowledge.
q.explanation: Indigenous knowledge is often known as local knowledge.

q.q: Give the term for the knowledge that assists society in making judgments about activities compatible with its way of life.
q.explanation: That is the textbook definition of indigenous knowledge.

q.q: Indigenous knowledge provides a basic and rich ground for the development of:
q.explanation: It provides basic and rich ground for the development of modern society.

q.q: Indigenous knowledge systems and technologies are socially desired, economically viable and sustainable.
q.explanation: The textbook says they have been proven to be socially desired, economically viable and sustainable.

q.q: Name the two main means through which indigenous knowledge is passed down.
q.explanation: It is passed down through oral tradition and practice.

q.q: Explain in one sentence how learning from indigenous knowledge helps development.
q.answer: it improves understanding of local conditions|it improves agriculture, healthcare, food security, education and natural resource management
q.explanation: Learning from it improves understanding of local conditions and of agriculture, healthcare, food security, education and natural resource management.

q.q: Which statement best explains why preserving indigenous knowledge matters for Ethiopia?
options: It replaces the need for modern science
It contributes to cultural and political self-reliance and conserves resources
It is only useful for tourism
It proves that Ethiopia needs no foreign knowledge
q.explanation: Preserving indigenous knowledge contributes to cultural and political self-reliance and conserves resources.

q.q: Arrange the stages by which local knowledge turns into development.
options: Pass the knowledge to the next generation
Use local knowledge to solve a local problem
Conserve the resources it depends on
Test and adapt the practice over time
q.explanation: The order is: use local knowledge on a local problem, test and adapt it, conserve resources, then pass it on.

q.q: Indigenous conflict resolution in Ethiopia is mainly described as:
options: an informal way of resolving conflicts through arbitration and mediation
q.explanation: It is an informal way of resolving conflicts, an old collection of techniques that works through arbitration and mediation.

q.q: The main aim of the indigenous dispute resolution mechanism is to:
options: reach a solution based on the recognised customs and morality of the society
q.explanation: Its main aim is a solution based on the recognised customs and morality of the society, restoring good relations.

q.q: Which indigenous mechanism of the Afar is an unwritten law transmitted orally from generation to generation?
q.explanation: The Afar mechanism of conflict resolution is known as Mada'a.

q.q: The most important function of the Dagu of Afar is:
options: to settle conflicts among the community
to strengthen economic support and aid
q.explanation: Dagu is an age-old system of information management used to pass and receive news.

q.q: Give the name of the indigenous democratic system of governance of the Oromo people, in which five classes succeed each other every eight years.
q.explanation: This is the Gadaa system.

q.q: What is the Oromo term for the process of reconciliation between conflicting individuals or groups by elders?
q.explanation: Jaarsummaa is reconciliation by a group of jaarsaas (elders).

q.q: Gumaa, among the Oromo, refers to:
options: blood money paid to the family of a slain person or to injured individuals
q.explanation: Gumaa is the blood money paid to the slain person's family or the payment made to seriously injured individuals.

q.q: The institution through which women's rights are duly respected among the Oromo is:
q.explanation: Siinqee (Siiqee) is the instrument through which women's rights are respected among the Oromo.

q.q: Shimgelina uses five elders appointed by the disputing parties themselves.
q.explanation: In Shimgelina, five shimageles are appointed by the disputing parties themselves based on their choice.

q.q: Name the moral code of the Sidama that provides the basis for distinguishing good from evil.
q.explanation: The Sidama moral code halale, the ultimate truth, distinguishes good from evil.

q.q: Arrange the steps of settling a dispute through the indigenous mechanism.
options: Agree a solution and restore the relationship
Elders are invited and hear both sides
q.explanation: A dispute arises, elders are invited, customs are examined, then a solution restores the relationship.

q.q: Heritage is best defined as something that:
options: can be sold quickly for profit
is passed from generation to generation and has historic or cultural value
was made in the last ten years
q.explanation: Heritage can be passed from generation to generation, can be conserved or inherited, and has historic or cultural value.

q.q: Language, popular song, literature and dress can be heritage.
q.explanation: The textbook says these practices are just as significant as physical artifacts and buildings.

q.q: Give the term for the meanings and values that people bestow on heritage.
q.explanation: These are called heritage values.

q.q: Name two classifications of heritage values given in the lesson.
q.explanation: Classifications include historical, aesthetic, economic, social and scientific values.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a classification of heritage values?
q.explanation: The listed classifications are historical, aesthetic, economic, social and scientific.

q.q: In the unit introduction, heritage is described as:
options: our inheritance: what the past passed to us and what we preserve for the future
q.explanation: Our heritage is our inheritance, what the past has passed to us and what we choose to preserve for the future generation.

q.q: Heritage values are meanings that individuals or groups bestow on heritage.
q.explanation: The term heritage values refers to the meanings and values that individuals or groups bestow on heritage.

q.q: Heritage is described as part of the social glue that binds communities together and expresses what?
q.explanation: Heritage expresses identity and binds communities together.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why heritage matters for Ethiopians.
q.answer: it gives a context for our perception of ourselves|it expresses identity|it binds communities together
q.explanation: It provides a context for our perception of ourselves as Ethiopians and binds communities together.

q.q: An old church, a folk song and a river gorge are all called heritage because:
options: they all belong to the state
each can be passed on, conserved and valued for historic, cultural or natural reasons
they were all built by kings
q.explanation: Heritage includes physical objects, practices and places with inherited historic, cultural or natural value.

q.q: Which of the following is an example of intangible heritage?
options: Palace of Jimma Abba Jifar II
q.explanation: Fiche-Chambalaalla is a New Year celebration, so it is intangible heritage.

q.q: Tangible heritages include all of the following, except:
q.explanation: Songs are an expression rather than a physical artifact, so they are not tangible heritage.

q.q: The indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo people is known as:
q.explanation: Gadaa is the indigenous democratic socio-political system of the Oromo people.

q.q: Which one of the following has been inscribed on the representative list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity by UNESCO?
q.explanation: Gadaa was inscribed on the representative list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity in 2016.

q.q: In which year were the Rock-hewn Churches of Lalibela registered by UNESCO?
q.explanation: They were registered as a World Heritage Site in 1978.

q.q: How many churches are found at Lalibela?
q.explanation: All eleven churches represent a unique artistic achievement.

q.q: Name the type of heritage that refers to practices, representations, expressions, knowledge, skills, instruments, objects and artefacts.
q.explanation: That is the textbook definition of intangible heritage.

q.q: The Simien Mountains National Park is home to which rare animals?
options: Gelada baboon, Simien fox and Walia ibex
q.explanation: The park is home to the Gelada baboon, the Simien fox and the Walia ibex.

q.q: Tiya is found 90 km south of Addis Ababa and contains:
q.explanation: The site contains 36 monuments, including 32 carved stelae covered with symbols.

q.q: The wall of Harar Jugol was built during the time of Emir Nur Ibn Mujahid in the 16th century.
q.explanation: The wall (Jugol) was built during the time of Emir Nur Ibn Mujahid in the 16th century.

q.q: In which year was the Gadaa system inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity?
q.explanation: Gadaa was inscribed on the representative list of the intangible cultural heritage of humanity in 2016.

q.q: Which of these is NOT a function?
q.explanation: Input 1 appears with outputs 2 AND 3 — one-to-many is forbidden in a function

q.q: The domain of a relation is…
q.explanation: Domain = inputs = first coordinates of the ordered pairs

q.q: A vertical line intersects a curve at two points. The curve represents…
q.explanation: Vertical line test: two hits means one x-value has two y-values — not a function

q.q: If A has 3 elements and B has 4, how many relations are possible from A to B?
q.explanation: A × B has 12 pairs; relations = subsets = 2¹² = 4096

q.q: Every function is a relation.
q.explanation: A function is a special kind of relation — one output per input

q.q: A many-to-one mapping fails the definition of a function.
q.explanation: Many-to-one is allowed; only one-to-many breaks the function rule

q.q: For f = {(2,5),(3,7),(4,9)}, write the range.
q.explanation: Range = the set of second coordinates: {5, 7, 9}

q.q: State the domain of y = 1/(x − 3) over the reals.
q.explanation: Division by zero: x = 3 is excluded; every other real works

q.q: Explain why the matching 'each Ethiopian → their woreda (district)' is a function but not one-to-one.
q.answer: many people same district|many-to-one|each person one district|multiple people share
q.explanation: Every person has exactly one district (function), but many people share a district (not one-to-one)

q.q: Order from most general to most specific:
q.explanation: All one-to-one functions are functions; all functions are relations

q.q: If f(x) = 3x − 4, what is f(−2)?
The natural domain of f(x) = 1/(x² − 9) is:
q.explanation: x² − 9 = 0 at x = 3 and x = −3; both must be excluded

q.q: Which graph is NOT a function?
q.explanation: A circle fails the vertical line test — most x-values give two y-values

q.q: f(x) = x + 1, g(x) = x². What is (f ∘ g)(3)?
f(a + b) always equals f(a) + f(b).
q.explanation: Only for special linear-through-origin functions; e.g. f(x)=x²: (a+b)² ≠ a²+b²

q.q: The range of f(x) = |x| is all non-negative reals.
q.explanation: Absolute value is never negative, and every y ≥ 0 is hit (x = ±y)

q.q: For f(x) = 2x² + 1, find f(2).
State the domain of f(x) = √(x + 3) over the reals.
q.answer: x ≥ -3|x >= -3|all reals greater than or equal to -3
q.explanation: Need x + 3 ≥ 0, so x ≥ −3

q.q: A table lists x: 1,2,3,2 and y: 4,5,6,7. Is it a function? Why?
q.answer: no|not a function|2 has two outputs|repeated x
q.explanation: x = 2 appears with both y = 5 and y = 7 — one input, two outputs

q.q: Taxi cost C(d) = 30 + 15d (ETB, d in km). How much for 8 km?
A candle 24 cm long burns 1.5 cm per hour. Which models its height?
q.explanation: Starts at 24 and decreases 1.5 per hour; domain 0 ≤ t ≤ 16

q.q: The slope of a cost model C(w) = 12w + 50 tells you…
q.explanation: Slope 12 = marginal cost, the ETB added per extra kg

q.q: For Q3-style revenue R(q) = 100q − 2q², revenue is maximised at:
A delivery costs 30 ETB base + 10 ETB/km, capped at 150 ETB total. The model is best described as:
q.explanation: Linear up to 12 km, then flat at the cap — two branches

q.q: A model's domain should reflect physical limits of the situation.
q.explanation: Negative time, negative copies, over-empty tanks are all impossible inputs

q.q: Extrapolating far beyond observed data is always safe if the formula is simple.
q.explanation: Real relationships bend; linear trends break outside their observed range

q.q: V(t) = 600 − 20t litres. How much water remains after 12 hours?
Phone plan: 200 ETB/month includes 5 GB, then 40 ETB per extra GB. Bill for 8.5 GB (charge per full extra GB, round up)?
q.explanation: 3.5 extra GB → 4 charged: 200 + 4×40 = 360 ETB (340 if not rounded up)

q.q: In C(n) = 2n (n ≤ 200), C(n) = 400 + 1.5(n−200) (n > 200): what is the breakpoint quantity?
q.explanation: The tier changes at n = 200 copies
