q.q: Ethiopia is described in the lesson as a country with:
q.explanation: The lesson states that Ethiopia is a country with rich indigenous knowledge systems.

q.q: Indigenous knowledge is usually transmitted from elders to young people through practice, proverbs and stories.
q.explanation: Young people inherit the tradition from elders because they are tomorrow's elders.

q.q: According to the lesson, when a husband and wife get into conflict in most parts of Ethiopia they:
options: go directly to the woreda court
take the case to local elders first
ask the police to arrest one party
q.explanation: They take their case to local elders to resolve the disagreement through a win-win approach.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why indigenous knowledge differs from one society to another.
q.answer: it is based on that society's culture, traditions, rituals, values and beliefs|because cultures and environments differ
q.explanation: Indigenous knowledge grows from the particular culture and environment of a community, so it varies.

q.q: Give the name of one artisan craft listed among Ethiopia's indigenous technologies.
q.explanation: Pottery, weaving, iron smithing, jewelry, wood carving and leather work are all listed.

q.q: Arrange the following in the order in which a local conflict is normally handled in an Ethiopian community.
options: An elder mediates between the parties
The two parties reach a win-win agreement
q.explanation: The disagreement comes first, then elder mediation, then a win-win agreement; a court case is the least usual step.

q.q: A responsible citizen is best described as a person who:
options: has knowledge and commitment to improve livelihood, community and country
q.explanation: This is the textbook definition of a responsible citizen.

q.q: Which is the indigenous conflict resolution mechanism of the Oromo people?
q.explanation: Jaarsummaa is practised by the Oromo; Guurt is Somali, Yejoka Gurage and Mada'a Afar.

q.q: In Ethiopia, indigenous conflict resolution mechanisms have paramount significance compared with modern courts in ensuring sustainable peace.
q.explanation: The lesson states that indigenous mechanisms are of paramount significance in ensuring sustainable peace.

q.q: Name the indigenous mechanism of the Somali people mentioned in the lesson.
q.explanation: The Guurt system is the Somali indigenous conflict resolution mechanism.

q.q: Indigenous technologies help Ethiopian citizens mainly because they:
options: use local products at reasonable cost with better accessibility
q.explanation: Local products are cheaper and more accessible than pricey and scarce imported products.

q.q: Young people have no part in indigenous conflict resolution because it belongs to elders only.
q.explanation: Young people inherit the tradition from elders because they are tomorrow's elders.

q.q: Give the term for the wise use of resources available in the natural environment.
q.explanation: This is the definition of environmental conservation given in the lesson.

q.q: Name the two Ethiopian communities given as examples of indigenous environmental conservation.
q.explanation: Konso terracing and Gedeo agroforestry are the two examples.

q.q: Which of the following is a major indigenous technology in Ethiopia?
q.explanation: Wood carving, with pottery, weaving, iron smithing, jewelry and leather work, is a major indigenous technology.

q.q: State one attribute of responsible citizens shown by people who keep indigenous crafts alive despite negative attitudes.
q.answer: hard work|determination|respect for indigenous wisdom|valuing their own wisdom
q.explanation: Their dedication shows determination, hard work and respect for indigenous wisdom.

q.q: Arrange the following steps in the order in which a community dispute is peacefully settled by elders.
options: A peaceful settlement is agreed by both sides
The parties agree to bring the dispute to elders
Elders listen to both sides and apply local custom
A quarrel breaks out between two families
q.explanation: The quarrel comes first, then agreement to involve elders, then mediation, then a peaceful settlement.

q.q: An indigenous social institution is best defined as an institution established:
options: locally by voluntary cooperation of community members on the basis of mutual trust
by a private company for profit
q.explanation: This is the definition given in the lesson and glossary.

q.q: Which institution is established primarily to provide mutual aid in burial matters?
q.explanation: Idir is established primarily to provide mutual aid in burial matters and other community concerns.

q.q: Iqub pays the pooled money to members through a lottery method.
q.explanation: Members agree on a fixed contribution and the money is paid to members by lottery.

q.q: Name the institution that is a culture of labour sharing during ploughing, weeding and harvesting.
q.explanation: Debo or Jigie is the culture of helping each other in agricultural and building work.

q.q: The stick that symbolises women's rights in the Oromo society is called:
q.explanation: Siinqee is literally a stick, Ulee, symbolising a set of rights exercised by women.

q.q: Give the name of the institution that provides interest-free loans to members in addition to burial support.
q.explanation: Idir acts as a credit institution by providing members with loans without interest.

q.q: Indigenous social institutions are found only in rural areas of Ethiopia.
q.explanation: Idir, for example, is widely practised among both rural and urban peoples.

q.q: Which of the following is a service provided by Idir besides burial matters?
options: Helping members cope with the death of livestock
q.explanation: Idir helps members cope with sudden risks such as the death of livestock, fire, theft and health problems.

q.q: Explain the main purpose of Mahber or Senbete.
q.answer: to help each other in serious problems and enjoy and socialise together|mutual help and social gatherings
q.explanation: Members help each other in serious problems, enjoy together and discuss common interests.

q.q: In which Oromo system does Siinqee symbolise married women's participation in public life?
q.explanation: In the Oromo Gadaa system Siinqee represents married women's participation in political, economic, social, cultural and religious activities.

q.q: Arrange the steps of an Iqub meeting in the correct order.
options: The winner receives the pooled money
Members agree on the amount and the date
Members contribute their money on the set date
The winner is chosen by lottery
q.explanation: First the group agrees on the amount and date, then members contribute, then the winner is drawn by lottery, then the money is paid.

q.q: Which statement best defines culture?
options: Only the food and dress of a group
Shared language, beliefs, values, norms and behaviours passed between generations
q.explanation: Culture is the shared language, beliefs, values, norms, behaviours and material objects passed from generation to generation.

q.q: There is no society without culture and cultural values.
q.explanation: The textbook states that there is no society without culture and cultural values that differentiate one society from others.

q.q: Culture is described as a lens because:
options: it is used to evaluate what is proper or improper
q.explanation: We evaluate what is proper or improper, normal or abnormal using our culture.

q.q: Name one element of culture mentioned in the lesson.
q.explanation: Language, beliefs, values, norms, rituals, customs, arts and music are elements of culture.

q.q: Explain why cultural diversity is described as a source of beauty in Ethiopia.
q.answer: many cultures and practices give beauty|diversity gives beauty and attraction
q.explanation: Various peoples with varieties of cultures give beauty and attraction to our society.

q.q: Which behaviour shows respect for cultural diversity?
options: Judging other cultures by your own standards
Taking part respectfully in another community's ceremony
Refusing to learn about other cultures
q.explanation: Respect means recognising and appreciating practices that are not our own.

q.q: Learning about other cultures helps us avoid negative stereotypes and personal bias.
q.explanation: The lesson states that learning about cultures helps us recognise differences and avoid negative stereotypes and personal biases.

q.q: What do we call a fixed and oversimplified idea about a group of people?
q.explanation: An oversimplified fixed idea about a group is a stereotype.

q.q: In the case study, a visitor joins an unfamiliar coffee ceremony respectfully. What value does she show?
q.explanation: She accepts and appreciates a cultural practice that is not her own.

q.q: Arrange the steps for learning about another culture in the correct order.
q.explanation: The order is: notice, pause, ask, participate and appreciate.

q.q: Which is an example of cultural diversity in Ethiopia?
options: Coffee ceremonies differ across the country
There is a single uniform culture
q.explanation: Coffee drinking cultures and ceremonies differ across Ethiopia, showing cultural diversity.

q.q: Multiculturalism is best defined as:
options: A single culture for all citizens
A body of thought about how to respond to cultural and religious diversity
A law that bans local festivals
q.explanation: Multiculturalism is a body of thought about the proper way to respond to cultural and religious diversity.

q.q: In a multicultural society every culture is unique in itself.
q.explanation: In a multicultural society every culture is unique in itself and cultural uniformity is uncommon.

q.q: In today's Ethiopia multiculturalism has been adopted to:
options: reconcile the imbalance between upholding ethnic and national identity
q.explanation: It reconciles the imbalance between upholding ethnic and national identity by maintaining unity within diversity.

q.q: Give the strategy used to maintain and preserve a country's national unity out of diverse identities.
q.explanation: Multiculturalism is the best strategy to accommodate diversity and preserve national unity.

q.q: Multiculturalism weakens national unity.
q.explanation: Multiculturalism maintains unity within diversity; it does not weaken it.

q.q: Which two identities does multiculturalism in Ethiopia try to hold in balance?
q.answer: ethnic identity and national identity|ethnic and national identity
q.explanation: It balances ethnic identity with national identity.

q.q: Which statement about cultural uniformity is correct?
options: All multicultural societies have one culture
Cultural uniformity is uncommon in diversified societies
q.explanation: The lesson states that cultural uniformity is uncommon in diversified societies.

q.q: Explain why multiculturalism is described as the best strategy for diversity accommodation.
q.answer: maintains unity within diversity|accommodates diversity and preserves national unity
q.explanation: It accommodates diversity while maintaining and preserving national unity.

q.q: Arrange the way a state manages diversity.
q.explanation: The order is: recognise, accept, respect, balance and share values.

q.q: Which is an example of multiculturalism in Ethiopia?
options: Christians and Muslims living together peacefully for a long period
Forcing one dress style on all citizens
q.explanation: Christians and Muslims have lived together peacefully based on mutual respect and tolerance.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT a pillar of multicultural societies?
q.explanation: The four pillars are accepting, respecting, tolerating and appreciating differences, not ignoring them.

q.q: Tolerance is described as the bedrock of multiculturalism in diverse societies.
q.explanation: The lesson states that tolerance is the bedrock of multiculturalism in diverse societies like Ethiopia.

q.q: Tolerance is best defined as:
options: the willingness to accept the existence of differences we dislike or disagree with
refusing to meet people who differ
q.explanation: Tolerance is the willingness to accept the existence of differences we dislike or disagree with.

q.q: Give the pillar that means understanding how we are alike, how we are different and treating everyone with respect regardless of the differences.
q.explanation: This is the definition of accepting differences.

q.q: Which pillar goes beyond tolerance by seeking to understand and learn about another culture?
q.explanation: Appreciating differences seeks to understand and learn about another culture.

q.q: Respect should be given only to people whose culture is the same as ours.
q.explanation: We must respect and support each other despite differences in our cultural backgrounds.

q.q: Diversity encompasses which of the following?
options: Culture, gender, religion, age, disability and career status
q.explanation: Diversity encompasses culture, gender, religion, age, disability and career status.

q.q: Explain the difference between tolerance and appreciation of differences.
q.answer: tolerance accepts without approving|appreciation seeks to understand and value the difference
q.explanation: Tolerance accepts what we dislike, while appreciation positively values and seeks to understand the difference.

q.q: If differences are accepted and respected they help to create:
q.explanation: Accepted and respected differences create peaceful coexistence and harmonious relationships.

q.q: Arrange the four pillars from the most basic response to the fullest response.
q.explanation: The order is: accepting, respecting, tolerating and appreciating differences.

q.q: Which of the following is a major form of diversity demonstrating multiculturalism in Ethiopia?
q.explanation: Ethiopia shows ethnic, cultural, linguistic and religious diversity.

q.q: Ethnicity by itself is a potential threat to multiculturalism.
q.explanation: Ethnicity and identifying oneself is natural; it becomes a threat only when it develops into ethnocentrism.

q.q: The basis of ethnicity is often:
options: a tradition of common descent or intermarriage and shared culture or history
q.explanation: The basis of ethnicity is often a tradition of common descent or intermarriage and shared culture or history.

q.q: Give the term for judging other cultures as inferior by the standards of your own group.
q.explanation: This is ethnocentrism, a potential threat to multiculturalism.

q.q: Name the principle that says different religions should live in harmony with each other.
q.explanation: Religious tolerance dictates that different religions live in harmony.

q.q: Gender is best described as:
options: the socially constructed roles and relationships society ascribes to the two sexes
q.explanation: Gender is a social construct that defines roles, rights and responsibilities for women and men.

q.q: Disability is a fundamental aspect of human diversity.
q.explanation: The lesson states that disability is a fundamental aspect of human diversity in the present-day world.

q.q: Explain why embracing disability requires more than tolerance.
q.answer: it requires moving beyond tolerance to embracing and celebrating|practical accommodation and inclusion
q.explanation: Disability diversity moves beyond simple tolerance to embracing and celebrating each individual.

q.q: Linguistic diversity means:
options: the presence of a variety of languages spoken in a community
q.explanation: Linguistic diversity is the presence of a variety of languages spoken within a community.

q.q: Give one example from the lesson of religious groups living together peacefully in Ethiopia.
q.answer: Christians and Muslims|Christians and Muslims living together
q.explanation: Christians and Muslims have been living together peacefully based on mutual respect and tolerance.

q.q: Unity in diversity refers to:
options: the feeling of being one over common destinies among members of a group
the rule of one ethnic group
q.explanation: The lesson defines unity in diversity as the feeling of being one over common destinies among members of a group.

q.q: Unity in diversity means uniformity in all things.
q.explanation: Unity in diversity is not uniformity; it is harmony between dissimilar individuals or groups.

q.q: Which statement best describes unity in diversity?
options: Commonality without uniformity and diversity without fragmentation
q.explanation: The lesson states that unity in diversity involves commonality without uniformity and diversity without fragmentation.

q.q: What term means the feeling of oneness across the entire country?
q.explanation: National unity is a feeling of oneness across the entire country.

q.q: Explain why unity in diversity is not the same as uniformity.
q.answer: unity respects differences|unity allows differences while keeping harmony|uniformity removes differences
q.explanation: Unity in diversity keeps differences and builds harmony, while uniformity removes differences.

q.q: Diversity means the existence of variations of different characteristics in a group of people.
q.explanation: Diversity refers to the existence of variations of different characteristics in a group.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT part of the meaning of unity in diversity?
options: Forcing everyone to be the same
q.explanation: Forcing sameness is uniformity, which is the opposite of unity in diversity.

q.q: Explain the difference between unity in diversity and national unity.
q.answer: national unity is oneness across the whole country|unity in diversity is harmony among dissimilar groups
q.explanation: National unity is oneness across the entire country, while unity in diversity is harmony among groups that differ.

q.q: Arrange these steps for upholding unity in diversity in the correct order.
options: Live together in harmony as one nation
Acknowledge the rich diversity in society
Design the right policy for diversity accommodation
q.explanation: The order is: acknowledge diversity, recognise and respect differences, design the right policy, then live in harmony.

q.q: Ethiopia is a country in which different peoples have lived together for many centuries. This shows:
q.explanation: Living together for many centuries shows the deep tolerance and unity of the Ethiopian people.

q.q: Unity in diversity is not about uniformity, but an expression of ____ between dissimilar groups.
q.explanation: The lesson calls unity in diversity an expression of harmony between dissimilar individuals or groups.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT an element of diversity?
q.explanation: Language uniformity is the opposite of a diversity element; linguistic diversity is the correct element.

q.q: Cultural diversity refers to:
options: the occurrence of different cultures, religions, languages and ethnic backgrounds
q.explanation: Cultural diversity is the occurrence of different cultures, religions, languages and ethnic backgrounds.

q.q: In true cultural diversity, no culture is superior to another.
q.explanation: The lesson states that in true cultural diversity all cultures should be seen equally.

q.q: Religious diversity means that everyone follows the same religion.
q.explanation: Religious diversity is the fact that there are significant differences in religious beliefs and practices.

q.q: Name the diversity that refers to significant differences in religious beliefs and practices.
q.explanation: Religious diversity is the fact of significant differences in religious beliefs and practices.

q.q: Explain what linguistic diversity is.
q.answer: the existence of different languages in a country|many languages in a country
q.explanation: Linguistic diversity is the existence of different languages in a given country.

q.q: Ethiopia is known as a land of peace and religious tolerance because:
options: Christians and Muslims and their places of worship live together peacefully
q.explanation: In Ethiopia churches and mosques are often in close proximity and relationships are peaceful, and indigenous beliefs also exist.

q.q: Give one advantage of respecting the equality of peoples from different backgrounds.
q.explanation: Respecting equality helps people live in harmony and peace as citizens of one country.

q.q: Why does language matter in a diverse society?
options: It is one of the most important aspects of culture
It removes the need for respect
q.explanation: Language is one of the most important aspects of culture and can promote different cultural entities.

q.q: In cultural diversity, all cultures should be seen as ____.
q.explanation: All cultures should be seen equally, with none superior or inferior.

q.q: What would happen to tolerance and peaceful coexistence if Ethiopians did not respect cultural and religious diversity?
q.answer: tolerance would decrease|peaceful coexistence would be threatened
q.explanation: Without respect for diversity, tolerance would fall and peaceful coexistence would be at risk.

q.q: Accommodation of diversity is best described as:
options: a distinct strategy to deal with cultural diversity
q.explanation: Accommodation of diversity is the distinct strategy to deal with cultural diversity.

q.q: Diversity management is a process intended to:
options: create and maintain a positive environment where similarities and differences are valued
q.explanation: Diversity management creates and maintains a positive environment where similarities and differences are valued.

q.q: In accommodation of diversity, differences are accepted.
q.explanation: The lesson states that in accommodation of diversity differences are accepted.

q.q: Accommodation and integration mean exactly the same thing.
q.explanation: Integration aims at equal citizenship and the privatisation of differences, so it is distinct from accommodation.

q.q: According to the lesson, accommodation implies the right way to what?
q.explanation: Accommodation implies the right way to diversity management.

q.q: State when accommodation of diversity can be achieved.
q.answer: when the components of society accept differences and respect their consequences|mutual acceptance of differences
q.explanation: It is achieved when society's components demonstrate mutual acceptance of differences and respect their consequences.

q.q: Integration, as distinct from accommodation, aims at:
options: equal citizenship and the privatisation of differences
q.explanation: Integration aims at equal citizenship and at the privatisation of differences.

q.q: Explain why diversity accommodation ensures that everyone can participate fully.
q.answer: it removes barriers such as ability, religion or gender|it accepts differences and includes all
q.explanation: Diversity accommodation ensures that everyone, regardless of physical ability, religion or gender, is able to participate fully.

q.q: A workplace that values the similarities and differences of its employees is practising:
q.explanation: Diversity management creates a positive work environment where similarities and differences are valued.

q.q: Name one factor, besides religion and gender, that diversity accommodation takes into account.
q.explanation: The lesson names physical ability, religion and gender as factors that should not prevent full participation.

q.q: Give one reason why diversity management is a prominent issue in developing countries like Ethiopia.
q.answer: multicultural societies need to accommodate diversity and achieve integration|many cultures live together
q.explanation: Managing cultural diversity has become prominent in developing countries such as Ethiopia, which must accommodate diversity and realise national integration.

q.q: Ethiopia contains how many ethnic groups according to the lesson?
q.explanation: Ethiopia contains over 80 different ethnic groups, each with tribes and sub-tribes.

q.q: Each ethnic group in Ethiopia has distinct cultural practices and speaks a language specific to the group.
q.explanation: The lesson states that each ethnic group has distinct cultural practices and speaks its own language.

q.q: Building unity in diversity from a multicultural state and a federal system has been adopted as a solution for:
q.explanation: It has been adopted as a solution for incorporating both unity and diversity.

q.q: A very crucial balance between unity and diversity within society is an easy goal to achieve.
q.explanation: The lesson states that this balance is not an easy goal to achieve.

q.q: A balance between unity and diversity is used to create national integration and a common national identity among all ____.
q.explanation: It is used to create integration and common identity among all nations.

q.q: List the differences that must be recognised and respected to ensure national unity and common identity.
q.answer: language, religion, identity, cultural values and historical background
q.explanation: The lesson names language, religion, identity, cultural values and historical background.

q.q: In the case study, the community welcomed Abdella warmly. This best shows:
options: respect for cultural and religious diversity
q.explanation: The community celebrated both Christian and Muslim holidays and respected religious diversity.

q.q: Explain how a sense of common citizenship is fostered among citizens of a state.
q.answer: when feelings of unity and harmony are in people's hearts|through shared unity and harmony
q.explanation: When feelings of unity and harmony are in the hearts of the peoples, a sense of common citizenship or loyalty to the nation is fostered.

q.q: Which factors does the lesson say must be considered to balance unity and diversity in Ethiopia?
q.explanation: The lesson stresses historical, political and socio-cultural factors.

q.q: According to the lesson, promoting diverse ethnic, linguistic, cultural and religious differences is as important as national unity.
q.explanation: The lesson states this equality of importance clearly.

q.q: What does the lesson call the process aimed at creating and maintaining a positive environment where similarities and differences are valued?
q.explanation: That is the definition of diversity management.

q.q: According to the lesson, a problem is:
options: an unpleasant situation that prevents people from achieving what they want
q.explanation: The textbook defines a problem as an unpleasant situation that prevents people from achieving what they want.

q.q: Problem-solving skills are described as valuable intellectual abilities for leading a successful life.
q.explanation: The lesson states that problem-solving skills are valuable intellectual abilities and capacities for leading a successful life.

q.q: Which statement best describes decision making?
options: Selecting the right option from a number of available alternatives
q.explanation: Decision making is about selecting the right option from available alternatives.

q.q: Give the term for the act of defining a problem, determining its cause, identifying and selecting alternatives, and implementing the solution.
q.explanation: This is the broader meaning of problem solving given in the lesson.

q.q: There is only one right way to solve any given problem.
q.explanation: The lesson says there is no right way to solve a given problem and different people solve it differently.

q.q: What is the step that must come before searching for a solution?
q.explanation: Defining and understanding the problem comes before finding the solution.

q.q: In the example of the lost bag, which skills does the lesson say the solution needs?
options: Creative problem solving and critical thinking
q.explanation: The lesson states that this serious problem needs creative problem solving and critical thinking skill.

q.q: Why is problem solving called a basic life skill?
options: Because it is taught only in Grade 9
Because it is needed at home, at school and at work every day
Because it applies only to engineers
Because it replaces all other skills
q.explanation: It is essential to our day-to-day lives at home, at school and at work.

q.q: Arrange the broad problem-solving process in the correct order.
options: Determine the cause of the problem
q.explanation: The order is: define the problem, determine the cause, identify and select alternatives, implement the solution.

q.q: Explain in one sentence how problem solving and decision making are linked.
q.answer: solving a problem involves making right decisions|they are inter-linked
q.explanation: The two are inter-linked because solving a problem tactfully involves making right decisions.

q.q: Where in daily life is the ability to solve problems said to be essential?
q.answer: home, school and work|at home and at school and at work
q.explanation: The lesson names home, school and work.

q.q: Problem-solving skills are considered to be:
options: a hard skill learned only at university
a soft skill, or an individual strength
a subject in the national timetable
q.explanation: The lesson describes problem solving as a soft skill rather than a learned hard skill.

q.q: Everybody may have problem-solving skill without formal education and training.
q.explanation: Because it is a soft skill, people may have it in different degrees without formal training.

q.q: Which of the following is listed as an importance of problem-solving skills?
q.explanation: Developing emotional intelligence is one of the listed benefits.

q.q: Name the method by which people settle differences and reach compromise while avoiding argument.
q.explanation: This is the definition of negotiation skill.

q.q: Why does the lesson value indigenous problem-solving skills?
options: They are used to resolve social and individual problems in society
They are written in textbooks only
q.explanation: Indigenous skills include negotiation, cooperation and diversity tolerance used to resolve problems in society.

q.q: Indigenous skills should replace scientific skills in problem solving.
q.explanation: The lesson says integrating indigenous skills with scientific ones is very important.

q.q: Give the term for producing many facts, ideas and possible solutions before judging them.
q.explanation: This describes brainstorming, one of the listed benefits.

q.q: A good problem solver who recognises and manages feelings is showing:
q.explanation: Emotional intelligence is the ability to recognise and manage emotions.

q.q: Explain why problem solving is called a basic life skill.
q.answer: needed at home, school and work every day|essential to day-to-day life
q.explanation: It is essential to our day-to-day lives at home, at school and at work.

q.q: Besides defining the problem and creating alternatives, what must a good problem solver also do with the response?
q.explanation: Receiving a response and responding properly is an essential aspect of problem-solving skills.

q.q: Arrange these actions of a good problem solver in the correct order.
options: Evaluate and select the best option
q.explanation: The order is: identify and define, create alternatives, evaluate and select, apply.

q.q: Good problem solvers are people who use a combination of:
q.explanation: The textbook states that good problem solvers use a combination of intuition and logic.

q.q: What is Step 1 in the problem-solving process?
q.explanation: The first step is to define the problem and identify its root causes.

q.q: Good problem solvers look for opportunity within the problem and learn from it.
q.explanation: They see problems as challenges and as chances to learn something new.

q.q: What is Step 2 of the problem-solving process called?
q.explanation: Step 2 is to brainstorm and collect as many facts as possible.

q.q: Which quality means acting early to stop a difficulty from becoming a crisis?
q.explanation: Good problem solvers do prevention more than intervention.

q.q: Give the term for the quality of being willing to consider ideas and opinions that are new or different from your own.
q.explanation: This is the definition of open mindedness.

q.q: A good solution cannot fail if the implementation is careless.
q.explanation: The lesson warns that even the best solution could fail because of ineffective implementation.

q.q: Which stage of problem solving is described as the critical peak of the process?
q.explanation: Implementation is called the critical peak of the problem-solving process.

q.q: Why do intelligent problem solvers develop several alternatives?
options: Because there is almost always more than one solution
q.explanation: They recognise that there is almost always more than one solution, so they prepare alternatives.

q.q: Arrange the four stages of problem solving in the correct order.
q.explanation: The order is: define the problem, brainstorm, decide on the solution, implement the solution.

q.q: In Step 2, the best way to gather information is to:
options: ask questions to those connected to the problem
wait for the problem to disappear
q.explanation: The best way to gather information is by asking questions to those who are connected or related to the problem.

q.q: Creative problem-solving is considered to be:
options: a hard skill learned by training
a soft skill, or personal strength
q.explanation: The lesson says creative problem-solving is considered a soft skill, or personal strength.

q.q: Critical thinking is the ability to engage in reflective and independent thinking.
q.explanation: This is the definition of critical thinking given in the lesson.

q.q: The difference between critical and creative thinkers is that creativity is associated with:
q.explanation: Creativity generates ideas, while critical thinking analyses and evaluates them.

q.q: What phrase describes the thinking of a creative thinker?
q.answer: outside the box|thinking outside the box
q.explanation: Creative thinkers are people who think outside the box.

q.q: Give the term for the art of addressing differences and finding common ground so that everyone can work together peacefully.
q.explanation: This is the definition of conflict resolution.

q.q: Which is a requirement of successful conflict resolution?
options: The readiness to forgive and forget
q.explanation: Readiness to forgive and forget is one of the listed requirements.

q.q: When conflict is handled respectfully it can strengthen the bond between the parties.
q.explanation: Handled well, conflict provides an opportunity for growth that strengthens the bond.

q.q: According to the lesson, problem-solving skill is:
options: one of the most important qualities of good citizens
q.explanation: Problem-solving skill is described as one of the most important qualities of good citizens.

q.q: Name the two primary attributes of good citizens that help to improve problem-solving skills.
q.answer: conflict resolution and critical thinking|critical thinking and conflict resolution
q.explanation: The lesson names conflict resolution and critical thinking skills.

q.q: What do good critical thinkers focus on instead of rumours and opinions?
q.explanation: Good critical thinkers focus on facts and on the scientific evaluation of information.

q.q: Arrange the requirements of successful conflict resolution in the order given in the lesson.
options: Recognise and respond to important matters
Believe that resolution can support both parties
Be ready to forgive and forget
q.explanation: The order is: recognise important matters, forgive and forget, seek compromise, believe that both parties can be served.

q.q: Foreign relations are best defined as:
options: the internal laws of a state
the external relations of a country with countries of the world
the trade rules of a region
q.explanation: Foreign relations are defined as the external relations of a country with countries of the world.

q.q: Which statement reflects the idea Aristotle used to explain why states need relations?
q.explanation: Aristotle described human beings as social animals who cannot live in isolation, and the same applies to states.

q.q: No state can exist or sustain itself in isolation from other states.
q.explanation: The lesson states that no state can exist or sustain in isolation from other states.

q.q: Ethiopia's principles for external relations are stated under Article 86 of the 1995 FDRE Constitution.
q.explanation: Article 86 of the 1995 FDRE Constitution states those principles.

q.q: Give the term for the goals, claims and demands that states seek to achieve, preserve and secure in relations with other nations.
q.explanation: This is the definition of national interest.

q.q: Give the name for the agreements, strategies, methods and guidelines that states use to accomplish their actions in the international arena.
q.explanation: This is the definition of foreign policy.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT a principle of Ethiopia's external relations under Article 86?
options: Non-interference in the internal affairs of other states
Interference in the internal affairs of neighbouring states
q.explanation: Article 86 requires non-interference, not interference, in the internal affairs of other states.

q.q: About 90 per cent of Ethiopia's imports arrive via:
q.explanation: Almost 90 per cent of Ethiopia's imports arrive via the port of Djibouti.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why the absence of peace in one state can threaten another state.
q.answer: insecurity spreads across borders|the security of one state depends on another
q.explanation: The absence of peace and security in one state can be a threat to the security of another, as with the crisis in Somalia.

q.q: Arrange a state's relationships from the closest circle to the widest.
options: Continental bodies such as the African Union
q.explanation: The closest circle is neighbouring states, then regional bodies, then continental bodies, then the world community.

q.q: Which Article of the 1995 FDRE Constitution states the principles of Ethiopia's foreign relations?
q.explanation: Article 86 states the principles of the country's external relations.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT listed as a major instrument of foreign policy?
q.explanation: The major instruments are diplomacy, propaganda, economic tools and military methods.

q.q: Diplomacy is best described as:
options: the ways states manage their sovereign relations with other mutually recognised states
a violent method of imposing force
the internal budget of a state
q.explanation: Diplomacy refers to the ways states manage their sovereign relations with other mutually recognised states.

q.q: Diplomacy is an end in itself, not a means.
q.explanation: The lesson says diplomacy is not an end but a means, not a purpose but a method.

q.q: States use military force when their national interests are not fulfilled by peaceful methods.
q.explanation: Force is used as the last resort when peaceful methods fail.

q.q: Name the instrument of foreign policy that works through trade, investment and development cooperation.
q.explanation: This is the economic instrument of foreign policy.

q.q: Give the term for the art and practice of conducting negotiations between nations.
q.explanation: This is one of the definitions of diplomacy given in the lesson.

q.q: Why do states depend on one another economically?
options: Because all states are at the same level of development
Because states are at different levels of development and depend on each other
Because trade is forbidden between states
q.explanation: States are economically at various levels of development, so they depend on each other.

q.q: Military force is called the last resort because:
options: it is used only when peaceful and diplomatic methods fail
q.explanation: Force is the instrument used when national interests cannot be fulfilled by peaceful methods.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why a state without a foreign policy is compared to a ship in the deep sea without knowledge of direction.
q.answer: it has no guide to reach its goals|it cannot achieve its national interests
q.explanation: Without a foreign policy a state has no direction for converting its goals and interests into reality.

q.q: Arrange the instruments in the order states normally prefer to use them.
q.explanation: Diplomacy is preferred first, economic methods are used continuously, and force is the last resort.

q.q: Name one state given in the lesson as having highly advanced military technology.
q.explanation: The lesson names the USA, Russia and China as states with advanced military technology.

q.q: Which regional organisation does Ethiopia use to realise its regional foreign policy?
q.explanation: Ethiopia uses the Intergovernmental Authority for Development (IGAD).

q.q: Ethiopia's two major national interests served by its regional policy are:
options: peace and security, and socio-economic transformation
q.explanation: The lesson names peace and security, and socio-economic transformation.

q.q: Ethiopia is the largest country in the Horn of Africa without a port.
q.explanation: The lesson states that Ethiopia is the largest country without a port in the Horn of Africa.

q.q: The port of Djibouti was designed from the start to serve Ethiopia.
q.explanation: The port of Djibouti was designed from the start to serve Ethiopia, given its proximity.

q.q: Which country does the Omo River flow to?
q.explanation: The Omo River flows to Kenya.

q.q: Give the term for cooperation and coordination between member states to promote their mutual socio-economic development and ensure regional security.
q.explanation: This is the definition of regional cooperation.

q.q: Which of these rivers flow to Somalia?
q.explanation: Wabishebelle, Genale and Dawa flow to Somalia.

q.q: Ethiopia is described as a regional power in the Horn of Africa because of:
options: its military and diplomatic influence and its population size
q.explanation: Ethiopia is described as a regional power owing to its military and diplomatic influence and its population size.

q.q: Explain in one sentence why the port of Djibouti is called the bedrock of the Ethio-Djibouti socio-economic relationship.
q.answer: it serves Ethiopia's trade and Ethiopia is a major market for Djibouti|both states benefit from port services
q.explanation: The port serves Ethiopia's trade while Ethiopia provides a major market for Djibouti.

q.q: Name one neighbouring state to which Ethiopia exports electric power.
q.explanation: Ethiopia exports electric power to Djibouti, Sudan and Kenya.

q.q: A country that is not peaceful domestically:
options: can still enjoy peace with its neighbours
cannot enjoy peace with its neighbours
q.explanation: A country that is not peaceful domestically cannot enjoy peace with its neighbours.

q.q: The term economics is derived from the Greek word oikonomia, which means:
options: Management of a family or a household
q.explanation: Oikonomia means the management of a family or a household, showing the subject was first studied in ancient Greece.

q.q: Which best captures the textbook definition of economics?
options: The study of banks and money
A social science studying the efficient allocation of scarce resources for maximum fulfillment of human needs
The study of government revenue only
A study of population growth only
q.explanation: Economics is the social science of efficiently allocating scarce resources to satisfy unlimited human needs.

q.q: Human needs are unlimited according to the definition of economics.
q.explanation: The definition explicitly recognises that human needs are unlimited.

q.q: According to the lesson, economics offers no procedures for solving problems such as unemployment and inflation.
q.explanation: As an art, economics provides principles and methods through which such problems can be solved.

q.q: Name the kinds of productive resources named in the definition of economics.
q.explanation: The definition lists land, labour, equipment and technical knowledge as scarce productive resources.

q.q: State the two natures of economics discussed under the nature of economics.
q.answer: science and art|both science and art
q.explanation: Some economists view economics as a science while others view it as an art; it can be seen as both.

q.q: Which activity shows economics functioning as an art?
options: Predicting next year's harvest from past facts
Setting a procedure to reduce unemployment
q.explanation: As an art, economics provides procedures and methods for solving problems like unemployment.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT derived from the definition of economics?
options: Allocation of resources should be efficient
Income must be distributed equally in every household
q.explanation: Equal income distribution is not among the four derived statements; the definition concerns scarce resources, efficient allocation and unlimited needs.

q.q: Name one worldwide problem that explains the growing importance of economics.
q.explanation: Poverty, unemployment, inflation, recession and population explosion are the worldwide problems named in the lesson.

q.q: Explain why there is no single completed definition of economics.
q.answer: definition has developed over time|still under improvement|wealth, welfare and scarcity definitions
q.explanation: Views about the subject matter shifted over time, so the definition keeps improving through wealth, welfare and scarcity stages.

q.q: Arrange the parts of the economics objective in logical order from start to finish.
q.explanation: The objective flows from unlimited needs, to allocating scarce resources, to doing it efficiently, to reaching maximum possible satisfaction.

q.q: The foundation of modern economics rests on which two major branches?
q.explanation: Microeconomics and macroeconomics are the two major branches on which modern economics rests.

q.q: The fundamental problem of macroeconomics is the full employment of economic resources.
q.explanation: The lesson states that macroeconomics is associated with full employment of economic resources.

q.q: Which of the following is a macroeconomic topic?
q.explanation: GDP of Ethiopia is an economy-wide aggregate and therefore macroeconomic.

q.q: What is the main tool of analysis of macroeconomics?
q.explanation: Macroeconomics uses aggregate demand and aggregate supply of the economy as a whole.

q.q: Studying the trend of the general price level of commodities over time in a country is:
q.explanation: The trend of the general price level is macro-analysis handled by macroeconomics.

q.q: Macroeconomics can be studied independently of microeconomics.
q.explanation: The branches are complementary and macroeconomics cannot be studied independently of microeconomics.

q.q: State the fundamental problem of microeconomics.
q.answer: resource allocation|price determination|the problem of price determination
q.explanation: The fundamental problem of microeconomics is resource allocation, or the problem of price determination.

q.q: Which central problems does microeconomics help to solve?
options: What, how and for whom to produce
q.explanation: Microeconomics helps solve the central problems of what, how and for whom to produce.

q.q: Name two emerging branches of economics mentioned in the lesson.
q.answer: development economics|environmental economics|industrial economics|international economics|labor economics|mathematical economics|monetary economics|welfare economics|resource economics|behavioural economics|experimental economics|health economics
q.explanation: Emerging branches include development, environmental, industrial, international, labour, mathematical, monetary, welfare, resource, behavioural, experimental and health economics.

q.q: Explain why microeconomics and macroeconomics are described as complementary.
q.answer: one supports the other|aggregates built from individual units|macro depends on micro
q.explanation: Macroeconomic aggregates arise from the behaviour of individual units, so the two branches support each other and neither replaces the other.

q.q: Arrange these points of difference from Table 1.1 from the units studied upward to the problems solved.
q.explanation: One first identifies the units, then the variables, tools and central problem of each branch.

q.q: A theory, in economics, is described as:
options: A complete report of every fact
q.explanation: The lesson defines a theory as a simplified picture of reality.

q.q: The deductive method proceeds from general to particular.
q.explanation: Deduction reasons from general principles to the analysis of specific facts.

q.q: Which statement is positive?
options: There should be government intervention in the economy
The current inflation rate in Ethiopia is 12 percent
The government should introduce school feeding programmes
q.explanation: A measurable fact about the inflation rate is a positive statement; the others are value judgments.

q.q: Which method develops theories on the basis of observations and experiments?
q.explanation: The inductive method builds theories from observations and collected data.

q.q: In the inductive example of the textbook, falling grain prices during the harvest period lead to the generalisation that:
options: keeping other factors constant, an increase in supply leads to a fall in prices
q.explanation: Observation of harvest-time price falls, linked to increased supply, generalises to the supply-and-price relationship.

q.q: Deductive and inductive methods are competing methods and one must replace the other.
q.explanation: The two methods are complementary; one supports the other.

q.q: Explain why normative disagreements cannot be settled by facts alone.
q.answer: value judgments are opinions|cannot be proved or disproved with facts|settled by voting
q.explanation: Normative analysis is a matter of opinion loaded with value judgments, so facts cannot prove or disprove it and voting resolves disagreements.

q.q: Name the two approaches of studying economics.
q.answer: positive economics and normative economics|positive and normative
q.explanation: Economics is analysed from the positive and the normative perspectives.

q.q: Which sequence correctly shows the classic deductive argument in the lesson?
options: Abebe is a man; therefore man is mortal
Man is mortal; Abebe is a man; therefore Abebe is mortal
Abebe is mortal; therefore all men are mortal
Man is mortal; therefore Abebe is a man
q.explanation: Deduction starts from the general principle, adds the specific fact, and reaches the particular conclusion.

q.q: State the objective that economics shares with any science.
q.answer: the establishment of valid generalisations about human behaviour|valid generalisations
q.explanation: The fundamental objective of economics, like any science, is establishing valid generalisations about certain aspects of human behaviour.

q.q: Arrange the inductive procedure from first step to final generalisation.
options: Form a hypothesis from the data
Collect comprehensive data on economic conditions
Observe phenomena such as falling harvest prices
q.explanation: Induction begins with observation and data collection, forms a hypothesis, and ends in a generalisation.

q.q: The basic decision-making units of an economy are:
options: households, business firms and the government
q.explanation: The three basic decision-making units, or economic agents, are households, business firms and the government.

q.q: Households are the chief owners of the factors of production.
q.explanation: The textbook states that households are the chief owners of land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.

q.q: The payment that corresponds to the service of capital is:
q.explanation: Households receive rent, wages, interest and profit for the services of land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship respectively.

q.q: What term does the textbook use for the services of the factors of production that households sell?
q.explanation: Households sell the services of their factors, termed factor service, to producers.

q.q: Business firms sell their commodities to:
options: households, other firms, the government or other countries
q.explanation: Firms sell commodities to households, to other firms, to the government or to other countries.

q.q: The general government includes government enterprises in its definition.
q.explanation: Government is taken in the sense of general government precisely to disregard government enterprises.

q.q: Explain the primary goal of a national tax system.
q.answer: to generate revenue for government expenditures|raise revenue for government expenditure
q.explanation: Taxes are levied primarily to raise revenue for government expenditures, which grow with the national product.

q.q: Name two examples of free services the government provides.
q.explanation: The government provides free services such as police, education, medical facilities, sanitation facilities and judicial services.

q.q: Which set names the factors of production correctly?
q.explanation: The factors of production encompass land, labour, capital and entrepreneurship.

q.q: Explain how a household's income moves through the economy.
q.answer: spent on goods from firms|saved|paid as taxes to government
q.explanation: Households spend an enormous portion of income on goods and services from producers, save part of it, and pay taxes to the government.

q.q: Arrange the circular flow steps starting from a household's factor service.
options: Firm sells commodities back to households
Household sells factor service to a firm
Household spends factor income on goods
Firm pays wages to the household
q.explanation: The flow runs: household sells factor services, the firm pays factor income, the household spends it, and the firm sells commodities to the household.

q.q: The fundamental economic problem that any human society faces is:
q.explanation: The textbook states that the fundamental economic problem any human society faces is scarcity.

q.q: If resources were fully abundant, there would be no economic problems at all.
q.explanation: Scarcity of resources generates economic problems, so full abundance would remove them.

q.q: A good is said to be scarce when:
options: the amount available is less than the amount people wish to have at zero price
q.explanation: Scarcity compares the available amount with the amount people wish to have even at zero price.

q.q: Give the term for the value of the next best alternative that must be sacrificed to obtain one more unit of a product.
q.explanation: That is the definition of opportunity cost.

q.q: Opportunity cost is measured in terms of:
q.explanation: Opportunity cost is measured in goods and services, not in terms of money.

q.q: A shortage is a specific and short-term problem, while scarcity is a universal and endless problem.
q.explanation: The textbook notes exactly this difference between shortage and scarcity.

q.q: Any point outside the production possibilities frontier is:
q.explanation: Points outside the PPF cannot be produced with the given resources and technology.

q.q: What shape does the PPF take because of the law of increasing opportunity cost?
q.explanation: Rising opportunity cost per extra unit makes the PPF concave to the origin.

q.q: Moving along a PPF from alternative B (420 food, 500 computers) to C (320 food, 1000 computers), state the opportunity cost of one additional computer.
q.answer: 0.2 metric tons of food|0.2 metric ton of food|0.2 units of food
q.explanation: 100 metric tons of food sacrificed divided by 500 computers gained gives 0.2 metric tons of food per computer.

q.q: Put the chain of economic logic in the correct order.
q.explanation: The order is: scarcity, limited output, choice, opportunity cost.

q.q: Asymmetric growth occurs when an economy grows because productivity increases in only one sector of the economy.
q.explanation: Asymmetric growth is growth in productivity in one sector, which shifts the PPF along only one axis, as with improved technology applied to either food or computers.

q.q: The basic economic problems are also known as:
options: the central problems of an economy
q.explanation: The basic economic problems are also called the central problems of an economy.

q.q: Which of the following best captures the three basic economic questions of every society?
options: How much, how often and for whom
q.explanation: Every society must answer: what to produce, how to produce and for whom to produce.

q.q: The problem of how to produce is also called the problem of the choice of technique.
q.explanation: How to produce is referred to as the problem of choice of technique.

q.q: A technique that uses more labour relative to capital per unit of output is called:
q.explanation: A labour-intensive technique uses more labour relative to capital per unit of output.

q.q: Give the name of the problem concerned with how the national product is distributed among members of society.
q.answer: problem of distribution|for whom to produce|distribution problem
q.explanation: For whom to produce is called the problem of the distribution of the national product.

q.q: Capital goods and consumption goods are alternatives in the what-to-produce problem.
q.explanation: The economy must choose between consumption and capital goods, among other allocations.

q.q: What two factors does the choice between labour-intensive and capital-intensive techniques depend on?
q.answer: available supplies of factors and their relative prices|factor supplies and relative prices
q.explanation: The choice depends on the available supplies of diverse production factors and their relative prices.

q.q: Explain the production order of an economy that wants to benefit the maximum number of people.
q.answer: necessities first then luxuries|necessary goods for the whole population first, luxury goods after
q.explanation: Such an economy first produces necessary goods for the whole population, then luxury goods.

q.q: Wheat produced with primitive tools and manual labour, or with modern machinery and few workers, is an example of the decision:
q.explanation: Choosing between alternative techniques of production is the how-to-produce question.

q.q: Because of scarcity, individuals, firms and governments are all forced to choose what to produce and what not to produce.
q.explanation: Scarcity forces individuals, firms and governments to choose outputs, quantities and allocations.

q.q: An economic system is best defined as:
options: a set of organizational and institutional arrangements answering the basic economic questions
q.explanation: An economic system is the set of arrangements established to answer the basic economic questions.

q.q: Economic systems are classified on the basis of:
q.explanation: The types of economic systems are classified according to who owns the economic resources.

q.q: Societies with traditional economies depend on agriculture, fishing, hunting, gathering, or some combination of them.
q.explanation: The textbook states this directly about traditional economies.

q.q: The central feature of a capitalist economy is:
q.explanation: The right to private property is the central feature of capitalism.

q.q: Give the principle which states that producers make goods in accordance with the demands and tastes of consumers.
q.explanation: Freedom of choice by consumers is called the principle of consumer sovereignty.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a capitalist economy?
q.explanation: Collective ownership is a feature of the command economy, not capitalism.

q.q: A command economy allows economic freedom for consumers and producers.
q.explanation: In a command economy the government has complete control over all economic activities, so freedom is restricted.

q.q: In which year, and in which country, did socialism start according to the textbook?
q.explanation: Socialism started in Russia with the Great October Revolution in 1917.

q.q: Explain why income distribution is more equal in a command economy than in a capitalist economy.
q.answer: no private property|no profit motive|no accumulation of wealth
q.explanation: Without private property, the profit motive and wealth accumulation, incomes become relatively more equal.

q.q: In a mixed economy, industries of national and strategic importance such as defence and power generation are typically placed in:
q.explanation: Defence, power generation and basic industry are set up in the public sector of a mixed economy.

q.q: Arrange the traditional economy's development path in the correct order.
options: Groups create some form of money
Nomadic hunting and gathering with no trade
Farming and settling down create a surplus
q.explanation: The order is: nomadic hunting and gathering, then barter between non-competing groups, then farming with surplus, then the creation of money.

q.q: Economics is best described as the study of:
options: how people, businesses, governments and societies make choices to cope with scarcity
q.explanation: The unit review defines economics as the study of how societies make choices to cope with scarcity.

q.q: Although a resource exists in unlimited supply, it can be considered as scarce.
q.explanation: A resource in unlimited supply is abundant, not scarce; scarcity requires limited supply relative to wants.

q.q: Which statement best describes the economic problem?
options: The fact that economies often go into decline
The presence of high levels of unemployment
Matching endless wants with limited resources
q.explanation: The economic problem is matching unlimited wants with limited resources, that is scarcity.

q.q: Using the revision table (A: X=0, Y=100; B: X=2, Y=90; C: X=4, Y=60; D: X=6, Y=20), state the trend in the opportunity cost of good X and the law it demonstrates.
q.answer: it increases|rising opportunity cost|law of increasing opportunity cost
q.explanation: The cost per unit of X rises from 5 to 15 to 20 units of Y, demonstrating the law of increasing opportunity cost.

q.q: The production possibility frontier can be considered a measure of:
q.explanation: The PPF shows the potential, the maximum output attainable with given resources and technology.

q.q: A production possibility curve is:
q.explanation: Producing more of one good means sacrificing some of the other, so the PPC slopes downward.

q.q: Economic growth can be achieved only through technological advancement.
q.explanation: Growth occurs when resources increase in quantity or quality, or when technology advances; either condition suffices.

q.q: Which of the following is a feature of a command economy?
q.explanation: Central economic planning by the state is the defining feature of the command economy.

q.q: Explain how resources are allocated in a mixed economy.
q.answer: through the price mechanism and the government|both the market and the government allocate
q.explanation: In a mixed economy some resources are allocated through the price mechanism and some through the government.

q.q: Most traditional economies produce only what they need, rarely leaving a surplus to trade.
q.explanation: Traditional economies produce mainly what they need, so surpluses are rare and trade is limited to barter.

q.q: Arrange the central problems in the order the textbook presents them.
options: For whom are goods to be produced
What goods and services are to be produced
How to produce goods and services
q.explanation: The order is: what to produce, how to produce, for whom to produce.

q.q: A resource is classified as free when:
options: the amount available is greater than what people desire at zero price
it has a very low price
it is made by human beings
q.explanation: Free resources are available in greater amount than people desire at zero price, so they carry no price.

q.q: What is the reward for the services of capital?
q.explanation: Capital earns interest; land earns rent and labour earns wage.

q.q: Price is the test of whether a resource is an economic or a free good.
q.explanation: Because economic resources are scarce, they have non-zero prices; free resources have none.

q.q: Which factor payment does the entrepreneur receive?
q.explanation: Entrepreneurship earns profit as its reward.

q.q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a free resource?
options: Clean water in a crowded town
q.explanation: Clean water is scarce relative to wants in a crowded town, so it becomes an economic resource with a price.

q.q: Give the factor payment that corresponds to land.
q.explanation: The reward for the services of land is rent.

q.q: Machines, intermediate goods and infrastructure belong to which resource category?
q.explanation: These manufactured inputs are capital resources.

q.q: Explain why fertile farmland near a big town carries a high price.
q.answer: it is scarce relative to wants|economic resources are scarce so they have prices
q.explanation: When the amount available is less than what people want at zero price, the resource becomes economic and gains a price.

q.q: Arrange these steps of classification in the order you would use: first state the definition, second apply the price test, third assign the payment.
q.explanation: Correct order: state the definition, apply the price test, then assign the factor payment.

q.q: Name any two examples of free resources given in the lesson.
q.explanation: Air, sunshine, solar energy and a mountain stream are free resources.

q.q: Which statement best describes labour in economics?
options: Physical and mental efforts in production and distribution
q.explanation: Labour covers both the physical and the mental efforts of human beings in production and distribution.

q.q: Renewable resources are resources that:
options: have the potential to be replaced over time through natural processes
are found only in the ground
q.explanation: Renewable resources are replaced over time through natural processes.

q.q: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
q.explanation: Natural gas is a fixed stock found in the ground and is non-renewable.

q.q: The formation of soil is a renewable process, though it may take hundreds of years.
q.explanation: Renewal may be very slow, as in soil formation, but it is still renewal.

q.q: How can the supply of non-renewable resources be partly replenished?
options: It can never be replenished at all
q.explanation: Recycling may replenish supply, but the overall supply of non-renewable resources remains relatively constant.

q.q: Give the three conservation actions named in the lesson.
q.answer: reduce reuse and recycle|reduce, reuse, recycle
q.explanation: To conserve natural resources, you can reduce, reuse, and recycle them.

q.q: Recycling means reusing a natural resource or product to make something new.
q.explanation: That is the textbook definition of recycling, including collecting and sending things for reuse.

q.q: Why does turning off unused lights conserve fossil fuels?
options: Electricity generation uses fossil fuels, so less demand burns less fuel
It does not affect fuel use at all
q.explanation: Generating electricity uses fossil fuels, so reducing electricity use reduces fuel use.

q.q: Explain why overuse can be as harmful to renewable resources as consumption is to non-renewable ones.
q.answer: renewable resources can be depleted if overused|they can be killed or run out
q.explanation: Even renewable resources can be depleted if they are all killed or overused.

q.q: Put these conservation actions from first habit to last resort: get rid of nothing, remake old into new, cut the amount you use.
q.explanation: Order: first reduce, then reuse, and recycle as the final action.

q.q: Name two examples of pollution given in the lesson.
q.answer: oil spilled into water|toxic chemicals in the air|garbage dumped on the roadside
q.explanation: Oil spilled into water, toxic chemicals in the air, and garbage dumped roadside are the pollution examples.

q.q: Which set contains ONLY easily recycled items?
q.explanation: Glass, paper, cardboard, aluminum and steel are easily recycled; mixtures of materials are hard to separate.

q.q: A market is best defined as:
options: an institution where two parties meet to facilitate the exchange of goods and services
a place where prices are fixed by law
q.explanation: A market is an institution where two parties, usually buyers and sellers, meet to exchange.

q.q: Markets may be digital, with no direct physical contact between buyers and sellers.
q.explanation: The market may be physical, like a retail outlet, or digital, like an online market.

q.q: In the goods and services market, money flows continuously:
options: from the consumer to the business firms
q.explanation: Consumers pay money to businesses to acquire goods and services.

q.q: The financial market is described as the basis of capitalist societies because it:
options: provides capital formation and liquidity for businesses
q.explanation: The financial market provides capital formation and liquidity for businesses.

q.q: Give one example of something traded in the financial market.
q.explanation: Securities, currencies, bonds and other financial assets are traded there.

q.q: The labour market should be viewed at both the macroeconomic and microeconomic levels.
q.explanation: The textbook says the labour market should be viewed at both levels.

q.q: Which of the following happens in the goods and services market?
options: Households purchase consumable goods sold by businesses
q.explanation: Households purchase consumable goods and services in this market.

q.q: Explain the difference between the goods and services market and the labour market.
q.answer: goods are bought and services sold in one while labour services are supplied in the other|one trades end products the other trades labour services
q.explanation: In the goods and services market end products are traded; in the labour market labour services and jobs are exchanged.

q.q: Rank these events from the household side as they happen in one day: receive wage, buy groceries online, deposit the remainder in a bank.
options: Buy groceries in the goods and services market
Deposit savings in the financial market
Supply labour and receive the wage
q.explanation: First supply labour and earn wage, then buy groceries, then deposit savings; each event belongs to one of the three markets.

q.q: Name the two forms a market can take.
q.explanation: Markets may be physical, like retail outlets, or digital, like online markets.

q.q: Shopping on the internet places you in which market?
q.explanation: The goods and services market includes the Internet as a place of exchange.

q.q: The circular flow of economic activities is best described as:
options: a simplified macroeconomic model of basic economic relationships in a market economy
q.explanation: It is a simplified macroeconomic model showing how economic agents interact in markets.

q.q: Real flows and money flows are two sides of the same coin.
q.explanation: Each real flow is matched by an equal but opposite money flow.

q.q: Which sector is added when moving from the two-sector to the three-sector model?
q.explanation: The three-sector model adds the government sector to households and firms.

q.q: What currency does the textbook use as its example in the circular flow definition?
q.explanation: The circular flow shows how a currency, such as the Birr, flows through markets.

q.q: In the two-sector model, the outer circle of the diagram shows:
q.explanation: The outer circle shows the money flow, while the inner circle shows the real flow.

q.q: State three assumptions of the two-sector circular flow model.
q.answer: no saving|no government|closed economy no exports or imports|two sectors only
q.explanation: Assumptions include two sectors only, no saving, no government, and a closed economy without exports or imports.

q.q: In the three-sector model, savings flow directly from households to firms without any intermediary.
q.explanation: Savings are deposited in the capital market, which in turn gives savings to firms for investment.

q.q: Government revenue comes from:
q.explanation: Government gets its revenue by imposing taxes on households and on firms.

q.q: Explain how the three important economic activities of an economy generate the circular flow.
q.answer: transactions among sectors make income and expenditure move in a circular way|production exchange and consumption create transactions
q.explanation: Because of the transactions arising from production, exchange and consumption, income and expenditure move in a circular way.

q.q: Put the three-sector government actions in the textbook sequence: impose taxes; subsidize firms; pay transfer payments to households.
q.explanation: The government first collects tax revenue, then returns it through purchases, subsidies to firms and transfer payments to households.

q.q: Which pair correctly shows a real flow matched by a money flow?
options: Goods to buyers matched by payment to firms
Goods to buyers matched by goods to firms
Wages paid matched by wages received without a real flow
q.explanation: The real flow of goods from producers to buyers is matched by an equal but opposite money payment.

q.q: Ethiopia's total area and the share suitable for agriculture are:
q.explanation: Ethiopia has a total area of 1,106,000 square kilometers, of which 35 percent is suitable for agriculture (CSA, 2007).

q.q: Which soil type needs proper drainage and conditioning to reach its excellent agricultural potential?
options: Brownish-to-grey and black soils with high clay content
q.explanation: With proper drainage and conditioning, high-clay black and brownish-grey soils show excellent potentials.

q.q: Under the slogan 'Land to the Tiller' in 1975, who ended up owning the land?
q.explanation: Paradoxically the slogan was overturned and the system ended in state ownership rather than giving land to the people.

q.q: The lifetime holding right of rural peasants and pastoralists grants all rights EXCEPT:
q.explanation: The holding right gives all rights except sale and mortgage.

q.q: How long is the lease-based agreement under which urban residents obtain residence land?
q.explanation: Urban residents get land for residence on a 99-years-lease basis agreement.

q.q: Redistribution of rural land is easy under the current land system.
q.explanation: Since redistribution of land is highly restricted, access to rural land is almost non-existent.

q.q: How has altitude benefited Ethiopian agriculture, according to the textbook?
options: It formed different agro-ecological zones that multiplied the land's resource potential
It made all highlands equally warm
q.explanation: Altitude created different agro-ecological zones, multiplying land potential and enabling diverse crops and exportables.

q.q: Explain why the amount of compensation during expropriation is considered a problem in the textbook's view.
q.answer: proclamations denied market value compensation|compensation is insufficient or unfair
q.explanation: Successive implementation of proclamations violated constitutional protection by denying market value, making compensation insufficient.

q.q: What year does the source (CSA, 2007) attach to the land suitability data?
q.explanation: The data on the 1,106,000 sq km area and 35 percent share come from CSA, 2007.

q.q: In the context of agriculture, land refers to:
options: areal extent as well as productivity of food crops and other crops
q.explanation: The textbook defines agricultural land as areal extent plus the productivity of crops.

q.q: Arrange the land-ownership history from earliest to latest: feudal holdings, 1975 removal, 1991 state continuity.
options: The feudal system with inequitable land holdings
The feudal system removed under the socialist slogan
q.explanation: First feudal inequitable holdings, then their removal in 1975, then state ownership continuing from 1991 to the present.

q.q: Demand reflects the quantity of a commodity that consumers:
options: want to buy at any price
need to buy at alternative prices
are willing and able to buy at alternative prices
q.explanation: Demand requires both willingness and ability to buy at the given prices.

q.q: A demand schedule is a tabular representation of the relationship between price and quantity demanded.
q.explanation: This is the textbook definition of a demand schedule.

q.q: A price change will have no effect on the quantity of coffee demanded.
q.explanation: By the law of demand, a change in the price of coffee does change its quantity demanded.

q.q: More of a commodity will be purchased at lower prices because:
options: consumers substitute it for others whose price has not changed
at lower prices consumers can buy more with a given money income
more consumers will buy it at lower prices than at higher prices
q.explanation: All three reasons together explain why quantity demanded rises when price falls.

q.q: Which one of the following is not held constant when a demand schedule is defined?
options: Price of the good in question
q.explanation: The schedule varies the price of the good itself; other factors are held constant under ceteris paribus.

q.q: What does the Latin phrase ceteris paribus mean?
q.answer: other things remain the same|other things remaining the same|other things being equal|other things constant
q.explanation: Ceteris paribus means other things remain the same.

q.q: A household demands 5 kg of oranges at Birr 5 per kg and 13 kg at Birr 1 per kg. This illustrates:
q.explanation: A lower price is matched by a larger quantity demanded, the inverse relation of the law of demand.

q.q: Under what three conditions does a desire become an effective demand?
q.answer: willingness and ability to pay and availability of the good|willingness to pay, ability to pay, availability
q.explanation: A desire becomes effective demand when backed by ability to pay, willingness to pay and the availability of the good.

q.q: The demand function Qd = f(P) means quantity demanded depends on the price of the commodity.
q.explanation: The demand function expresses quantity demanded as a function of price, other things constant.

q.q: The market demand curve is the horizontal summation of individual demand curves at the market price.
q.explanation: Market demand is derived by adding the quantities demanded by all buyers at each price.

q.q: Using the textbook schedule for oranges, how many kilograms per week are demanded at Birr 1 per kg?
q.explanation: The schedule shows 13 kg demanded when the price is Birr 1 per kg.

q.q: Stock is the total volume of a commodity produced during a period less the quantity already sold out.
q.explanation: This is the textbook definition of stock.

q.q: Which statement about stock and supply is correct?
options: Stock is potential supply and supply may be less than or equal to stock
Supply is always greater than stock
Stock is what is actually brought to the market
q.explanation: Producers often hold part of their stock back, so supply can be less than stock.

q.q: The law of supply states that, ceteris paribus:
options: price and quantity supplied are inversely related
price and quantity supplied are directly related
quantity supplied does not depend on price
q.explanation: The law of supply says the higher the price, the higher the quantity supplied.

q.q: A fall in the price of a commodity raises the quantity that producers will offer for sale.
q.explanation: The relationship is positive: quantity supplied falls when price falls.

q.q: Using the textbook schedule for oranges, how many kilograms per week does the seller offer at Birr 20 per kg?
q.explanation: The schedule shows 80 kg offered per week at Birr 20 per kg.

q.q: Why do producers keep part of their stock off the market?
options: Because stock must never be sold
