q.explanation: The war did not abolish slavery and did not consider the Red Indians as citizens.

q.q: Name the Commander-in-Chief of the Army of the United Colonies appointed in 1775.
q.explanation: The Congress appointed Colonel George Washington as Commander-in-Chief on May 10, 1775.

q.q: Give the name of the first congress of the thirteen colonists, held at Philadelphia.
q.explanation: The thirteen colonists gathered at Philadelphia in the First Continental Congress.

q.q: In which city did representatives of the thirteen colonies meet to declare independence?
q.explanation: In 1776 representatives from the thirteen colonies met in Philadelphia to declare independence.

q.q: Explain how the American War of Independence influenced the French Revolution.
q.answer: it was one of the immediate causes|it inspired the French against feudal oppression
q.explanation: It was one of the immediate causes for the French Revolution outbreak in 1789, alongside the Enlightenment.

q.q: The Constitution made itself the supreme law of the land so that leaders would not stand above the law.
q.explanation: The founding fathers included a provision making the Constitution the supreme law of the land.

q.q: The Congress of Vienna began in:
q.explanation: The Congress of Vienna began in September 1814, five months after Napoleon's first abdication.

q.q: The Final Act of the Congress of Vienna was signed on:
q.explanation: The Final Act was signed on June 9, 1815.

q.q: Which four powers were chiefly instrumental in the overthrow of Napoleon?
options: Austria, Prussia, Russia and Great Britain
q.explanation: Austria, Prussia, Russia and Great Britain concluded the Treaty of Chaumont and led the settlement.

q.q: The objective of the Congress of Vienna was to:
options: provide a long-term peace plan for Europe by settling critical issues from the wars
q.explanation: Its objective was to provide a long-term peace plan for Europe by settling critical issues arising from the wars.

q.q: The Treaty of Chaumont, an alliance of the four powers, was concluded on:
q.explanation: The four powers concluded the Treaty of Chaumont on March 9, 1814.

q.q: The Congress of Vienna respected the idea of nationality when it redrew the map of Europe.
q.explanation: The idea of nationality was almost entirely ignored, and territories were bartered without much reference to the wishes of their inhabitants.

q.q: Name the Austrian principal minister who represented Emperor Francis II at Vienna.
q.explanation: Klemen (Metternich), principal minister of Austria, represented his emperor, Francis II.

q.q: Give the principle the statesmen successfully worked out to keep the great powers in check.
q.explanation: The statesmen successfully worked out the principle of a balance of power.

q.q: Which country refused to sign the Final Act as a protest against the Italian settlement?
q.explanation: Spain refused to sign the Final Act as a protest against the Italian settlement.

q.q: The political boundaries laid down by the Congress of Vienna lasted, except for one or two changes, for more than 40 years.
q.explanation: The boundaries lasted, except for one or two changes, for more than 40 years.

q.q: Explain why the statesmen of Vienna were criticised by later historians and partly defended.
q.answer: they ignored nationality|they secured a period of peace for Europe
q.explanation: They were criticised for ignoring nationality and bartering territories, but later historians realised how difficult their task was and that they secured for Europe a period of peace.

q.q: Which is a well-defined set?
options: The beautiful paintings in the National Museum
The even natural numbers less than 10
The fast runners in Addis Ababa
q.explanation: 'Even natural numbers less than 10' has objective membership: {2,4,6,8}. The others depend on opinion.

q.q: If A = {1, 2, 3}, how many subsets does A have?
q.explanation: 2ⁿ = 2³ = 8 subsets, including ∅ and A itself.

q.q: Which statement is correct for B = {2, 4, 6}?
q.explanation: {2} is a set whose only element lies in B, so {2} ⊆ B. Use ∈ for elements, ⊆ for sets.

q.q: U = {1,…,10}, A = {x : x is prime}. What is A′?
q.explanation: A = {2,3,5,7}, so the complement in U is {1,4,6,8,9,10}. Remember 1 is not prime.

q.q: The proper subsets of {a, b} are:
q.explanation: Proper = all 4 subsets except {a,b} itself: ∅, {a}, {b}.

q.q: A ∩ B = ∅ means the sets are:
q.explanation: No shared elements — disjoint. Venn circles do not overlap.

q.q: Which equals {x : x² = 4, x ∈ ℤ} in roster form?
q.explanation: Both 2 and −2 square to 4, and both are integers.

q.q: If n(A) = 5, the number of PROPER subsets is:
q.explanation: 2⁵ − 1 = 31: all subsets except A itself.

q.q: If A = {1,2,3} and B = {3,4,5}, then A ∩ B =
q.explanation: Only 3 is common to both sets.
